540173|2026-06.headline: PNB Housing Q1 FY27 PAT rose 4% YoY to INR 557 crore, with ROA 2.37% and ROE 11.44%, while NIM fell 19 bps QoQ to 3.50%.
540173|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 PAT grew 4% YoY to INR 557 crore, with ROA of 2.37% and ROE of 11.44%. Disbursements moved to a cheque-realisation basis this quarter, so reported disbursement grew 18% YoY to INR 5,882 crore against 56% on the old cheque-handover basis. Loan book grew 15% YoY to INR 89,670 crore, NIM moderated to 3.50% and gross NPA was 0.95%. Management says margin and yield have bottomed and expects Q2 to be much better than Q1, especially in Affordable.

financial_highlights.change: -19 bps QoQ (12 bps leverage, 7 bps Q4 true-up)

financial_highlights.metric: Spread / portfolio yield / cost of borrowing
financial_highlights.change: Spread stable QoQ; yield +1 bp; cost of borrowing +1 bp

financial_highlights.value: Negative 12 bps (recoveries INR 67 crore from written-off pool)

segments.name: Prime
segments.commentary: Disbursement INR 3,083 crore in Q1 FY27, double-digit YoY growth; Prime yield up about 8 bps QoQ, which management attributes mostly to mix shift toward self-employed and non-home loans.

segments.name: Emerging Markets
segments.commentary: Disbursement INR 2,029 crore in Q1 FY27, double-digit YoY growth; INR 71 crore disbursed under the new Emerging Developer Finance programme.

segments.name: Affordable / Emerging (retail)
segments.commentary: Affordable and Emerging book grew 27% YoY and is 41% of retail portfolio (target 45% by FY27-end). Affordable net disbursement only INR 555 crore, below target; management cites about 11% YoY growth on a like-for-like basis.

segments.name: Corporate loan book
segments.commentary: INR 493 crore outstanding at 30 June 2026, with about INR 215 crore disbursed in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Written-off pool (retail)
segments.commentary: About INR 340 crore remaining; INR 67 crore recovered in Q1. One legacy account of about INR 420 crore was classified as fraud, already fully provided in FY23, so no incremental P&L impact.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 overall loan book growth guidance of 18% to 20% maintained; management says it expects to beat it.
Affordable loan book growth guidance of 50% to 60% maintained for FY27.
Construction finance capped at about 3% of the overall book in FY27.
Affordable and Emerging share to reach 45% of book by FY27-end and about 50% in FY28.
FY27 ROA guided around 2.4%; FY28 ROA around 2.3% as credit cost normalises. Long-term ROA 2.3% to 2.35%.
NIM expected to have bottomed; gradual improvement from H2 FY27. Yield expected to keep improving on mix.
Credit cost expected to stay negative through FY27 on continued recoveries.
Q2 FY27 disbursement (net) expected 60% to 70% above Q1 overall and 2.5x to 2.6x in Affordable; management says July was promising.
Rating upgrades (CARE done; ICRA and CRISIL pending) expected to cut cost of borrowing by at least about 10 bps.
capex_capacity: Branch network expanded by 12 in the quarter to 404 branches.
Affordable business launched from selected Prime and Emerging branches; about INR 30 crore disbursed in June, and 15% to 18% of Affordable business in July.
Management does not plan to open more branches; plans to use existing branches to contain opex.
Micro-housing policy formulated and rolled out in Q2 FY27; meaningful contribution expected from H2 FY27.
Full buyout transactions started; loan assets of INR 146 crore acquired in Q1 FY27.
demand_pricing: Management cites steady housing demand across retail mortgage segments, particularly Affordable and Emerging Markets; RBI repo unchanged at 5.25%.
Gross disbursement YoY growth of 56% on cheque-handover basis vs 18% on the new net basis; the gap reflects the accounting change, not lost demand.
Incremental disbursement yield is above the 9.48% book yield, per management.
Incremental cost of borrowing rose about 18 bps in Q1 on tighter liquidity and market volatility; management says it has eased somewhat but remains elevated.
BT-in share of sourcing fell to 4.4% from 5% a year ago; Affordable BT-in fell to 3.4% from 10.5%.
Prime yield mix benefit about 10 to 15 bps; Affordable yield up about 50 bps QoQ per management.

qa_highlights.question: How should yield and cost of funds trend, and does the medium-term NIM expansion thesis from mix shift toward Affordable/Emerging/CF still hold over two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin, yield and cost of funds have all bottomed; gradual margin improvement expected from H2 FY27. Construction finance capped at 3% of book in FY27; Affordable and Emerging share at 41% now, targeting 45% by FY27-end and nearly 50% in two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the gross disbursement momentum (55%+ on cheque-handover basis) carry into Q2 and make the 18-20% loan growth guidance conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to beat both gross and net Q2 numbers, said Q2 gross will be much better than Q1 and July showed strong gross and net momentum. It said it expects to do much better than the 18-20% loan growth guidance but did not raise it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did leverage and NII move sharply when debt-to-equity barely changed?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said average leverage rose from 3.6x to 3.75x; Q4 disbursement realisations flowed into Q1 borrowings, and lower investment yields also weighed on total yield.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gap between reported and gross disbursement across all segments, and what is Affordable growth on a like-for-like basis?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap spans Prime, Emerging and Affordable since retail and wholesale moved to debit-from-account recognition. Like-for-like Affordable YoY growth is about 11%.

qa_highlights.question: Will credit cost turn positive in H2, and what ROA path follows?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said credit cost should stay negative through FY27 given line of sight on recoveries. FY27 ROA guided around 2.4%; FY28 around 2.3% as credit cost normalises; long-term 2.3% to 2.35%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did recoveries of about INR 77 crore not fully flow through ECL writeback, and where did the difference go?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said regular OTS settlements cost about INR 10-12 crore, booked as write-offs in Prime and Emerging legacy pool, explaining the gap versus the INR 67 crore recovery figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is Q2 net disbursement growth versus Q1 net, and what does July look like?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall Q2 net disbursement expected about 60-70% above Q1 net; Affordable 2.5x-2.6x Q1 net. Management said July was promising, with Prime and Emerging contributing 15-18% of Affordable business in July.

qa_highlights.question: How much benefit from rating upgrades and when will it show in cost of borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: CARE upgrade is done; ICRA and CRISIL pending. CFO said at least about 10 bps reduction in cost of borrowing should come through; some fresh borrowing already at better rates.

qa_highlights.question: Prime yield rose 8 bps: how much is mix versus like-for-like, and does self-employed mix raise risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 10-15 bps benefit to mix shift toward self-employed and non-home loans; without mix, Prime yield would have been roughly stable at 8.92-8.95%. Delinquency in Prime and Emerging said to have improved QoQ.

risks_watch: Affordable execution: Q1 net disbursement of INR 555 crore is below target; Q2 needs 2.5-2.6x Q1 net and 50-60% full-year Affordable growth is guided, with new CBO leadership still unproven.

Cost of borrowing: incremental cost rose about 18 bps in Q1 and management says it is still elevated; the NIM bottoming thesis depends on yield gains offsetting this plus further leverage increase (average 3.6x to 3.75x).
Rating upgrades: ICRA and CRISIL still pending; management expects at least 10 bps cost-of-funds benefit, timing not firm.
Credit cost: negative 12 bps in Q1 relies on written-off pool recoveries (INR 67 crore) that will shrink from about INR 340 crore; sustainability of negative credit cost beyond FY27 is open.
Fraud account of about INR 420 crore: fully provided in FY23, but recovery timing and quantum not guided; management declined to quantify expected FY27 recoveries.
Disbursement realisation under cheque-realisation accounting: management expects the transition to flow through over about two months, so Q2 reported figures depend on timing of realisations.
key_quotes: Yes, I think if I talk about Q2, I think we will try to beat both the numbers, which is gross or net.
So I think 18 to 20%, that's the guidance which we are going to definitely, our team is focusing on better growth than what we have given guidance.
Going forward, we feel NIM has largely bottomed out and should start improving from second half of this financial year.
So it was an artificial lift in NIM in Q4, whereas that start getting normalized from Q1 onwards.
540173|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term margin, yield and disbursement recovery, with repeated claims that margin, yield and cost of funds have bottomed and that July was strong. Cautious on specifics: management did not give exact Q2 figures, declined to quantify recoveries on the fraud account, and called incremental cost of borrowing still elevated.

rows.why: NIM fell 19 bps QoQ to 3.50% (12 bps leverage, 7 bps Q4 true-up); management says margin and yield have bottomed, with Prime yield +8 bps (10-15 bps mix benefit) and Affordable yield up ~50 bps QoQ, offset by incremental cost of borrowing up ~18 bps and average leverage up from 3.6x to 3.75x.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branch network rose by 12 to 404 but management plans no further branch openings and will use existing branches to contain opex (opex +10% YoY to INR 237 crore).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 overall loan book growth guided at 18-20% (maintained, with management expecting to beat it) and Q2 net disbursement guided 60-70% above Q1; loan book grew 15% YoY to INR 89,670 crore, so the guide implies acceleration.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; with no new branches planned and CRAR at 28.26%, there is no capacity-driven need for a capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says it expects to beat the 18-20% loan growth guidance but did not raise it; Q2 net disbursement guided 60-70% above Q1, but Affordable Q1 net was only INR 555 crore with ~11% like-for-like growth.

rows.why: Affordable needs 2.5-2.6x Q1 net disbursement in Q2 to hit 50-60% full-year growth, the new CBO leadership is unproven, and credit cost depends on written-off pool recoveries shrinking from ~INR 340 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Micro-housing policy rolled out in Q2 FY27 with meaningful contribution expected from H2 FY27; Emerging Developer Finance programme already disbursed INR 71 crore in Q1.

rows.label: Cost of borrowing relief from rating upgrades
rows.why: CARE upgrade done; ICRA and CRISIL pending; management expects at least ~10 bps lower cost of borrowing, against an incremental cost up ~18 bps in Q1.

rows.label: Affordable disbursement ramp
rows.why: Affordable net disbursement was INR 555 crore in Q1; July showed 15-18% of Affordable business and management guides Q2 Affordable at 2.5-2.6x Q1, but execution is unproven.

rows.label: Fraud account recovery (INR 420 crore)
rows.why: Fully provided in FY23, so no P&L impact, but management declined to quantify expected FY27 recoveries and timing is not guided.

tone.note: Management was confident that margin, yield and cost of funds have bottomed and that July was strong, but cautious on specifics: no exact Q2 figures, no quantified fraud-account recoveries, and incremental cost of borrowing still elevated. 540175|2026-03.headline: Regency Fincorp FY26 PAT rose 170% to INR13.4 crore on AUM of INR261.2 crore (up 45%), with secured MSME now about 61% of AUM.
540175|2026-03.overview: Maiden earnings call for FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) covering AUM, disbursements, profitability and asset quality. Management said the book is shifting from unsecured and JLG microfinance toward secured MSME lending and a planned salaried digital lending product (Cash My Salary app). Net NPA rose to 0.74% from 0.31%, which management attributed to legacy JLG and short-tenor unsecured loans. Management outlined a target of INR500-550 crore AUM this year and INR3,000 crore by FY30, funded by INR400-450 crore of expected lender borrowings. Cost of funds is currently 13-14%, with a target of 11-12% and a longer-term aim of 10-10.5%.

segments.name: Secured MSME lending
segments.commentary: Secured share of disbursement rose to about 57% in FY26 from 23% in FY25; secured book is about 61% of AUM versus 18% a year earlier. Average tenure 48-60 months, LTV 50-60%, ROI reducing from 20% to 24%.

segments.name: Unsecured MSME lending
segments.commentary: Book run down from about INR104 crore to about INR60 crore. Tenure around 12 months, kept for cash flow and collection continuity.

segments.name: JLG (group microfinance)
segments.commentary: About 10.5% of AUM. No disbursements since November 2025. Expected about 70% run-down by end FY27 and zero by end of calendar 2027.

segments.name: Digital personal loans (Cash My Salary)
segments.commentary: Salaried borrowers earning above INR45,000; pilot live with approval in 30-45 minutes; priced at about 24% flat for a six-month tenor. Targeted at 15-20% of AUM.

guidance_outlook: AUM target of about INR500-550 crore this year, roughly doubling from INR261 crore, with about 80% secured MSME, about INR75-100 crore digital, and INR400 crore secured.
Branch network to roughly double to about 50 branches by end FY27 and mid-calendar 2027, from 23 currently.
Cost of funds target of 11-12% this year (from 13-14%), with a further goal of 10-10.5% within 12 months; 10.25% cited for a net cost of funds.
Opex expected at about 2-2.75% of AUM; lending rates expected at 15-16% after cost reductions.
AUM target of INR3,000 crore by FY30.
NIM expected to be maintained at current levels rather than increased; PPI licence approval expected in the coming quarter or financial year.
capex_capacity: 23 branches; average branch AUM about INR10-12 crore (range from INR3 crore to INR10 crore).
Branches capable of disbursing about INR2-2.5 crore per month on average.
Plan to raise INR400-450 crore from banks and NBFCs this year, including ICICI, Axis, Yes Bank, LC Venture Debt, Lighthouse Canton and others.
RBI NOC received for PPI licence; digital wallet RedPay to launch within 12 months.
INR25 crore raised via compulsorily convertible debentures in April 2026, to fund secured MSME growth and digital lending.
demand_pricing: Average MSME ticket size INR35-45 lakh; collateral is residential or commercial constructed property (no land, industrial land or agri land), with an LTV of 50-60%.
Lending is restricted to non-trading MSMEs (hardware, small restaurants, hotels, small manufacturers); no real estate or trading lending.
Collection efficiency about 95-96% on zero-month basis and 97-98% on zero-plus basis.
Zero-plus DPD about INR2.2 crore (under 1% of AUM); 90-day PAR about INR65-70 lakh per the Q&A answer, and about INR40-60 lakh in another answer.
Expansion focus remains North India (Punjab, Haryana, Uttarakhand, UP, NCR); West India is next and South is not planned for 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What collateral secures the MSME loans and what is the SARFAESI and recovery process?
qa_highlights.answer: Collateral is mainly residential or commercial property at 50-60% LTV, with an average collateral value of INR65-75 lakh. Only one 90-DPD secured account is in legal recovery, expected to be liquidated within the quarter; in-house lawyers handle notices and third parties handle recovery.

qa_highlights.question: How will AUM reach INR500-550 crore and then INR3,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans to run down the unsecured book, raise INR400-450 crore from lenders, double branches to about 50, and keep opex at 2.5-2.75%. It targets INR3,000 crore AUM by FY30.

qa_highlights.question: How are NIMs protected as the mix shifts to secured lending, and what is the cost of funds target?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM is about 10.75-11% and is expected to hold at current levels as the digital product at about 24% offsets lower MSME yields. Cost of funds is 13-14% today, targeted at 11-12%, with a further decline possible once public sector banks lend.

qa_highlights.question: What drives asset quality deterioration and is the NPA rise structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the NPA rise to legacy JLG and Karja Mukti Abhiyan stress in Punjab and Haryana, plus short-tenor loans. It said the secured salaried book is less risky and cited industry NPA of about 1.5-1.6% versus its 0.76%.

qa_highlights.question: What differentiates the company and how does the PPI licence help?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sources 100% of leads in-house with no DSA, and the PPI wallet will give bank-statement visibility for early risk signals and cheaper lead generation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the cost of funds fall to 8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit to 8%, saying it expects a significant reduction in cost of funds and would pass part of the 2% arbitrage to customers within 12 months.

risks_watch: Net NPA rose to 0.74% from 0.31%, and the secured book is still seasoning; watch 90-DPD and collections in the secured book.
Heavy dependence on borrowings (INR400-450 crore planned) and a high cost of funds of 13-14%; rate cuts are targeted but not yet achieved.
Asset-liability tenor matching depends on borrowings of 4-5 years matching 48-60 month loans.
Regulatory approval of the PPI licence and the scale-up of Cash My Salary are still pending.
Concentration in North India, a region the company itself described as having delinquency-prone segments; the JLG run-down is still ongoing.
Disclosure inconsistencies on 90-DPD and CRAR prior-year figures; verify against the audited financial statements.
540175|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and growth-focused on strategy, with specific numbers on secured mix and cost targets. Answers on asset quality and forward cost of funds were more hedged, and some figures (PAR, CRAR trend) were given inconsistently.
key_quotes: Our approach has been to operate in these spaces with a model that is high yield, but tightly controlled. Because in lending, growth without discipline does not last.
The shift is deliberate strategy move to build a more resilient and low risk portfolio.
We will only have two products which has been focused for our company, which is MSME secured lending and digital lending part of it.
We are not doing any lending to any trading company, no real estate, no trading.

financial_highlights.change: up 45% YoY from INR170 crore in FY25
down YoY per analyst question; no prior figure stated

rows.why: Cost of funds at 13-14% targeted to fall to 11-12% this year and 10-10.5% within 12 months, but management said NIM (about 10.75-11%) is expected to be maintained, not increased, and lending rates are expected to fall to 15-16%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branch network guided to roughly double from 23 to about 50 by end FY27, a 117% increase, with average branch AUM of INR10-12 crore and branches disbursing INR2-2.5 crore per month.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides AUM to INR500-550 crore from INR261.2 crore (roughly doubling, up 45% in FY26) with cumulative disbursement of INR142 crore in FY26 (up 43%).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Net NPA rose to 0.74% from 0.31%, the secured book is still seasoning, and the INR400-450 crore borrowing plan and cost-of-funds cut to 11-12% are not yet achieved with cost of funds at 13-14%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Cash My Salary digital salaried loans (pilot live, about 24% flat, targeted at 15-20% of AUM) and RedPay wallet launch within 12 months after RBI NOC; PPI approval expected in coming quarter or FY.

rows.label: Unsecured and JLG run-down
rows.when: end FY27 for JLG (about 70% run-down), zero by end CY27
rows.why: JLG is about 10.5% of AUM with no disbursements since Nov 2025, and unsecured book has fallen from about INR104 crore to about INR60 crore.

rows.label: Lender funding of INR400-450 crore
rows.why: Plan to raise INR400-450 crore from banks and NBFCs (ICICI, Axis, Yes Bank and others) against AUM of INR261 crore, with INR25 crore of CCDs already raised in April 2026.

rows.label: Cost of funds cut to 11-12%
rows.why: Cost of funds is 13-14% today; management declined to commit to 8% and said a significant reduction is expected once public sector banks lend.

tone.note: Management was confident on secured MSME mix, branch doubling and AUM targets, but hedged on asset quality and the cost-of-funds path; analysts pushed on NPA drivers, CRAR and whether cost of funds could reach 8%.

540175|2026-06.headline: Regency Fincorp Q1 FY27: PAT of INR7.0 crore on total income of INR17.4 crore (+86% YoY); AUM INR345 crore; blended cost of funds 13.25%.
540175|2026-06.overview: Regency Fincorp reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR17.4 crore (+86% YoY), PBT of INR9.4 crore and PAT of INR7.0 crore, with AUM rising to INR345 crore from INR261 crore at March 2026. Secured loan book grew to INR230 crore from INR159 crore, and unsecured share fell from 26% to 18%. Management said the blended borrowing cost is 13.25% and expects it to fall toward 12.75-12.95% by end-Q2 and 11.75-12.5% by year-end. Management reiterated FY27 targets of revenue above INR75 crore and PAT of INR25-30 crore, and AUM of INR500-550 crore by year-end.

financial_highlights.change: +44% from INR159 crore at Mar 2026; ~5x YoY

segments.name: Secured MSME lending
segments.commentary: Secured loan book INR230 crore at June 2026, up 44% from INR159 crore in March 2026. Yield on MSME deployments about 21-22%, net borrowing about 13.5%, opex about 2-2.25%, credit cost about 1%, spread about 3.4-3.5%.

segments.name: Digital lending (Cash My Salary)
segments.commentary: Digital portfolio about INR23 crore since launch, roughly 6-7% of AUM. Average tenor about 4 months, flat ~30% interest plus 5-7% processing fee, APR about 89% per management. Management reported 95-96% collection in month 0-1 across two cycles.

guidance_outlook: FY27 total revenue guided at upwards of INR75 crore (management calls this conservative); Q2-Q4 expected to exceed Q1.
FY27 PAT guided at INR25-30 crore.
AUM target of INR500-550 crore by end of FY27.
Blended cost of borrowing expected near 12.75-12.95% by end of Q2 FY27 and 11.75-12.5% by year-end; target to bring lending rates down to 11.5-12%.
Gross NPA to stay within 1-1.25% and net NPA at or below about 1%; credit cost below 1%.
Planned private placement of NCDs of INR50-75 crore in Q2 FY27 (board approved); proceeds to MSME secured and digital lending books.
Target to become a small finance bank by FY30; no deposit-taking until then.
Leverage target 3.5x-4x debt-to-net-owned-funds; management cited AUM target INR3,000 crore by FY30 in a question.
capex_capacity: Presence in five states (Punjab, Haryana, parts of Uttarakhand, eastern UP, Chandigarh base); board cap of 20% of portfolio in any state.
Branch AUM cap of INR12 crore for MSME secured (INR15 crore in Ludhiana); 20+ branches serving 16,000+ customers.
Digital pin code coverage about 11,000 today, targeted to rise to about 18,000 in the coming year.
Tech and digital team of 50+ members at Noida office; corporate office shifted to Delhi/Noida.
PPI license approved; expected to be operational in about 3-5 months.
demand_pricing: Secured MSME lending focused on Tier 2 cities; excludes trading, realty, livestock, agri and services; collateral is self-occupied built-up residential/commercial property at about 50% LTV; minimum 3-year business vintage.
Management targets MSME secured yield of 15-17% over time versus about 21-22% today, passing lower borrowing costs to customers.
Digital borrowers are salaried employees of corporates or LLPs with at least 6 months of salary credits; 70% fresh and 30% repeat customers.
Management sees organised salaried borrower universe of INR50,000-60,000 crore, and says competition is less intense in Tier 2 unorganised segments.
Cost-of-funds update: NCDs at 13% in Q1, plus a INR10 crore bank line at 10.35%; new banks guided at 10.75-11%.

qa_highlights.question: Why are recent NCDs at 14% when incremental cost of funds was guided to lower double digit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an NCD mandate signed earlier was at 14%, with later issuance at 13%; blended cost is 13.25%, targeted to fall to 12.75-12.95% by end-Q2 and 11.75-12.5% by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sectoral exposure of the secured MSME book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the book is mainly retail manufacturers and suppliers (hardware, small manufacturing, beverage/pulp sub-segments); trading, realty, livestock, agri and services are excluded.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 bottom-line and NNPA expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided FY27 revenue above INR75 crore and PAT of INR25-30 crore, with gross NPA not exceeding 1-1.25% and net NPA around 1%; it declined to give quarterly PAT guidance beyond calling Q1 numbers conservative.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company fund growth to INR1,500-2,000 crore AUM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will keep borrowings at 3.5x-4x net owned funds, so INR200 crore net worth supports about INR750-800 crore debt and about INR1,000 crore AUM, with further equity via internal accruals or preferential issues.

qa_highlights.question: How is digital customer acquisition done and at what cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisition relies on digital ads, referrals and RM-generated leads; management cited about 4% opex plus acquisition spend on digital book and said initial tech set-up is largely complete.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company replicate auditor and governance stability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Monika Garg is the current auditor and that any future change would be to a larger firm.

qa_highlights.question: What is the promoter holding outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to elaborate on the call and offered a one-to-one discussion, saying promoter holding is higher than the 24-25% that appears.

risks_watch: Concentration in Tier 2 Northern India markets; dependence on branch and state caps.
Digital unsecured book (about 20% of target mix) has short history of two cycles; NPA behaviour at scale is untested.
Cost-of-funds reduction depends on new bank lines (10.75-11%) and NCD pricing; NCDs were still raised at 13-14%.
Guidance implies sharp PAT step-up (INR25-30 crore vs INR7 crore in Q1); management did not provide quarterly path.
Auditor changes and promoter holding clarity were raised as governance points; management deferred promoter holding details to one-to-one.
Pending PPI licence and digital pin code expansion to 18,000 are dependencies for growth.
540175|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, digital strategy and cost-of-funds reduction, but evasive on promoter holding (deferred to one-to-one) and on quarterly profit outlook beyond calling the numbers conservative. Several answers were long and repetitive, and some figures (NNPA 0.74% vs 0.76%, digital share 6% vs 20% target) were inconsistent across the call.
key_quotes: We are not wanting being at a 23%, 24%. Our desire is 15%, 16%, 17%, okay?
We are not funding any thing which is related to livestock, whether it is a poultry, whether it is an animal husbandry onto it.

Our medium-term objective is very clear, that is to scale AUM towards INR500 to INR550 crores by the end of this fiscal year while maintaining strong asset quality, capital adequacy and governance standards.

rows.why: Blended cost of borrowing 13.25% is guided down to 12.75-12.95% by end-Q2 and 11.75-12.5% by year-end, while secured MSME spread is about 3.4-3.5% and the NCD mandate at 14% is being replaced by 13% issuance and a 10.35% bank line.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Digital pin code coverage is about 11,000 today, targeted at about 18,000 in the coming year, and the PPI licence is expected to go live in 3-5 months, but no physical capacity or branch number was given beyond the INR12 crore branch AUM cap.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM is guided from INR345 crore to INR500-550 crore by year-end, about 45-60% growth in roughly three quarters, backed by secured book up 44% QoQ to INR230 crore and the planned INR50-75 crore NCD placement in Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the asset-light model with branches capped at INR12 crore AUM and growth funded by NCDs of INR50-75 crore and a INR10 crore bank line points to no major capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management called FY27 revenue guidance of upwards of INR75 crore conservative against Q1 total income of INR17.4 crore (+86% YoY), but gave no quarterly path.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Guided PAT of INR25-30 crore requires a step-up from INR7.0 crore in Q1 (roughly 3.5-4x over the remaining three quarters), and NCDs are still being raised at 13-14%, so the cost-of-funds path is not yet proven.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: PPI licence approved and expected to be operational in about 3-5 months, so launch falls around Q2 FY27 end to Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Debt funding via NCDs and bank lines to fund growth
rows.why: Planned private placement of INR50-75 crore NCDs in Q2 FY27 (board approved) plus a INR10 crore bank line at 10.35%, with leverage held at 3.5x-4x net owned funds on INR181 crore net worth.

rows.label: Small finance bank conversion by FY30
rows.why: Management targets SFB status by FY30 with no deposit-taking until then, and cites an AUM target of INR3,000 crore by FY30; this is a long-dated, conditional goal.

rows.label: MSME secured yield reduction to 15-17%
rows.why: Yield on MSME deployments is about 21-22% today and management plans to pass lower borrowing costs to customers, which would compress yields toward 15-17% over time and could trade off against spread.

tone.note: Management was confident on AUM growth, cost-of-funds reduction and digital strategy, but evasive on promoter holding (deferred to one-to-one) and gave no quarterly PAT path; analysts pushed on the 14% NCD cost, the step-up needed to reach INR25-30 crore PAT, and governance points.

540175|2026-09.headline: Regency Fincorp H1 FY27 PAT rose 146% to INR16.3 crore; AUM reached INR610.25 crore and FY27 PAT guidance raised to INR40-42 crore.
540175|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 total income was INR32.44 crore (up 240% YoY) and PAT was INR9.01 crore (up 170.37% YoY). H1 FY27 total income of about INR49.5-49.87 crore and PAT of INR16.3 crore both already exceeded full-year FY26 levels. AUM reached INR610.25 crore at 30 September 2026, and management revised FY27 AUM guidance to INR900-950 crore and PAT guidance to INR40-42 crore. The company announced a proposed preferential issue of about INR312-313 crore to fund acquisitions of a digital lending platform and a gold loan business, with asset quality (GNPA 0.99%, NNPA 0.75%) reported within target range.

segments.name: Secured MSME lending
segments.commentary: Secured book of about INR452 crore (Q&A: INR410-420 crore) with cumulative disbursement of about INR252 crore across 2,366 active loans. Average ticket size INR50-55 lakh, possibly rising to INR75 lakh; target 70-75% of book.

segments.name: Digital lending (CashMySalary)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 disbursement of INR125 crore, more than 87,000 active loans across about 15,000 pin codes and 25-26 states. Short-tenure (90-day) salary-linked product; target 20-25% of book, capped at 30%.

segments.name: JetFund
segments.commentary: Newly launched digital instant salary advance and personal loan product, ticket size INR20,000 to INR1 lakh. Targeting AUM of INR50-55 crore by March 2027.

segments.name: Regency Fintech subsidiary
segments.commentary: Booked about INR14 crore revenue in Q2 with about INR1 crore profit contribution; management says it builds digital lending tech infrastructure and charges a nominal fee, with no revenue-sharing model. Regency Pay awaiting RBI licence, expected this quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM target revised to INR900-950 crore (earlier about INR600 crore), against INR610.25 crore at Sep 2026.
FY27 PAT target revised to INR40-42 crore or higher (earlier INR35-40 crore); management called it '100% achievable'.
Blended borrowing cost target of 10.75-11.25% by March 2027, with management also citing 11.5%; further 100 bps reduction expected.
AUM projections of INR2,000 crore in FY28 and INR3,000 crore in FY29, subject to acquisitions.
Leverage ceiling of 3.5-4x debt-to-equity, with conservative target of 3-3.2x.
Net worth expected to rise to INR290 crore by March 2027 and about INR615 crore by March 2028 after full preferential issue.
capex_capacity: Proposed preferential issue of about INR312-313 crore (equity plus warrants), approved by Board on 16 Oct 2026, with corporate, AIF and fund-house commitments.
INR100-125 crore to acquire a digital lending platform (100% stake), staged over 3-9 months; internal metrics done for one target, the other under independent due diligence.
Up to INR75 crore to acquire a majority (over 50%) stake in a gold loan company, expected over 3-4 months; two candidates evaluated.
Expanded tech and digital team; moved into a large office in Noida; headcount of 390 employees.
Possible four hub-and-spoke digital centres (Noida plus Bangalore, east and west India) subject to capacity build-out.
demand_pricing: Management says the secured book is about 70% of portfolio with LTV around 60% and collateral cover above 100%.
Digital book is limited to salaried customers (2 years ITR, 6+ months tenure, six salaries received).
Digital customer retention reported at 70%; company says in-house digital marketing lowers vendor costs versus associates.
Competition: management says NBFC peers run debt-to-equity of 4.5-5x versus Regency's 2.66x.

qa_highlights.question: Is the rise in GNPA to 0.99% driven by mix or specific segment stress, and what safeguards exist against the targets of GNPA below 1.25% and NNPA below 1%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross NPA is about INR6.2 crore, with asset-backed recovery of INR2.5-2.75 crore expected, and saw no foreseen stress. Secured book is being pushed to 75% with LTV around 60%, and the digital book is limited to salaried borrowers.

qa_highlights.question: How much headroom is there on leverage, and what is the optimal debt-to-equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a leverage ceiling of 3.5-4x, conservative 3-3.2x, versus 2.66x now. Preferential equity adds about INR100 crore to net worth of INR189.55 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the cost of funds decline and the FY27 revenue and PAT guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended borrowing cost fell from 13.5% to 12.35% in six months, with a further 100 bps targeted by March 2027. Revised PAT guidance of INR40-42 crore reflects AUM growth and the acquisitions adding revenue later.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Regency Fintech subsidiary's revenue and cost structure, and any related-party link to the digital platform acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the subsidiary builds tech infrastructure and charges a nominal fee passed between balance sheets, with no revenue-sharing model. The target platform is a third party generating about INR2 crore profit per month and is an arm's-length deal.

qa_highlights.question: How will the preferential proceeds be used, and will any go to lender repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: INR100-125 crore goes to the digital platform, up to INR75 crore to the gold loan stake, and the balance to MSME and digital lending growth plus general corporate purposes. Management said no proceeds will go to repay lenders, since repayments come from the portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AUM trajectory from FY27 to FY29 and the AUM growth between FY26 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM rose from INR290-294 crore at March 2026 to INR610 crore, with growth from new borrowers, including INR125 crore in digital disbursement. Management projects INR2,000 crore in FY28 and INR3,000 crore in FY29.

risks_watch: Acquisitions (digital platform and gold loan) are subject to approvals and due diligence; revenue contribution from the gold loan business is expected mainly in FY28.
Related-party question on Regency Fintech was answered qualitatively; no quantified intercompany fee or cost breakdown was disclosed.
Regency Pay licence from RBI is pending and expected in the current quarter.
Asset quality: GNPA rose to 0.99% against a target below 1.25%; watch digital and secured book slippages.
Rising leverage on a 2.66x base, with dependence on preferential issue completion.
Q2 PAT is reported as INR9.01 crore in one place and INR9.3 crore in another; the figure needs reconciliation against the filed results.
540175|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and assertive, with strong forward targets (AUM, PAT and FY28-29 projections). Less precise under questioning: related-party and subsidiary economics were answered qualitatively, and several figures were inconsistent across answers.
key_quotes: Our assets under management stood at INR610.25 crores as of 30th September 2026.
We are targeting an AUM of approximately INR900 crores to INR950 crores by the end of the financial year 2027.
The net interest margin increased to 7.54% in H1 FY2027 from 3.51% in H1 FY2026, supported by a high-yield portfolio mix and a lower blended cost of funds.

Our revised numbers of INR900 crores to INR950 crores of AUM and profitability of between INR40 crores to INR42 crores of northwards should be 100% achievable with the numbers that we are putting across.

INR452 crore (Q&A: INR410-420 crore secured AUM)

financial_highlights.change: INR425 crore raised via NCDs and term loans in H1 FY27
down from 13.5% at start of FY27
expected INR290 crore by Mar 2027 post issue

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM is INR610.25 crore at Sep 2026 against FY27 guidance of INR900-950 crore, requiring roughly 48-56% growth in the second half, and H1 digital disbursement was INR125 crore.

rows.why: Utilisation is not disclosed, but the company has announced acquisitions and said four hub-and-spoke digital centres are possible subject to capacity build-out.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 PAT guidance was raised to INR40-42 crore or higher from INR35-40 crore, H1 PAT of INR16.3 crore already covers about 40% of the midpoint, and management calls it '100% achievable'.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: GNPA rose to 0.99% against a target below 1.25%, leverage is rising from 2.66x toward a 3-3.2x target, and the plan depends on completing the INR312-313 crore issue and the acquisitions.

rows.when: Regency Pay licence expected this quarter; JetFund AUM targe
rows.why: JetFund was newly launched with an INR50-55 crore AUM target by March 2027, and Regency Pay awaits an RBI licence expected this quarter.

rows.label: Leverage rising toward 3-3.2x target
rows.why: Debt-to-equity is 2.66x on INR505 crore borrowings, and the target is 3-3.2x with a 3.5-4x ceiling, so the preferential issue adds about INR100 crore net worth and new debt is likely.

rows.label: Digital disbursement and retention
rows.why: H1 FY27 digital disbursement was INR125 crore with more than 87,000 active loans and 70% customer retention, supporting the digital book's growth to 20-25% of the total.

rows.label: Preferential issue completion
rows.why: The INR312-313 crore issue was approved by the Board on 16 Oct 2026 with corporate, AIF and fund-house commitments, and it lifts net worth from INR189.55 crore to about INR290 crore by March 2027.

tone.note: Management was confident on AUM, PAT and FY28-29 targets and the cost of funds decline, but was qualitative on related-party economics of Regency Fintech; analysts pushed on asset quality, leverage headroom and the use of preferential proceeds.

540180|2026-03.headline: Varun Beverages Q1 CY2026 revenue rose 18.1% to Rs 65,742 mn and EBITDA 21% to Rs 15,289 mn on 16.3% volume growth.
540180|2026-03.overview: Consolidated volumes grew 16.3% to 363.4 mn cases, with India up 14.4% and international up 21.4%, after a weak prior-year summer hit by rains. Consolidated realisation per case rose 1.6% on favourable currency in international markets, while India realisation fell 1.5% on pack upsizing and selective Rs 10 price points. EBITDA margin expanded 55 bps to 23.3% and PAT rose 20.1% to Rs 8,787 mn, though depreciation (+30.9%) and finance cost (+18%) rose on new plants and the Twizza acquisition. Management said it is covered on packaging and raw materials for the current quarter and holds about 6 months of inventory internationally, with the crude-linked cost risk flagged for later quarters.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Volume up 14.4%; realisation down 1.5% on pack upsizing and selective Rs 10 price points; India EBITDA margin up 112 bps on operating efficiencies and gross margin gains.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Volume up 21.4%, with management saying all international markets grew double digits except Morocco; Twizza (South Africa) acquired via BevCo at EV ZAR 2,053 mn.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: CSD 73.6% of volume, non-carbonated beverages 7.5%, packaged water 18.9%; low/no-sugar products about 63% of consolidated volume. Dairy growing about 60% with realisation near 3x normal; Tropicana PET above 100% growth.

segments.name: Snacks / food distribution (Africa)
segments.commentary: Q1 snack foods revenue Rs 112 cr vs Rs 52 cr in Q1 CY25; Zimbabwe plant commissioned end of last year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q2 demand to be better than Q1 if weather holds; said first month of summer 'looks very good'.
India raw material cover is complete for this quarter and partial for next; international inventory about 6 months, so near-term impact described as zero to a couple of points.
Gasoline/transport cost increases expected to be absorbed by reducing discounts and efficiency gains; no major P&L impact expected if volumes hold.
India capex for CY26 expected below Rs 500-600 cr, with only one plant planned.
Management expects double-digit growth in India for the next 5-10 years and international growth not below double digits absent external shocks.
Expects about 500,000 new outlets to be added in CY26 on a base of about 4 mn outlets.
Crickley Dairy acquisition (EV about ZAR 238 mn incl. working capital) subject to regulatory approvals.
capex_capacity: India capex for CY26 to be under Rs 500-600 cr, with only about one new plant; existing capacity seen sufficient to deliver up to 50% growth without new capacity.

Four plants commissioned last year (Buxar, Prayagraj, Damtal, Meghalaya) have stabilised; management says it is no longer opening smaller plants and cost of production in larger plants is about half that of smaller ones.
Twizza revenue about Rs 800 cr (last full year), acquisition price about Rs 1,140 cr; Crickley Dairy revenue about Rs 160 cr; combined about Rs 1,000 cr. Margins not yet guided.
Typical plant payback 3-4 years at around 30% RoCE, per management.
Aluminium cans are under 2% of sales; cans tied up above that level, though shortage in the industry.
demand_pricing: Management says the summer season is strong after a weak prior year, with May and June the key months; April end was 'not great'.
Industry chilling equipment additions of about 1 mn units per year (about 0.5 mn from Campa, Coke and VBL combined plus 0.4-0.5 mn own coolers by outlets).
Rs 10 price point used selectively, under 2% of total volume, to retain distributors.
Competitors (B-brands, water players) have cut discounts rather than raise prices, per management; PET and can shortages affecting the whole industry.
Ad-Rush (Rs 60 mid-priced energy drink) performing well above plan; can shortage constraining supply. Sting Classic launched in cans and PET (April), with early response described as strong.

qa_highlights.question: What is the near-term impact of higher oil prices on packaging and other costs?
qa_highlights.answer: International raw materials impact practically zero to a couple of points given about 6 months inventory; India has minor impact for this quarter and some for next, offset by lower discounts and cost cuts. Transport cost cannot be stocked but is absorbable.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India realisation improve to -1.5% from -4% last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Premiumisation through new launches and dairy growth of about 60% (realisation near 3x normal) helped, along with lower discounting and efficiency; Rs 10 price points are used selectively.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company placed on aluminium cans and PET supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Cans are under 2% of sales and tied up above that requirement; shortage is industry-wide and customers may switch to PET or glass.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2-year CAGR slowdown in India a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the 6-8% figure, citing a 23% average CAGR historically; said last year was an exceptional weather-hit year and growth should stay double-digit.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a margin hit if crude stays high for several quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it holds 6 months inventory and expects competitors to take price increases or absorb the hit first; does not expect to take a hit itself.

qa_highlights.question: Is the upsizing from 250 ml to 400 ml adding consumption, and is India margin affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumption is rising both in litres and in units; full-quarter upsizing effects already absorbed by volumes and plant efficiency, with minor upsides to be absorbed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plant payback and utilisation impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Normal payback 3-4 years at around 30% RoCE; higher utilisation is helping as larger lines (1,000 bottles per minute vs 200) replace old high-cost plants.

risks_watch: Crude-linked input cost (PET, gasoline, transport) and aluminium can shortage could pressure margins from Q2 if discounts cannot be cut further.
India realisation may fall further (management said it 'might even become lower') with discounting and pack upsizing.
Weather risk: management says the season depends on rains and any abnormal rain could hurt volumes; prior-year weather hit was severe.
Integration of Twizza and Crickley Dairy: margins not yet disclosed; Crickley subject to regulatory approvals.
Finance cost and depreciation growth (+18% and +30.9%) will weigh on PAT growth relative to EBITDA.
540180|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and summer trends, with an assertive tone on cost cover. Management was evasive on specifics such as Twizza/Crickley margins, future price increases and competitor share, and pushed back on the analyst's 2-year CAGR framing.
key_quotes: We are completely covered for this quarter, and we are partly covered for the next quarter also.
We think other people will blink before we blink, we have to wait and see.
Normally we work on a 3-4 year payback. 30% RoCE.
Water is like a commodity, you can increase your sales as much as you want by offering discounts, which we are not in the game of and that is why we can sustain our margins.

Four new plants commissioned last year (Buxar, Prayagraj, Damtal, Meghalaya)

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Sting Classic launched in cans and PET in April with a strong early response, Ad-Rush (Rs 60) is running well above plan, and dairy is growing about 60%, though no further launch dates were given.

rows.label: Twizza and Crickley Dairy acquisitions
rows.why: Twizza (acquired at about Rs 1,140 cr, last-year revenue about Rs 800 cr) is already consolidated and Crickley (about ZAR 238 mn, revenue about Rs 160 cr) awaits regulatory approval, adding roughly Rs 1,000 cr combined revenue with margins not yet guided.

rows.label: Offsetting crude cost via lower discounts and efficiency
rows.why: Management says gasoline and transport increases will be absorbed by cutting discounts and efficiency gains, with no major P&L impact if volumes hold; international inventory covers about 6 months.

rows.label: Competitor price increases before VBL
rows.why: Management expects competitors to take price increases or absorb the crude-cost hit first, and says B-brands and water players have cut discounts rather than raised prices, though under 2% of volume is on Rs 10 price points.

tone.note: Management was confident on summer demand, cost cover and double-digit growth, but evasive on Twizza/Crickley margins and future price increases, and pushed back on the analyst's 2-year CAGR slowdown framing; analysts pressed on India realisation and the 2-year CAGR.

540180|2026-06.headline: VBL Q2 CY2026 revenue rose 20.4% to Rs 84,512.3 mn and EBITDA 17.2% to Rs 23,430.4 mn, with India volume up 14.4%.
540180|2026-06.overview: Consolidated sales volume grew 19.8% to 466.7 million cases in the quarter, with net revenue up 20.4% year-on-year. India volume grew 14.4%, with growth of about 20% or more in every month since March except April, which was roughly flat due to El Nino-driven rain. International volumes rose 38.4%, including 11.8 million cases from the newly consolidated Twizza business in South Africa. EBITDA margin fell 76 bps to 27.7% on Twizza's lower margins, while India margin improved 38 bps. Management also extended the PepsiCo bottling licence to April 2049 and announced the Calpis tie-up with Asahi and the Devyani Kenya acquisition.

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue from operations (net of excise and GST)

financial_highlights.value: Rs 0.50 per share (25% of face value), cash outflow ~Rs 1,691 million

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Volume grew 14.4% in Q2 with 20%+ monthly growth from March except April (about flat). India EBITDA margin improved 38 bps on operating efficiencies, partly offset by higher transport and distribution costs. Low-sugar/no-sugar products were about 73% of consolidated volume in H1.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Volume rose 38.4% including 11.8 million cases from Twizza in South Africa; ex-Twizza growth was above 25%. Management said all African markets are growing except Zambia, which is small and slower. Twizza operates at lower margins, which diluted group EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Value-added dairy (VAD) and Nimbooz
segments.commentary: Management said VAD is growing above 40% and Nimbooz above 30% for the company, about 3x-4x the overall business. Growth figures were given only as ranges, with no absolute values.

segments.name: Food distribution and manufacturing in Africa
segments.commentary: Management said this business is growing about 50%. No absolute figures or targets were given.

guidance_outlook: Management expects India growth of at least 20% month-on-month after June, with July tracking the same trend.
Management said India can keep growing in double digits despite a stronger competitive field from Campa and Coca-Cola, and argued the industry is growing about 20%.

Raw material costs have risen with the West Asia crisis. Part of the increase is booked in Q2 under average costing, and the balance will hit Q3. Management said the impact will not be large and pricing will hold.
Management said EBITDA margins can be maintained even in a high-crude year and would improve once the conflicts ease.
Energy drink labels must drop the word 'energy' within 90 days, per the regulator's guidance. Management said volumes are returning to STING as new labels roll out.
Management will not scale Rs 10 pricing for now, as it is not profitable for the company, unless monthly growth falls below 20%.
capex_capacity: H1 net capitalised capex of ~Rs 9,500 mn: ~Rs 2,000 mn brownfield India including a value-added dairy line at Supa, ~Rs 1,000 mn for a snack plant in Zimbabwe, and ~Rs 4,000 mn for market infrastructure (visi-coolers, glass bottles, pallets, vehicles).
Capital work-in-progress of ~Rs 4,900 mn at 30 June 2026, mainly South Africa expansion and a CSD line in Kenya.
Inorganic capex of Rs 11,314 mn for the Twizza Limited acquisition in South Africa.
Devyani Food Industries (Kenya) business acquisition agreed, giving a ready go-to-market for CSDs and energy drinks in Kenya.
Twizza in South Africa helped overcome capacity constraints, with the company strengthening its manufacturing and route-to-market footprint there.
demand_pricing: India Q2 volume +14.4%, with April about flat due to heavy rain. May seasonality has shifted (it used to be about 15% of business before 2025), and management says non-weather months show high double-digit growth.
Rs 10 price point: management said it has not scaled it up because it is not profitable and the company is growing 20%+ without it. Some markets are pushing Rs 10 packs, but the mix is small.
Pack changes: the company is upsizing and downsizing packs by market. Management said volume is reported on an 8-ounce basis, and realisation per 8-ounce case and gross margin are said to be stable.
Competition: Campa Cola is expanding at Rs 10 and Rs 20 price points, and management said the Rs 20 gap has narrowed. The 400 ml Rs 20 pack is driving recruitment.
GST cuts: management said the impact on dairy, water and soda was minimal. Some prices were held despite geopolitical cost pressure.
Management declined to give market share data, saying it does not track share.

qa_highlights.question: Is there room to scale the Rs 10 price point, and how much of the April weakness was rain versus competition from Campa?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not scaling Rs 10 because it is unprofitable. It said India is growing 20%+ month-on-month outside April, which was hit by El Nino.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company expanding into alcobev in India, and is it bidding for Bira?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is only looking at possible new categories and is not bidding for Bira. Prathmesh Mishra was hired for the group, not the company.

qa_highlights.question: Can India grow at low double digits given stronger competitors and a high base?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman Ravi Jaipuria said H1 India growth was 14.4% and July is continuing at the same trend, so double-digit growth looks achievable. Varun Jaipuria said weather, not demand, was holding back growth in months without rain.

qa_highlights.question: Up to what crude level can margins be maintained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are maintainable even in a worse geopolitical year and that margins cannot get worse once conflicts ease. It did not give a crude threshold.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the energy drink labelling change on STING?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said June and July saw a temporary dip as volume moved to CSD. Volumes are returning as new labels roll out, and the regulator gave 90 days to remove the word 'energy'.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Calpis tie-up extend to other Asahi brands or other categories?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current focus is stabilising Calpis. Dairy is a core category, and no decision has been made on RTD tea or coffee.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation from the West Asia crisis: part of the cost is in Q2 under average costing, and the balance hits Q3.
Monsoon and El Nino weather volatility, which hurt April and shifted the seasonal pattern of May.
Lower Twizza margins, which pulled group EBITDA margin down 76 bps; further integration and dilution is possible.
Energy drink labelling change, with a 90-day compliance deadline. Some volume shifted to CSD in June-July.
Rising competitive intensity from Campa Cola's Rs 10 and Rs 20 packs and Coca-Cola, which could pressure India volume and pricing.
Net debt of ~Rs 3,730 mn at consolidated level after the Twizza acquisition.
540180|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on volume momentum and margins, with management repeatedly citing 20%+ growth and calling the margin outlook comfortable. It was evasive on Rs 10 scale-up, market share, Bira and PepsiCo's share data, and deferred on the Calpis expansion and new categories.
key_quotes: If you see our growth, which is March onwards, we are growing healthily at 20% plus.
We can comfortably maintain our margins even in a year, which is the worst year for the geopolitical reasons and all the costing has gone up internationally.
Cans is 1- 2% of our business, nothing major.
Largely our portfolio is low sugar or Zero Sugar as you call it.
