rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin fell 76 bps to 27.7% on Twizza's lower margins, India margin rose 38 bps, and West Asia raw material costs hit Q3 in part, so management says margins are maintainable but gives no expansion number.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About Rs 4,900 mn capital WIP at 30 June 2026 for South Africa expansion and a Kenya CSD line, plus Rs 2,000 mn brownfield India including the Supa dairy line, but no capacity numbers or dates were given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: India volume grew 14.4% in Q2 with 20%+ monthly growth since March except April, management guides at least 20% month-on-month growth after June, and ex-Twizza international growth was above 25%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is already running at about Rs 9,500 mn in H1 and the Devyani Kenya deal is agreed, but utilisation was not disclosed, so a fresh capex announcement cannot be tied to a capacity number.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held India growth at low double-digit or better and called margins comfortable, with no sign of raising guidance; the Q3 raw material hit and Rs 10 not being scaled cap the upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Part of the raw material cost increase from the West Asia crisis hits Q3, and Twizza dilutes margins, though management says the impact will not be large and pricing will hold.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is stabilising Calpis with no decision on RTD tea or coffee, and is only looking at possible new categories, with Rs 10 pricing not being scaled for now.

rows.label: Devyani Food Industries Kenya acquisition
rows.why: The acquisition is agreed and gives a ready go-to-market for CSDs and energy drinks in Kenya, where a CSD line is already in capital WIP.

rows.label: Energy drink label change hits STING volume
rows.why: June and July saw a temporary dip as volume moved to CSD, and the 90-day compliance deadline means volumes return only as new labels roll out.

rows.label: Rs 10 price point not scaled
rows.why: Management will not scale Rs 10 packs unless monthly growth falls below 20%, and Campa is expanding at Rs 10 and Rs 20 price points.

tone.note: Management was confident on India volume momentum (14.4% in H1, 20%+ monthly since March) and on margins, but evasive on Rs 10 scale-up, market share, Bira and Campa competition, while analysts pressed on the high base and whether double-digit India growth holds.

540203|2026-03.headline: Sheela Foam Q4 FY26 consolidated core EBITDA rose 90% YoY to INR121 crore at an 11.5% margin, with first-ever dividend of 20% recommended.
540203|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 24% YoY to INR1,050 crore, and FY26 revenue rose 11% to INR3,821 crore, with management citing record foam production, top line and EBITDA. Core EBITDA for FY26 was INR414 crore (10.8% margin, up 261 bps), and consolidated PAT was INR92 crore in Q4 (about 7x YoY) and INR161 crore for FY26. Net debt fell INR156 crore in FY26, and the Board recommended a first-ever 20% dividend. Management flagged raw material (TDI, polyol) volatility from the Middle East conflict, saying prices were 25-35% higher on average, and that pass-through has largely been taken.

financial_highlights.value: INR161 crore; INR144 crore earned in H2

segments.name: Mattress (India, Sleepwell + Kurlon)
segments.commentary: Volumes grew 13% YoY in Q4 and 12% for FY26; value grew 13% in Q4 and 10% for FY26. Around 600 net new showrooms were added in FY26.

segments.name: Foam (India)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume grew 34% and value 36%, aided by better price realisation. FY26 volume grew 18% and value 14%. Management said B2B and comfort foam grew upwards of 15% annually.

segments.name: U2O (unorganised to organised, small-town India)
segments.commentary: Served through 8,400 dealers across over 5,000 towns in 24 states. FY26 volume grew 65% and value 111%, helped by a higher-priced second model and price increases.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Brand.com sales grew 136% YoY and platform sales 39% YoY in FY26; management cited a 52% value growth figure in Q&A.

segments.name: Australia (Joyce)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR422 crore with EBITDA margin of 10%, up almost 400 bps from FY25, driven by yield programmes, price renegotiation and supply-chain restructuring.

segments.name: Spain
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR391 crore with EBITDA margin of 10.4%, against 8.4% in FY25. Management sees a stable 30-32% gross margin range.

segments.name: Furlenco
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR370 crore (over 60% growth) and PAT of close to INR60 crore versus INR3 crore in FY25. Company holds about 43% fully diluted; FY27 revenue target is about INR500 crore.

segments.name: Staqo (IT)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue of INR70 crore.

guidance_outlook: Targeted growth of 15%+ over the medium term, expected to be higher given raw material-led price increases; management is aiming for a 3-5 year horizon to become a full product player.
Management believes core EBITDA margin is in an 11-12% range and can move higher with growth; Q1-Q2 FY27 margin impact from raw materials expected at no more than 50-100 bps.
FY27 standalone depreciation guided at INR140-145 crore on a consolidated basis, roughly INR35 crore per quarter.
FY27 capex guided at INR125-150 crore including maintenance, debottlenecking, marketing capex for new stores, across India, Australia and Spain.
Consolidated finance cost guided at about INR50 crore for FY27 (about INR35 crore interest plus INR15 crore other charges).
India debt of about INR300 crore expected to be repaid in 1-1.5 years; Australia and Spain debt of about INR350 crore is self-liquidating.
Remaining Kurlon synergies of about INR40 crore (out of INR250 crore total) depend on new machines that are delayed about 1.5 quarters; installation expected by mid or end of Q1 FY27.
Furlenco IPO decision to be taken in the next 3-4 months; listing expected in about one year or later.
Dividend of 20% for FY26 recommended, subject to shareholder approval; first dividend in company history.
Pillows (about INR100 crore market) to be treated as a separate category going forward; brand.com and U2O remain focus areas.
Hope to cross 100 integrated Furlenco-Sheela stores in FY27 (currently over 40).
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at INR125-150 crore including maintenance, debottlenecking to support volume growth of about 15% in FY26, and new store marketing capex.
Greater Noida foaming machine has run for 22 years, producing about 25,000 tonnes of foam per annum; management cited 40-50 year asset lives in the depreciation policy change.
A 500 kW solar plant is operational at Jabalpur, with over 1,000 kW of additional solar under progress at other manufacturing locations.
New imported machines for malleable-fibre comfort-layer production are under installation, delayed about 1.5 quarters, to support INR40 crore synergy.
demand_pricing: Raw material pricing: TDI and polyol rose 25-35% on average. Polyol was about INR120/kg in January, peaked near INR220, and is now around INR180-200. TDI is currently around INR275 (GNFC price); management cites a 5-year average of about INR240.
Pass-through is strong in B2C and industrial foam and partial in B2B. Management said the price increase has already been taken and margins will not be hit going forward.
Q4 volume spike was partly from smaller foam players exiting due to supply constraints, and from share gains in comfort and B2B foam. Management said no major channel stocking occurred.
TDI supply: GNFC plant shut for technical and gas reasons, so the company added a new hedging supplier (Korea, Japan and China sources) and avoided stock-outs at higher prices.
Management said organised share is rising relative to unorganised, reversing the trend of the last couple of years.
Marketing spend for FY26 is around 4.5% of sales, similar to last year.

qa_highlights.question: Are margins under pressure in Q1-Q2 FY27 given higher-cost raw material inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Gupta said price changes flow through in 10-15 days and inventory costs match, so the gross margin impact is limited to about 50-100 bps. Volume growth, given a 30%+ contribution margin, should support EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why is U2O value growth (111%) far above volume growth (65%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Rakesh Chahar said a higher-priced second model was introduced and both models saw price increases. U2O margins are between offline and e-commerce margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the change in depreciation policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Gupta said the written-down method front-loaded depreciation (70-75% in the first 3-4 years) for assets with 40-50 year lives, so the policy was realigned to useful life.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Australia and Spain margins, and is a sale still under consideration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees Spain gross margins at 30-32% and Australian margins up about 4-5 points on a normal basis. The target is 10-12% EBITDA. Rahul Gautam said the company is open to a sale but is not actively pursuing one.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Furlenco plans and how is ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Gupta said the company holds about 43% fully diluted and invested about INR430 crore, with ROCE of 30-35%. FY27 revenue target is about INR500 crore; an IPO is considered once a threshold size is reached, possibly in about a year.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the remaining synergy is pending?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Gupta said INR190-200 crore of the INR250 crore synergy is achieved, with INR40 crore pending on new machines that are delayed about 1.5 quarters and expected to be installed by mid or end of Q1 FY27.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility (TDI, polyol) from the Middle East conflict and GNFC supply disruption; management admits pricing is hard to predict.
Sustainability of the Q4 volume spike, which was partly from competitors exiting; whether customers stay after supply normalises.
Delayed INR40 crore synergy from new machines; watch whether it is installed by end of Q1 FY27.
Depreciation policy change flatters reported profit; compare with peers on a like-for-like basis.
Furlenco IPO timing and valuation, and integration of its stores into the network.
Management did not disclose the U2O volume share of total mattress volumes; a follow-up was promised.
540203|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, margins and the dividend, with explicit targets. Cautious and somewhat evasive on raw material pricing trajectory and on the timing of any sale of the international business.
key_quotes: This marks the first dividend recommended by the company since listing or for that matter, forever.
We are a 30% plus contribution margin business.
So polyols should be around INR120 plus and TDI should be around INR240 or something like that.
It will not revert to 28%, 29%, which we had seen in the past.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Core EBITDA margin rose to 11.5% in Q4 (from 7.5%) and 10.8% for FY26 (+261 bps); management sees 11-12% range moving higher with growth, with 30%+ contribution margin on volume and Australia/Spain margins expanding (Australia 10%, Spain 10.4%).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Only new capacity is comfort-layer imported machines delayed ~1.5 quarters, due mid or end Q1 FY27, supporting INR40 crore synergy; FY27 capex of INR125-150 crore is mostly maintenance and debottlenecking, and no new plant or utilisation figure was disclosed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q4 foam volume grew 34% and mattress volume 13%, with ~600 net new showrooms in FY26 and B2B/comfort foam growing above 15% a year, though Q4 spike was partly from competitors exiting.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex guided at INR125-150 crore (raised range) but utilisation was not disclosed, so a new plant announcement cannot be confirmed from the brief.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Medium-term growth target is 15%+, expected to be higher given raw-material-led price rises; FY26 volume grew 15% (foam volume +18%, U2O volume +65%) and Q4 share gains came from exiting competitors.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw material (TDI, polyol) prices rose 25-35% on average and management guided a 50-100 bps gross margin hit in Q1-Q2 FY27, while TDI supply depends on GNFC which is shut; management says pass-through is largely done.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Pillows (~INR100 crore market) to be treated as a separate category and brand.com and U2O remain focus areas, but no specific new product launch dates were given.

rows.label: India debt repayment of ~INR300 crore
rows.why: Net debt fell INR156 crore in FY26 and India debt of ~INR300 crore is expected to be repaid in 1-1.5 years, with FY27 finance cost guided at ~INR50 crore.

rows.label: Furlenco IPO decision
rows.when: decision in 3-4 months; listing in about a year or later
rows.why: Company holds ~43% fully diluted in Furlenco (FY26 PAT ~INR60 crore vs INR3 crore in FY25) and FY27 revenue target is ~INR500 crore; IPO considered once threshold size is reached.

rows.label: Kurlon synergy INR40 crore pending
rows.why: INR190-200 crore of INR250 crore synergy achieved; remaining INR40 crore depends on imported machines delayed ~1.5 quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, margins, the first dividend and debt paydown, but cautious and somewhat evasive on raw material pricing trajectory and on any sale of Australia and Spain; analysts probed margin impact of costlier inventory, U2O value-versus-volume gap, and the depreciation policy

540203|2026-06.headline: Sheela Foam Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 26% to INR1,032 crore and EBITDA 45% to INR109 crore, with margin at 10.6%.
540203|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to INR1,032 crore and EBITDA rose 45% to INR109 crore, with margin up 139 bps to 10.6%. Standalone India revenue grew 20% to INR761 crore and EBITDA 13% to INR68 crore, with gross margin compressed by sharp raw-material (TDI/polyol) swings that management attributes to the Middle East conflict. Management chose to keep growing foam volumes, which was cash-accretive, and international subsidiaries (Australia, Spain) posted sharply higher margins on inventory gains. Management reiterated a 15% EBITDA margin target for next year and expects volumes to recover in the festive quarters.

segments.name: India mattresses
segments.commentary: Value up 15% and volume up 6% YoY. U2O channel revenue up 81% with volume up 19%, now about 10,000 dealers, helped by 5- and 6-inch mattresses.

segments.name: India foam
segments.commentary: Value up 26% and volume up 4% YoY; faster foam growth diluted gross margin but was cash-accretive as competitors lacked raw material.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Brand.com sales up 69% YoY, platforms up 19%; overall category up 30% with volumes up 23%.

segments.name: Staqo (IT)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 67% YoY with EBITDA margin around 28-30%; Presence 360 crossed 3.2 lakh users.

segments.name: Furlenco (associate)
segments.commentary: Operating profit roughly INR9 crore per quarter; Q1 PAT share reflects 35% stake and no deferred tax asset recognition (DTA only booked at year end, likely Q4).

guidance_outlook: Reiterated 15% EBITDA margin target for next year; management said there is no change to this stance, though Rachna Kukreja's question suggested earlier 11-12% FY27 guidance.
Expects more than 15% revenue growth for the full year and double-digit volume growth in both foam and mattresses for FY27.

International operations to grow about 5% in local currency with 10-12% EBITDA margins; for FY27, management is confident of crossing INR1,000 crore revenue and about INR120 crore EBITDA for overseas operations.
Synergy benefit of about INR40 crore still pending; machine under installation, with full impact expected in Q3.
Integration of Kurlon about 96-97% complete; roughly 75-80% of synergies realised, with the balance expected.
Expects volume recovery with Q3 (festive) and Q4 the strongest quarters; FY27 volume expected to exceed last year.
Expects ROCE to reach roughly 20-25% in three years from about 10% currently.
Debt: India debt above INR300 crore to be cleared in about one year; overseas debt of about INR350 crore to be repaid over five years. Balance sheet will not be debt free by year-end.
capex_capacity: Company-operated stores (COCO): about INR27 lakh capex per store plus INR20-22 lakh working capital; about INR50 lakh per store, so about INR25 crore for 50 stores. Stores are about 2,000 sq ft (range 1,800-3,000).
COCO store rollout: 22 existing stores upgraded; target 50 stores with about 42 operational.
Furlenco shop-in-shop: about 40-50 stores currently; first target 100 stores. Company has about 3,500 exclusive brand outlets.
Standalone synergy-related machine under installation, expected to deliver full impact in Q3.
Operating units reduced from 21 to 12 as part of Kurlon integration.
demand_pricing: Standalone India volume growth about 6%; management views sub-10% as satisfactory and says industry grew close to 5%.
U2O price increase taken last year to fix channel margins; value growth well ahead of volume as a result; management says the pricing level is now sustainable.
Raw material (TDI/polyol) prices swung roughly +40% to -20% in the period; prices spiked in March after the Feb 28 Iran conflict, eased in April, then rose again about a month before the call.
Management says price increases pass through commensurately, but in-pipe inventory on the high seas can lag on sharp falls and hit margin.
Foam share of COGS: TDI and polyol are 65-70% of COGS.
Premiumisation: ASP marginally up across segments; new products introduced to lift ASP; consumer-led promotions launched.
Organised mattress market combined share of Sleepwell and Kurlon close to 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Australia/Spain margin gain sustainable, and how much of it is inventory benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gains came from longer-held low-cost inventory and yield and supply chain programmes. Overseas momentum should moderate as India recovers, with normal inventory levels by Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone volume growth slow to single digits and margins fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a price-volume trade-off after the steep price hikes, and expects double-digit volume growth for the year once volatility eases. Gross margins were hit mainly by foam, while incremental foam sales generated cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 15% EBITDA margin target and 13-14% FY28 guidance hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not guided for 13% for FY27 (only 11-12%) but stands by its margin commitment; the current volatility makes it hard to comment, and gross margin has fallen more than the guided range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and rollout of company-owned stores?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR27 lakh capex plus INR20-22 lakh working capital per store, with 42 operational of a 50-store target; about INR25 crore for another 50 COCO stores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kurlon integration status and synergy realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Integration about 96-97% complete, operating units cut to 12 from 21, and roughly 75-80% of synergies realised, with the remainder on track.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Furlenco store rollout?
qa_highlights.answer: Furlenco is present in 40-50 shop-in-shop stores with a first target of 100, and will go only where it fits its micro-market strategy.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility: TDI/polyol (65-70% of COGS) swung roughly +40% to -20%; management expects volatility for at least a couple of months, possibly to October-November, so gross margin recovery timing is uncertain.

Margin target credibility: management reiterated 15% EBITDA margin for next year but declined to comment on the 12-13% FY27 and 13-14% FY28 figures put to it, saying volatility makes it hard to judge; gross margin fell more than the guided range.

Overseas margin sustainability: Australia and Spain margins (12.8% and 14.7%) were helped by longer-held low-cost inventory and lower frequency of price changes; management expects moderation as India recovers and inventory normalises by Q2.

Volume recovery: standalone India volume grew about 6% against double-digit growth last year; management expects double-digit volume growth for FY27 and strongest volumes in Q3 and Q4, contingent on volatility subsiding.

Synergy and capex execution: about INR40 crore synergy pending the machine installation (full impact expected Q3); COCO rollout of 50 stores at about INR50 lakh each (~INR25 crore) and Furlenco shop-in-shop target of 100 stores from about 40-50.

Balance sheet: India debt above INR300 crore to be cleared in about one year; overseas debt of about INR350 crore over five years; company will not be debt free by year-end despite INR150-200 crore cash generation.
key_quotes: For the first time in the group's history, Sheela Foam has reported a consolidated revenues of more than INR1,000 crores and EBITDA of more than INR100 crores in the first quarter of any fiscal year.
So, we guided for 11% to 12%. We never guided for 13% for the current year. Yes, we do stand for it.
There is no change in stand on the margins. We have a target of 15% EBITDA margin for the next year.
So, there would definitely be volume recovery. I would say we would go back higher than what the volumes we clocked last year.
540203|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on the quarter, the Kurlon integration and the medium-term targets, but cautious and non-committal on near-term margins, which it attributed to raw-material volatility. It declined to give a view on the 12-13% FY27 and 13-14% FY28 margin figures put to it and repeatedly said it would revisit once volatility eases.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: H2 FY27 (Q3 festive recovery), with 15% margin target 'next
rows.why: Consolidated margin rose 139 bps to 10.6%, but standalone gross margin fell on TDI/polyol swings of +40% to -20%, management declined to back 11-12% FY27 or 13-14% FY28 figures, and reiterated 15% target only for next year; overseas margins (12.8% Australia, 14.7% Spain) flatter the group and are expected to moderate as inventory normalises by Q2.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Synergy machine under installation with full impact expected Q3, and COCO rollout of 50 stores (42 operational target) at about INR25 crore capex; capacity adds are guided with a plan but are small (no capacity utilisation or tonnage numbers given).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone India volume grew about 6% in Q1 (mattress volume +6%, foam +4%, U2O volume +19%, e-commerce category volume +23%), and management guides double-digit volume growth for both foam and mattresses for FY27 with Q3 and Q4 strongest, though this is contingent on volatility easing.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held rather than raised guidance, and volume growth of 6% against a double-digit target and sub-target margin trajectory argue against an upgrade near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gross margin has fallen more than the guided range, management expects raw-material volatility until about October-November, and standalone volume growth slowed to about 6% versus its double-digit FY27 target.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management says new products are being introduced to lift ASP and consumer-led promotions have launched, but no specific product launch dates or counts were given.

rows.label: Overseas revenue above INR1,000 crore and EBITDA about INR120 crore in FY27
rows.why: Management says it is 'very confident' of crossing INR1,000 crore revenue and about INR120 crore EBITDA, against Q1 Australia INR120 crore (+31%) and Spain INR133 crore (+54%), though inventory-driven margin gains may moderate.

rows.label: Kurlon synergies: about INR40 crore pending, 75-80% realised
rows.why: Integration 96-97% complete, operating units cut from 21 to 12, and the remaining ~INR40 crore synergy depends on the machine installation with full impact expected in Q3.

rows.label: India debt above INR300 crore cleared in about one year
rows.why: Management guided to clear India debt within about a year from INR150-200 crore cash generation, though the company will not be debt free by year-end and overseas debt of about INR350 crore runs over five years.

tone.note: Management was confident on the quarter, Kurlon integration and overseas targets but cautious and non-committal on near-term margins, attributing them to raw-material volatility; analysts pressed on the 12-13% FY27 and 13-14% FY28 margin figures and management declined to endorse them.

540205|2026-03.headline: Aditya Vision Q4 FY26 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR625 crore and PAT 36% to INR22 crore, despite a weak summer and FY26 PAT up only 11%.
540205|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 18% to INR2,672 crore and PAT grew 11% to INR117 crore, with EBITDA at INR228 crore (8.5% margin) and gross margin at 15.6%. Q4 was the strongest quarter, with revenue up 28% and same-store sales growth of 18%, though gross margin (16%) and EBITDA margin (8.1%) were lower than the prior year. Management said H2 is now as important as H1, reflecting a shift away from a seasonal model. Store count reached 207 across four states, with Chhattisgarh entered and Madhya Pradesh planned this year. Inventory was built up to about INR840 crore ahead of anticipated OEM supply constraints and BEE-driven price increases.

segments.name: Bihar
segments.commentary: Largest market at 74% of Q4 FY26 revenue and 75% of FY26 revenue; 118 stores across 38 districts.

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh
segments.commentary: 14% of Q4 and 13% of FY26 revenue; 53 stores covering 30 of 75 districts, with most new stores opened in Feb-Mar 2026 and contributing less than a full year.

segments.name: Jharkhand
segments.commentary: 12% of both Q4 and FY26 revenue; 33 stores covering 22 of 24 districts.

segments.name: Chhattisgarh
segments.commentary: Entered early with 3 stores covering 2 of 33 districts; no revenue split disclosed.

segments.name: Product categories
segments.commentary: Mobiles and laptops together exceed 25% of sales; ASP of mobiles rose about 20% in Q4, diluting gross margin. Small appliances grew about 50%, per analyst; cooling products (ACs, coolers, refrigerators) underperformed due to weak summer.

guidance_outlook: Management gives no formal store guidance; it cites about 25 stores when asked, and has added over 30 stores a year for the last 3-5 years.
Madhya Pradesh entry is on track for this financial year; Chhattisgarh and UP to be scaled up.
Management expects opex to grow in line with overall expenses rather than rise faster, as the store base becomes more mature.
Management cites an 8% to 10% EBITDA margin range as its endeavour, with 9% as a central target, but declined to give a timeline.
April 2026 described as very robust; May started colder but is expected to normalise into a normal summer.
No equity raise planned this financial year; internal accruals and working capital borrowings are expected to suffice.
capex_capacity: Store base reached 207 at March 31, 2026, after 102 stores were added in the last three years versus 105 in the prior 23-24 years.
Stores take 9 to 12 months to break even, per management.
Inventory of about INR840 crore held at end Q4 FY26, built ahead of OEM supply uncertainty (gas shortages linked to a Gulf conflict) and BEE-driven price increases of about 8% to 10%.
Plans to scale UP and Chhattisgarh while deepening Bihar and Jharkhand; a neighbouring state, previously held back by political uncertainty, is now being considered.
demand_pricing: Weak summer and extended rains hit H1; Q1 FY26 revenue grew 6% and H1 grew 11%. Q3 grew 28%, driven by festive demand.
Historically Q1 and Q2 contributed 55% to 60% of annual sales; management says this is now shifting towards a more balanced full-year model.
Price increases on mobiles and laptops lowered the margin mix; management said price hikes are not the main driver of profitability.
Management said OEMs bear the burden of unsold inventory and do not take returns; they help liquidate stock before new billing.
Real estate slowdown seen in Pune, Bengaluru and Hyderabad has not yet affected Bihar, UP or Jharkhand, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will high inventory give a competitive and margin advantage over peers in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on peers' inventory and said it holds inventory as per its own strategy and historical levels, not to profit from price hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall about 100 bps YoY in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to weak cooling-product sales in H1 and a Q4 surge in low-margin mobiles (ASP up about 20%) and laptops (ASP up 8-10%), which together exceed 25% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 50% rise in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to brand ambassador onboarding, UP expansion, and variable costs such as freight, card commissions and dealer discounts that rise with the 18% volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: What are the normalised margins for mature Bihar, and when will UP match them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose state-wise margins, saying it aims to bring other states up to Bihar's level over time without sacrificing sales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the store expansion target for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance given; management cited 25 stores when pressed and said it expects to keep beating its informal targets.

qa_highlights.question: When will EBITDA margin return to about 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no timeline and pointed to an 8% to 10% margin range, with 9% as the central target, while not compromising sales growth.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from mix shift toward mobiles and laptops, whose ASPs are rising.
Q4 inventory build (about INR840 crore) exposes the company to price-cut and demand risk if the summer underperforms; May started colder than normal.
Cash conversion: management declined to guide on OCF/EBITDA, saying it depends on inventory and working capital.
Finance cost implies about 12.8-13% on average debt per analyst, but this includes lease liability interest; the bank borrowing rate was not disclosed.
Most UP stores opened in the last months of FY26, so UP contribution and unit economics are not yet visible on a full-year basis.
Opex rising faster than revenue in new geographies (UP, Chhattisgarh, MP) could weigh on EBITDA margins.

540212|2026-03.headline: TCI Express Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6% YoY to INR 327 crore, EBITDA margin 11.3%, PAT flat at INR 21 crore amid fuel and labour cost pressure.
540212|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew about 6% YoY to INR 327 crore and 4% QoQ, with total income of INR 331 crore. EBITDA rose 11% YoY to INR 37 crore (11.3% margin) while PAT was flat at INR 21 crore (6.3% margin). Full-year revenue grew about 2% to INR 1,236 crore, with PAT of INR 90 crore (7.2% margin). Management said the Gulf conflict pushed ATF prices up sharply and labour costs rose, and volume growth slowed to 4% YoY in Q4 after March.

segments.name: Surface Express
segments.commentary: Largest contributor; management said surface margin should improve with diesel-linked price pass-through, citing about 30% arbitrage. Surface grew in single digits in the last two quarters, with mid-single-digit to ~10% growth expected going forward.

segments.name: Multimodal (Air, Rail, C2C, e-commerce)
segments.commentary: About 18.5% of FY26 revenue, with management citing about 20% growth; target of 22% to 25% share over 2 to 3 years. Domestic and international air margins were hit this quarter, while rail and C2C margins were described as stable.

segments.name: Rail Express
segments.commentary: Management said rail gross profit is above 30% and realisation is about 2.5x surface. Rail volumes are not disclosed.

segments.name: E-commerce Express
segments.commentary: About 2.5% of business, with a target of 5%. Focus is on D2C and B2B merchant-to-warehouse movement with SME clients, not quick commerce.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at about 10% to 11%, with revenue growth of about 15% including price hikes.
FY27 margin improvement of 100 to 150 basis points at EBITDA and PAT levels, conditional on fuel prices stabilising.
Q1 FY27 volume expected at high single-digit growth, improving QoQ through the year.
Multimodal growth guided at about 20% in FY27.
Depreciation run-rate of INR 30 to 32 crore per year after ROU additions; about INR 6 to 6.25 crore per quarter.
Capex plan revised from INR 500 crore to INR 400 crore for FY23 to FY27; about INR 130 crore planned for FY27. A new five-year plan will follow.
Branch expansion of about 100 branches in FY27 (40 surface, 60 rail, air and C2C).
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation was about 83.25% in Q4, improved QoQ.
Nagpur sorting centre upgraded and now owned; semi-automated, about 70,000 to 75,000 sq ft, with only 5% to 7% change in cut-off time.
Ahmedabad and Kolkata sorting centres under construction, to finish in FY27, with automation ramping up in the first half of FY28. Lucknow also in progress.
Mumbai and Kolkata sorting centres moved to 5-year leases, which added ROU assets and raised depreciation.
Next sorting centres planned for Chennai and Bangalore.
demand_pricing: Management said diesel rose about INR 8 and the company is passing it on to customers, with 85% pass-through expected and 10% to 15% of customers still negotiating.
Air fuel (ATF) rose about 50% and international air rates went up 2x to 3x after the Gulf conflict began at end-February, leading customers to hold shipments in March.
Labour costs rose 15% to 20%, adding about 100 basis points to overall cost, per management.
SME share of revenue was 48% to 52% against a historical 50:50 split; management expects a return to 50%+ with the last two months' results described as good.
Revenue per kg is about INR 12.3 to 12.4 with EBITDA of about INR 1.25 to 1.27 per kg, against a historical INR 1.8 to 2.0 per kg, per an analyst's calculation.
The company expects to benefit from air-to-surface and rail shifts as higher air prices push customers to other modes.

qa_highlights.question: Why has growth been restricted and margins fallen from 15% to 16% to 10% to 11%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the Gulf war and ATF spike, airline consolidation, airport privatisation, lower truck utilisation and a 100 bps hit from labour costs. It guided FY27 PAT margin recovery of 100 to 150 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and revenue guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of about 10% to 11% and revenue growth of about 15% for FY27, with Q1 at high single digits and QoQ improvement after that.

qa_highlights.question: Is the multimodal segment margin dilutive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said air margins were temporarily hit by costs. Rail and C2C margins are stable and surface margin should improve with diesel pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the depreciation and interest increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Two sorting centres were moved to 5-year leases under Ind AS 116, which lifted ROU assets. Management said depreciation runs at about INR 6 to 6.25 crore per quarter. Pre-Ind AS EBITDA would have been about INR 29 crore, versus INR 32 crore reported, per the analyst's calculation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the e-commerce strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce is about 2.5% of business, targeted to 5%, through D2C and B2B merchant-to-warehouse flows with SMEs and some aggregator platforms. Quick commerce is not in the strategy.

Labour cost inflation from minimum wage and social security norms, plus state-level pressure.
Rupee weakness raising input costs.
SME stress and the share of SME revenue, which fell to 48% to 52%.
Management has not disclosed non-surface volumes, which limits visibility on the rail and air business.

540212|2026-06.headline: TCI Express Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to INR 312 crore, with PAT up 6% to INR 22.4 crore and volumes up 7.5% to 2.5 lakh tonnes.
540212|2026-06.overview: Income from operations grew about 9% YoY to INR 312 crore and EBITDA rose 11% to INR 37 crore, with margin at 11.7% versus 11.5%. PAT rose 6% to INR 22.4 crore (7.1% margin). Management said the fuel price hike taken in mid-May was only partly reflected in Q1 (June only), so benefits should show from Q2. The company stated it is debt-free with net cash of about INR 118 crore.

financial_highlights.change: up ~6% YoY from INR 21 crore; margin 7.1%

segments.name: Surface Express
segments.commentary: Largest contributor; grew 9% YoY on existing customers, new accounts and industrial growth. Management targets accelerating to double-digit growth.

segments.name: Domestic Air Express
segments.commentary: Grew 29% YoY per opening remarks (CEO-level figure); later cited ~28% on enterprise account wins and airline partnerships.

segments.name: International Express
segments.commentary: Grew 27% YoY on new customers, win-backs and expanded global carrier partnerships.

segments.name: E-commerce Express
segments.commentary: Grew 63% YoY, the fastest-growing vertical, but only ~2-2.5% of revenue; target small-merchant, D2C and e-commerce B2B segments at 16-18% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Rail Express / C2C Express
segments.commentary: Rail added operational branches; C2C added clients, regional branch coverage and a larger dedicated vehicle fleet. No growth figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at 11-12%, with net price realisation of about 3%, implying 13-15% overall revenue growth.
FY27 PAT growth guided at 20-25%.
EBITDA margin expansion of 100-150 bps targeted for FY27; margin benefit from fuel pass-through expected from Q2.
Multimodal share of revenue targeted at 17-18% to 19% in FY27 and 22-25% by 2030.
FY27 capex guided at INR 125-140 crore; management said it expects to cross INR 125 crore, with about INR 20 crore spent so far.
Kolkata hub automation expected by March 2027 or June 2027 at latest; Ahmedabad around mid-2027, taking automated hubs to four by 2027.

Ongoing construction at four sites: Ahmedabad, Kolkata, corporate office and Lucknow.
Management said it is close to finalising a land purchase in one of Mumbai, Chennai or Bangalore.
Regional branch expansion ongoing across Surface, Air, Rail and C2C; e-commerce regional branches being opened and bikers hired for sub-5 kg deliveries.
demand_pricing: Volume grew ~7.5% to 2.5 lakh tonnes, but management said price hikes were held back until fuel increased in mid-May; diesel and annual hikes together gave a 'handsome' increase, with ~90%+ of customers passed through in June.
Analyst noted peers are taking 3-5% price hikes; management did not give a specific Q1 price-hike percentage.
SME to B2B mix returned to 50:50 in Q1 from 48:52 in FY26.
Management cited pipeline visibility, manufacturing demand and SME recovery; growth expected from both existing customers and new industries.
Analyst raised competitive pricing in certain segments and elevated operating costs industry-wide; management said its service quality and tech investment keep it ahead.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Q1 volumes and price hikes versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume was 2.5 lakh tonnes, up ~7.5%. Management said fuel-linked pass-through came in mid-May, with the full price increase reflected mainly in June; the company deferred hikes ahead of expected fuel increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategic rationale for expanding e-commerce given lower margins historically?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce is ~2-2.5% of revenue. Management said D2C margins are 16-18% and it is targeting small merchants, D2C and e-commerce B2B, with regional teams and branches to support Surface.

qa_highlights.question: What changed to drive consistent double-digit EBITDA growth and volume acceleration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it strengthened vertical-wise regional teams and built regional structures across Air, International, Rail and C2C. Air grew ~28% on new customers, and a clear pipeline supports growth.

qa_highlights.question: What are the volume, pricing and PAT targets for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of 11-12%, net price hikes of about 3%, total growth of 13-15%, and PAT growth of 20-25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of hub automation and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Two hubs are automated (Tajnagar, Chakan); Kolkata is expected by March or June 2027 and Ahmedabad around mid-2027. FY27 capex is INR 125-140 crore, with about INR 20 crore spent so far.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins improve in Q2 as fuel pass-through takes full effect, and what is the multimodal share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the fuel increase was passed on to 90%+ of customers in June, so margins should improve from Q2. Multimodal share is about 17-18% now, targeted at 17-19% this year and 22-25% by 2030.

540222|2026-03.headline: Laurus FY26 revenue rose 23% to INR6,813 crore and EBITDA margin hit 26.8%, with Q4 margin at 28.9%; FY27 capex guided to about INR3,000 crore over two years.
540222|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a strong year: revenue of INR6,813 crore (+23%), gross margin about 60.4%, EBITDA of INR1,826 crore (26.8% margin, +6.7 pp) and PAT of INR889 crore (+148%). Q4 revenue grew only 5% YoY to INR1,812 crore, but Q4 EBITDA margin reached 28.9% on operating leverage and better mix. CDMO grew about 38% in small molecules to INR1,896 crore, while Affordable Medicines (formerly Generics) grew 18% to INR4,733 crore. Management raised its multi-year capex expectation sharply, to around INR3,000 crore over the next two years from the earlier INR1,000 crore a year reference, and the call stressed CDMO share rising to 50% by FY30.

segments.name: Small molecule CDMO
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR1,896 crore (+38%); Q4 sales about INR524 crore. Growth came from late-stage programs, commercial NCE API supplies and ramp-up of growth projects.

segments.name: Total CDMO (incl. Bio)
segments.commentary: Full-year CDMO business a little over INR2,000 crore (INR2,080 crore), above 30% of revenue versus 13% six years ago.

segments.name: Laurus Bio
segments.commentary: Q4 sales about INR65 crore (+124% YoY on a low base); FY26 sales up about 15%. Phase 1 fermentation capacity at Vizag due by end-2026.

segments.name: Affordable Medicines (formerly Generics)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,223 crore with growth moderating; FY26 revenue INR4,733 crore (+18%), driven by ARV and oncology volumes and developed-market launches.

segments.name: ARV
segments.commentary: FY26 ARV revenue about INR2,800 crore, versus the INR2,500 crore plus or minus 200 crore run-rate previously cited; ARV now 41% of revenue, down from 67% six years ago. Mix is about two-thirds API and one-third formulations.

guidance_outlook: Capex guidance raised to about INR3,000 crore over the next two years, from the INR1,000 crore a year reference; one analyst's question cited INR1,500 crore a year.
Gross debt may rise slightly in FY27, but debt/EBITDA is expected to hold at or soften from 1.25x.
Effective tax rate around 25-26%; standalone at 25%.

R&D spend to stay around 4.1% of sales in FY27.

Laurus Bio fermentation greenfield at Vizag: Phase 1 operational by end-2026. Bangalore R2 is fully occupied (4 x 45,000 litre fermenters); 250,000 litres now, another 400,000 litres by year-end, with room for 600,000 more.
KRKA JV formulation facility in Hyderabad: Phase 1 by mid-2027.
Formulation capacity up 20% to 12 billion units in FY26; a new tertiary packaging/formulation facility is due in June for an existing 3-billion-tablet CMO partner.
Company exceeded 8,200 cubic metres of small-molecule reactor volume in FY26. Asset turnover 0.89x.
demand_pricing: ARV pricing was broadly constant in FY26; higher ARV sales were driven by full utilisation of ARV assets.
Gross margin gain was attributed to softer raw-material prices and process improvements, with better product mix.
Q4 saw some solvent price pressure, but management said production is not affected and it expects no disruption through June; some pressure expected, offset by higher utilisation.
Management said the three recent commercial APIs have multi-year patent life and partner forecasts, and it sees no destocking risk; it also said there is no single-product concentration.
Geopolitical disruption may pressure raw-material availability, logistics and OTIF performance across the industry.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said three commercial APIs delivered in the last 18 months have multi-year patent life and clear partner forecasts; no destocking seen and no single-product dependence.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating leverage drive margins beyond gross margin gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects operating leverage next year as capacity utilisation rises; Q4 EBITDA margin was near 29% and rose through each quarter of FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Vizag fermentation: yield variability and ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial Vizag batches are industrial chemicals, surfactants and polymers (non-pharma); contamination is the main risk, and products are moving from 45 KL to 110 KL fermenters after commercial gates were cleared.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ARV API/formulation split and non-ARV formulation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About two-thirds API and one-third formulations for FY26 overall; non-ARV formulations are growing with momentum expected into FY27 from existing products.

qa_highlights.question: Will ARV share fall, and what is the CDMO target?
qa_highlights.answer: ARV stays around INR2,800 crore in absolute terms but its share falls; CDMO is targeted at 50% of sales by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Why was capex raised, and what are return expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says capex is growth-led with visibility on customer and product, and expects about INR3,000 crore over two years.

Solvent and raw-material price pressure and geopolitical supply risk; management expects some pressure but claims stable margins.

CDMO lumpiness quarter to quarter; a peer with destocking challenges was cited.

540222|2026-06.headline: Laurus Labs Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29% to INR2,026 crores, with EBITDA margin at 31.8% and CDMO up 69% to INR835 crores.
540222|2026-06.overview: Revenue of INR2,026 crores grew 29% YoY, led by commercial supplies in CDMO and continued strength in Affordable Medicines. Gross margin was about 62.7% and EBITDA of INR644 crores at a 31.8% margin, up about 7 percentage points QoQ, as management attributed the gain to operating leverage and product mix. Profit after tax was about INR368 crores and ROCE about 19% versus 17.7% a year earlier. Management raised the FY27 capex guidance to about INR2,000 crores from INR1,500 crores, and net debt rose to INR2,656 crores with debt-to-EBITDA at 1.28x.

540293|2026-03.headline: Pricol Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,000 crore at INR 1,077.9 crore, EBITDA margin 13.29%, but management guides to near-term earnings softening from geopolitical and input-cost headwinds.
540293|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was INR 1,077.9 crore with EBITDA of INR 143.28 crore (13.29% margin) and PAT of INR 73.23 crore (6.79% margin). For FY26, revenue was just under INR 4,000 crore (up 51.24%), EBITDA INR 492.91 crore (12.44% margin) and PAT INR 250.80 crore. Management said West Asia-related input cost spikes (polymers, aluminium, semiconductors, freight, rupee) will soften earnings, with cost recovery from OEMs still under negotiation. It is holding capex, R&D and dividend at prior levels, and plans INR 680-700 crore capex this year.

540293|2026-06.headline: Pricol Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 23.5% YoY to Rs 1,083.6 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.41% on West Asia-driven cost headwinds.
540293|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was about Rs 1,083.58 crore, up 23.46% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs 123.69 crore (11.41% margin) and PAT of Rs 67.02 crore (6.19% margin). Management said EBITDA grew only about 21% YoY because of polymer, LPG, freight, rupee and minimum-wage cost increases, which it expects to recover through quarterly and half-yearly indexation over Q2 and Q3. The call also covered a proposed demerger of the DIS/DICVS business from the ACFMS and polymer businesses, a Rs 700 crore capex cycle, and a one-year pause on M&A.

segments.name: DIS / DICVS (driver information systems, two-wheeler, CV, PV)
segments.commentary: Growth about 25% YoY in Q1 per CEO, equal to ACFMS. Two-wheeler revenue grew 28% vs industry 23%. Targets growth at least 5% above market; two-wheeler DIS volume share 30-35%, CV share about two-thirds, PV share 8-9% (Tata Motors dependent).

segments.name: ACFMS (auto components, fluid management and switches)
segments.commentary: Growth about 25% YoY in Q1 per CEO. Target is 10% growth above market; first switches business won from Suzuki; disc brake production started for a major Indian OEM, with meaningful revenue from FY28.

segments.name: Polymer (plastics)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs 249 crore at 7.8% EBITDA margin; most affected by polymer and LPG price spikes. Capacity about Rs 1,000 crore turnover today, targeted at about Rs 2,000 crore post capex; management targets 2.5x FY25 base, and sees ROCE muted during capex cycle before 16-18% steady state.

guidance_outlook: Q2 and Q3 FY27 expected to recover delayed earnings via indexation: about 75% of revenue indexed from Q2, balance from Q3 (half-yearly indexation).
EBITDA expected under pressure for next couple of quarters until West Asia-related costs normalise; management said Q1 costs were delayed, not lost.
Minimum wage increases in three states add about Rs 21 crore per annum; customer pass-through still under negotiation.
Steady-state blended EBITDA margin target 12.5-13%; management estimates about 1.5% EBITDA lost in Q1 and about another half of that still recoverable via price increases and indexation.
FY30 (CY30/FY31) revenue ambition of Rs 8,000 crore for DICVS retained; FY30 targets unchanged despite M&A pause.
Demerger expected to take at least 4 quarters, management hopes for 12 months; businesses to operate as separate entities from October and fully by December.
Disc brake and switches revenue to become meaningful only from FY28.
capex_capacity: Rs 700 crore capex cycle over 18-24 months: about Rs 400 crore for polymer (including relocating out of TVS campuses under lock-in), Rs 150-180 crore for DICVS, about Rs 120 crore for ACFMS.
Five new factories being brought on stream: Hosur (state-of-the-art), Mysore, Aurangabad (greenfield), Sanand Gujarat (for Honda), and Bhiwadi/NCR under construction.
Polymer Centre of Excellence to be fully operational by May 2027; in-house tool room being built.
Partnership with BOE for backlight modules for screens in progress.
Polymer capacity expected to support about Rs 2,000 crore turnover from about Rs 1,000 crore today; plants on schedule barring a month or two of delay.
demand_pricing: Industry growth in Q1 about 22-23% weighted average; company grew about 26% overall, outperforming by about 4 points.
Q1 sequentially flat versus Q4, which management said is seasonal; no share loss claimed.
Raw material costs rising sharply for memory-controlled devices due to AI-driven demand; polymer, LPG, crude, freight and rupee all adverse.
Two-wheeler TFT penetration about 7-8% of two-wheelers produced; management expects this to double in 2-3 years.
Polymer customer wins include Ather, River, Simple Energy, Raptee, Honda, Royal Enfield, Suzuki (switches) and Yamaha (final stage); Mahindra engagement started for PV and DICVS.
E-cockpit: proof of concept shown to customers; global competitors have volume advantage of 40-50x, so cost competitiveness limited.

qa_highlights.question: Why demerge the DIS/connected vehicles business from the rest of the group?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the board debated it for over two years; the DIS business needs large investment and technology partners, which investors find hard to back inside a multi-business company. Demerger is intended to allow a debt and equity mix and partner onboarding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 margin outlook and steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady-state blended EBITDA margin of 12.5-13% is the target; Q1 lost about 1.5% of margin; Q2 and Q3 expected to recover through indexation, with about half of the lost margin still recoverable if prices hold.

qa_highlights.question: Capex split and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 700 crore over 18-24 months: Rs 400 crore polymer, Rs 150-180 crore DICVS, about Rs 120 crore ACFMS.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: At least 4 quarters per advisers; management hopes for 12 months. Internal operation as separate entities from October, fully by December.

qa_highlights.question: Is M&A still on the cards?
qa_highlights.answer: M&A paused for about one year after due diligence found asset quality issues; FY30 targets unchanged. Will consider only attractive quality assets.

qa_highlights.question: Disc brake revenue and ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: No material revenue yet; meaningful revenue expected only from FY28, consistent with prior guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Polymer business performance in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue Rs 249 crore with EBITDA margin of 7.8%; polymer and LPG cost spikes expected to correct in Q2 and Q3.

risks_watch: Rupee at record lows against the US dollar; management flagged a possible move toward three digits per dollar, which would keep imported electronic component costs elevated.

Recovery depends on indexation: about 75% of revenue indexed from Q2 and the balance from Q3, with about half of the lost ~1.5% margin still recoverable only if prices hold. Minimum wage cost of ~Rs 21 crore per annum is still under customer negotiation.
West Asia conflict effects: crude could return to the $90s, LPG, polymer, freight (expected high for at least four quarters) and AI-driven memory chip costs all rising.

540358|2026-03.headline: RMC Switchgears FY26 consolidated revenue rose 26.4% to Rs 401.59 crore, but profit fell short, with Q4 back to Rs 9.3 crore net profit after a Q3 loss of Rs 7.07 crore.

Consolidated revenue grew 26.4% to Rs 401.59 crore, but margins were hit by PulseBox product development spend, rain-delayed execution in Maharashtra, and solar EPC cost pressure from China-linked supply, safeguard duty and aluminium/silver prices. Q4 returned to profit (Rs 9.3 crore) from a Rs 7.07 crore loss in Q3, which management attributed to execution catch-up and better material availability. Receivables rose from Rs 148 crore to Rs 205 crore and operating cash flow turned negative; management attributed this mainly to March-concentrated billing. No FY27 revenue or profit guidance was given; management said the unexecuted order book is about Rs 850 crore plus and the tender pipeline about Rs 1,500 crore plus.

540376|2026-06.headline: DMart FY26 revenue near INR67,000 crore (+16%), PAT margin ~4.8%; management targets ~15% annual store additions and says SSSG stays at last year's levels.
540376|2026-06.overview: This was DMart's annual analyst call, the first with Anshul Asawa as MD & CEO, covering FY26 results and the outlook for FY27. Management said the fundamentals were intact but flagged higher staff costs for capability build, a slowdown in same-store growth in mature metro stores, and heavy competitive pressure from quick commerce. Avenue E-commerce (DMart Ready) was narrowed to 11 cities after exits from seven cities, with its EBITDA falling about 43% and a net loss of INR307 crore. Management reiterated a roughly 15% internal store-addition target and did not disclose e-commerce KPIs.

financial_highlights.change: Roughly flat; gross margin +16 bps, employee cost +27 bps, other expenses -9 bps
Total debt incl. AS 116 INR2,267 crore
Retail business area ~20.6 million sq ft
Sales +17%; PBT -24%; net loss INR307 crore

segments.name: Avenue Supermarts (standalone DMart stores)
segments.commentary: Sales +~16% with gross margin up 16 bps to within the 14-15% range; employee cost up ~33% in standalone financials including wage code impact. Entered five new states in FY26.

segments.name: Avenue E-commerce (DMart Ready)
segments.commentary: Sales +17% but EBITDA down ~43% and net loss INR307 crore. Exited seven quick-commerce cities; now focused on 11 cities, with 165 pickup points cited. Contract labour cost +24% and transport +34%.

segments.name: Align Retail (grocery packing)
segments.commentary: Sales +~16.5% and PAT +~24%.

segments.name: Avenue Food Plaza (fast/ready food)
segments.commentary: Sales +~35.5%; returned to profit with PAT margin ~9% after prior-year losses from expansion.

guidance_outlook: Internal store-addition benchmark ~15% of store base annually; could run a few points higher or lower depending on real estate timing.
Same-store growth expected to hover around last financial year's level (~7.5-8%) for FY27 for older stores; no sharp increase expected, all else equal.
Long-term North Star: ~15% gross margin and ~5% net margin; no intention to expand margin at the cost of customer proposition.
Expect efficiency gains in AEL from consolidation to 11 cities in FY27 onwards, per AEL CEO.
Staff cost built ahead of volume growth; management says it is hard to say if the build-up has ended.
Plans to invest in ERP and wider technology upgrades; management expects only marginal near-term margin impact.
capex_capacity: FY26 store additions: 85, with 15 on long-term lease; 68 stores in total now on lease out of 500+.
Land-to-store conversion takes 2-3 years depending on store configuration; pipeline of projects covers the next 2-3 years.
Debt: CP outstanding ~INR800 crore; INR1,000 crore NCD approved, may take total borrowing to ~INR2,000 crore by year-end, mainly to fund capex and reduce cost of debt.
Warehouses added in FY26 raised inventory days to 33.2.
demand_pricing: Quick commerce competition intensifying in dense metros (Mumbai, Bangalore, Hyderabad) where mature stores are saturated; management cites capacity, saturation, high throughput and competition as reasons for slower metro SSSG.
Management says FMCG vendors are not shifting attention away from DMart; many are doubling down.
Management says monthly/bulk shopping in metros is stable and strong, with good traction in Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities; newer Tier 2/3 stores are doing better than older metro stores.
Pricing follows vendor pass-through; no pricing guidance given.
Quarterly growth was 13% (Dec-25 quarter, deflation in staples), 19% (Mar-26 quarter, panic buying), and 15% (Jun-26 quarter).

qa_highlights.question: Will SSSG recover to double-digit levels given quick-commerce and maturity pressures in metros?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SSSG is likely to hover around the current range (~7-8%) and not rise considerably, especially for older stores; new stores are opened nearby to reduce pressure on existing stores.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 15% store-addition target conservative and can it go to 100-150 stores a year?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal target is ~15%; capital and people are not constraints, and land acquisition, permissions and build time (2-3 years) are. Management said 100-150 stores is not a reasonable number at about 500 stores currently.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economics of leasing versus owning stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share lease vs owned economics; said both models work. 68 stores are on long leases and 15 of the 85 stores added in FY26 were leased. Niladri said PBT is a fair measure of lease impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the mix of AEL get cut to 11 cities and why not experiment with faster delivery?
qa_highlights.answer: Seven cities were exited because their contribution was minimal. Management said it will not pursue immediate delivery; it will prove the six-hour slotted model in 11 cities first because losses had grown with expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in employee costs and why are contractual headcounts lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Permanent headcount rose ~4,000 (75-80% of additions are store-management cohorts). Frontline staff are non-permanent; productivity and mechanisation held down non-permanent headcount. Wage code from December 2025 also added costs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add non-metro growth via quick commerce given Flipkart and Blinkit expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not see a risk of LFL falling below 5%; it sees organised retail still under-penetrated in smaller towns and has no point of view on QC adoption outside top cities.

risks_watch: Continued SSSG slowdown in mature metro stores (~7-8% range expected) as quick commerce and new nearby stores take share.
AEL profitability: EBITDA down ~43% with net loss INR307 crore; watch whether consolidation to 11 cities improves throughput and transport/labour costs in FY27.
Rising staff costs (employee cost +27 bps of sales, standalone employee expense up ~33%) with wage code impact and capability build.
Lower return ratios (ROE ~13.5%, ROCE ~17.1%) and rising debt to fund expansion; NCD plan of INR1,000 crore.
Store-addition pace (85 in FY26 vs ~15% target) depends on land and lease availability; slower ramp in new Tier 2/3 stores.
Management declined to disclose DMart Ready KPIs, store-level margins, lease economics, land value, and category-level data.

540401|2026-06.headline: Maximus Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 52% YoY to INR59.91 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.64% from 9.81% on Middle East war input costs.
540401|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR59.91 crores versus INR39.52 crores a year earlier, with EBITDA up about 18% to INR4.58 crores. Margin compression, attributed to higher input and freight costs from the ongoing Middle East war, and higher finance costs (INR1.53 crores vs INR0.92 crores) left PAT at INR2.05 crores versus INR2.33 crores a year ago. Management highlighted the proposed associate acquisition of Quebec Petroleum (40% stake), a Kenya grease plant planned for Q3 FY27, and a Tanzania warehousing expansion. Management guided to crossing about INR200 crores revenue in FY27 on a conservative basis.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Highest EBITDA margin among the three verticals (manufacturing, toll blending, trading) in Q1 FY27 and historically. Operations in UAE and Kenya.

segments.name: Toll blending
segments.commentary: Management says it is being pursued aggressively; in talks with an East African MNC for toll blending.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Lowest-margin vertical per management. Long-term target split: manufacturing plus toll blending 75-80%, trading 20-25%.

segments.name: Specialty lubricants
segments.commentary: Contribute around 40% of topline, per CFO.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected to cross about INR200 crores on a conservative basis, with healthy EBITDA margins (stated even under the ongoing war scenario).
Margins expected to hold at current levels or improve over the next couple of quarters if supply disruption persists, through product mix diversification.
Kenya grease manufacturing facility planned for commissioning in Q3 FY27.
Tanzania expansion: initially warehousing and distribution, moving to manufacturing once scale is reached.
Recently launched modernisation programme: automated batch blending, additional storage and warehousing, improved filling lines, and capacity expansion at UAE and Kenya plants.
Capacity considered sufficient for next 2-3 years on single-shift basis; additional storage capex needed for full utilisation.
capex_capacity: Combined manufacturing capacity of about 50,000 KL across UAE and Kenya plants.
Capacity utilisation at about 45% across both units.
Kenya grease plant to cater to East African market, which has few grease manufacturers; also to support toll blending.
Proposed acquisition of an additional manufacturing unit as an associate; process underway, details to be shared later.
Quebec Petroleum: associate investment with initial 40% stake, aimed at entering the Indian domestic market.
demand_pricing: Management says demand for lubricants is supported by industrialisation, infrastructure, vehicle ownership and mining, power and construction; customers are shifting toward premium and specialty products.
Cited Middle East and Africa lubricant market growing from about USD 9.1 billion (2024) to USD 12.4 billion (2034).
Company serves more than 400 customers across 25+ countries and 50+ industries.
Top 10 customers account for roughly 70-75% of revenue, including distributors; company sells mainly through distributors, not B2C.
Product prices and landed costs (freight, insurance) rose due to the Middle East war; company passed on a partial cost increase, which also raised receivables.
Base oil and white oil prices are positively correlated with crude, with a lagged and non-identical impact on lubricant prices.
In Kenya, incumbents Shell and Total have not changed payment terms despite new entrants.

qa_highlights.question: How sensitive are margins to base oil and crude price movements?
qa_highlights.answer: Not directly coupled but positively correlated; raw materials (base oils and white oils) move in the same direction with a lag and not in the same proportion.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation of the 50,000 KL capacity, and targets over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: About 45% utilised; capacity is sufficient for 2-3 years on a single shift, but full utilisation would need additional storage capex.

qa_highlights.question: Which vertical has the highest EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing, both in Q1 FY27 and historically; toll blending is being pursued more aggressively.

qa_highlights.question: Share of premium and specialty versus conventional revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialty lubricants contribute around 40% of topline.

qa_highlights.question: Why have receivables risen faster than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher topline (about 50% growth), higher product prices and landed costs from the war, and partial pass-through of cost increases to selling prices.

qa_highlights.question: What if supply disruption lasts more than six months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has onboarded new customers and broadened product baskets; margins may dip further but aim to hold or improve through diversification; still expects over INR200 crores revenue in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How will Quebec Petroleum contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Associate with 40% stake; its profits will be included in consolidated financials; focus is India domestic market, while Maximus covers Middle East, East and North Africa.

qa_highlights.question: Target revenue split between trading and toll blending over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing plus toll blending 75-80%, trading 20-25%; split between manufacturing and toll blending not disclosed as they overlap in co-branding.

qa_highlights.question: Concentration of revenue and B2B versus B2C mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Top 10 customers about 70-75% of revenue (distributors included); no own retail outlets; major revenue comes via distribution channels.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin down about 217 bps YoY to 7.64% due to input and freight costs from the Middle East war.
Working capital: receivables rising faster than revenue; financial cost up about 65% YoY to INR1.53 crores.
Customer concentration: top 10 customers about 70-75% of revenue.
Quebec Petroleum associate acquisition and additional manufacturing unit acquisition: terms and financials not yet disclosed.
Competitive response in Kenya from incumbents such as Shell and Total; payment terms unchanged so far.
Management did not split revenue between manufacturing and toll blending; the reported Q1 PAT decline despite revenue growth needs monitoring.

up ~INR0.6 crores from INR0.92 crores in Q1 FY26

540403|2026-03.headline: CL Educate revenue rose about 55% to ₹570 crore in FY26 and EBITDA more than doubled to ₹69 crore, driven by the DEXIT acquisition.
540403|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 as the first year the group crossed ₹500 crore revenue, with revenue up from ₹368 crore to ₹570 crore and EBITDA up from ₹33 crore to ₹69 crore. Cash generated from operations rose to ₹79 crore from ₹26 crore, and the acquisition-linked borrowing has been reduced from ₹210 crore to ₹180 crore. The DEXIT (assessments) integration is described as complete. The L&D/EdTech segment remains under structural pressure, with realisations down 12-14% and revenue down about 11%, and management expects it to stay flat for roughly four more quarters. Fundraising has been put on a slight pause.

financial_highlights.change: acquisition debt reduced to ₹180 crore from ₹210 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and bank balance (as on date)
financial_highlights.change: from about ₹50 crore last year, excluding ₹185-190 crore pending RPS redemption

segments.name: Assessments (DEXIT)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose to ₹223 crore from ₹205 crore and EBITDA to about ₹51 crore from ₹34 crore. All existing contracts were rolled over and 20 new customers were added. FY27 order book is about 80-85% of FY26 revenue, per management.

segments.name: L&D / EdTech (test prep, university engagement, publishing)
segments.commentary: Enrollment volume grew about 4% but average realisation fell 12-14%, so revenue declined about 11%. Management expects revenue to stay roughly flat for about four quarters, with profitability improving from Q1 FY27 after cost recalibration.

segments.name: MarTech (Kestone, events, VOSMOS, VIRSA)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 11% to about ₹161 crore: international up about 20%, India up about 5%. EBITDA was slightly lower due to set-up costs for the new social events and luxury wedding business. Domestic to international mix is about 1:2.

guidance_outlook: Assessments: management expects reasonably healthy revenue growth in FY27, backed by an order book of about 80-85% of FY26 revenue six weeks into the year.
L&D: revenue expected flat for about four more quarters; profitability expected to show upward movement from Q1 FY27.
MarTech: shift to higher-margin CEP and VOSMOS/VIRSA products over 12-18 months; pruning low-margin MMS and pass-through businesses.
Discontinued operations: bulk of losses done, with a little residual impact possible in Q1 FY27 and none expected beyond that.
Talevate: target to sign 8-10 corporates and about 100 jobs over the next few quarters, testing the MVP before scaling.
capex_capacity: Working capital is about 50% of revenue despite about 50% revenue growth, per management.
Management is marketing land assets, including a Raipur plot earmarked for a school, and is seeking a buyer at the right price.
A new EdTech personalised-learning pilot is to launch in about one month, with a roll-out to all programmes and centres if successful.
Remote proctoring and BYOD technology is being built out at DEXIT; the mySathi IP platform has started going to market.
Settlement of ₹185-190 crore RPS amount awaits NCLT capital reduction approval; order reserved, next hearing on May 15, 2026.
demand_pricing: L&D: enrollment volume up about 4%, but realisation down 12-14%. Students are shifting from ₹30,000-60,000 full programmes to ₹2,000-4,000 modular components.
MBA revenue expected flat to slightly down, with volumes rising. UG segments (law, BBA, IPM) are holding or raising prices, and growth is expected there.
Assessments: government contracts are about 40-45% of mix and private 55-60%. Pricing is similar across both and the market is price-sensitive.
Assessments: rollover of exam dates by 60-120 days shifted some FY26 revenue into FY27.
Competition: PhysicsWallah-type players are seen as low-price and not a direct threat; management launched products at about 50% above PhysicsWallah pricing and one-third of regular prices.

qa_highlights.question: Does the NEET controversy open opportunities for DEXIT in nationwide exams?
qa_highlights.answer: Yatrik Vin said it is a significant opportunity; DEXIT already conducts exams for IRDAI, ICAI and NISM, and its digital and surveillance tech is ready.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DEXIT government/private mix, contract duration, and government tender criteria?
qa_highlights.answer: Government is about 40-45% and private 55-60%. Contract tenure varies from one to five years, or order-based. RFPs weigh technical at 65-70% and commercial at 30-35%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the order book work, and why is it not 100% revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says 80-85% coverage is in hand for FY27, and sales efforts target a higher rollover. Exam timing set by clients can push revenue into the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the fundraising plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Satya Narayanan said fundraising is on a slight pause given the environment, and the boards want value at the right valuation. Updates are expected in the next quarter or two.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the cash and current liabilities linked to NSE?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹182 crore was left behind from the NSEIT transition and has earned ₹11-12 crore of interest, so about ₹193-194 crore is on the balance sheet. It will be knocked off against RPS after NCLT approval and moved from non-current to current liabilities.

qa_highlights.question: How will VIRSA affect MarTech in North America?
qa_highlights.answer: Pilots with Salesforce, Dell and Infosys have had positive feedback. The Salesforce work is for Canada, with a scale-up to the US expected over the next couple of quarters.

risks_watch: L&D revenue flat for about four quarters, with AI and modular pricing pressure expected to persist for four to five quarters.
Assessment revenue timing depends on client exam schedules, which have rolled over by 60-120 days before.
Pending NCLT approval for the capital reduction and ₹185-190 crore RPS redemption; timing of upstreaming to NSE Investments is 'hopefully over this year'.
Fundraising is on pause, with no timeline given.
Interest and depreciation of ₹85 crore weighs on profitability; PPA-related depreciation is included.

540403|2026-06.headline: CL Educate Q1 FY27: revenue fell about ₹17.5 crore QoQ-type decline offset by ₹18 crore cost cuts, lifting EBITDA margin ~218 bps to 16.6%, though still loss-making after tax.

After-tax profit remained negative due to interest and depreciation. Test prep (EdTech L&D) revenue fell about 15% to ₹45 crore from ₹53 crore amid MBA market churn, while DEX digital assessments revenue fell about 17% on a base effect and ₹4.7 crore of deferred revenue. Management framed Q1 as the seasonally weakest quarter and guided to Q2 and Q3 recovery for MarTech and DEX.

540404|2026-06.headline: Prime Fresh Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15.7% to INR81.71 crore and EBITDA jumped 51% to INR6 crore (9.83% margin), which management says is not fully sustainable.
540404|2026-06.overview: Prime Fresh reported Q1 FY27 sales of INR81.71 crore (vs INR53.34 crore), EBITDA of INR6 crore (9.83% margin vs 7.53%) and PAT of INR4.35 crore (vs INR2.89 crore). Management attributed part of the jump to one-off recoveries of pending service-business billings, inventory gains from rising F&V and onion prices, and strong service volumes, and guided that margins may not be sustained. Forward guidance is EBITDA margin of 7% to 7.5% and volume growth of 15% to 25%, with value growth of 25% to 30%. The company is pursuing the Nashik cluster development project under the National Horticulture Board, expected to be awarded in August 2026, and a Bank of Baroda working capital limit increase to INR20 crore.

540497|2026-03.headline: S Chand FY26 EBITDA hit Rs1,449m (18.1% margin) with net cash Rs1,048m; FY27 revenue growth guided at 10-15%, margin at 17-19%.

EBITDA rose to Rs1,449m (18.1% margin, within the 18-20% guidance) and PAT grew 21% to Rs731m. Operating cash flow was Rs747m, below the ~Rs1,000m five-year average, because receivables (160 days) and inventory (232 days) rose. Management guided FY27 operating revenue growth of 10-15%, EBITDA margin of 17-19% (1pp below FY26), and OCF above Rs1,000m.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there no buyback despite a strong net cash position and low valuation?

540530|2026-06.headline: HUDCO guides FY27 disbursement of about INR65,000 crore and a INR3 lakh crore loan book by 2029-30, with spreads held near 2%.

Management reiterated a spread of around 2% and NIM of around 3%, though an analyst cited Q1 spread near 1.8%, and said compression is due to fast growth and should reverse by Q3.
