540544|2026-03.headline: PSP Projects Q4FY26 revenue rose 66% YoY to INR1,115 crores, but a INR29 crore Kashi ECL provision kept FY26 PAT flat at INR55 crores.
540544|2026-03.overview: Q4FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR1,115 crores (up 66% YoY), with EBITDA up 85% to INR60 crores and PAT up to INR21 crores. Reported margins were depressed by a INR29 crore expected credit loss provision on unbilled revenue from the Kashi project, which took other expenses from INR17 crores to INR46 crores. For FY26, revenue grew 25% to INR3,149 crores, EBITDA rose 5% to INR189 crores with margin down to 6% from 7.14%, and PAT was flat-to-down at INR55 crores. Order book reached INR13,447 crores (up 85%) after record order inflow of INR10,925 crores, 85% of it from the Adani group.

segments.name: Adani group (in-house) orders
segments.commentary: Adani group accounted for 85% of FY26 order inflow and about INR9,000 crores (67%) of the current INR13,400 crore order book. Management says materials are pass-through on Adani contracts.

segments.name: External / non-group orders
segments.commentary: External projects are about 33-43% of the order book (about INR4,300 crores per the Q&A). Government projects fell to about 25% of the order book from 43% a year earlier.

segments.name: Precast manufacturing
segments.commentary: Current precast capacity is 3 million sq ft per year. Management says expansion to 1.5x would need only INR15-20 crores of equipment since sheds are already built. Project 90 was pre-executed in 148 days.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance is about INR4,500 crores, reiterated by management.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 7-8%, with management saying it can move 1% plus or minus; the Q&A confirmed 7-8% as the band for the next two years.
Management expects to be debt-free within about two to three quarters, with interest cost of about INR11-12 crores per quarter falling toward nil.
Working capital: trade receivable days are expected to fall to about 60 days (60-70 days per the Q&A) from about 94 days.

Order inflow is expected at INR5,000-6,000 crores from the group plus INR1,000-2,000 crores from outside in FY27. The bid pipeline is about INR6,500 crores, of which about INR5,000 crores is group and INR1,500 crores external.
Capex for FY27 is expected at about INR120-150 crores (roughly 2-4% of revenue), with quarterly lumpiness possible.
Employee cost is expected to grow about 2-4% (per the Q&A), with operating leverage as revenue rises.
Medium-term goal is 20-25% growth per year, with a target of about INR9,000-10,000 crores revenue by FY30 (per the analyst's recap, not restated by management).
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was INR192 crores; Q4FY26 capex was INR40 crores. Gross block is INR764 crores and net block INR412 crores.

Record FY26 order inflow of INR10,925 crores, 85% from Adani group. Major wins include SVPI Airport Ahmedabad development, Matunga Rehab Building Mumbai, and Shri Ambaji Mata Temple extension.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kashi ECL provision and will more come?

qa_highlights.answer: About INR60 crores unbilled and INR40 crores trade receivable across seven projects. INR40 crores of GST invoices are pending, and final certification is awaited.

qa_highlights.question: Will PAT margin reach 4-5%?

540595|2026-03.headline: Tejas Networks Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8% QoQ to INR333 crores, but Q4 PAT loss widened to INR211 crores; FY26 PAT loss INR909 crores.

Order book closed at INR1,514 crores versus INR1,019 crores a year earlier, with India at about 88% of revenue and around 83% of order book, excluding the BSNL 4G add-on PO. qa_highlights.answer: Prince Tiwari said these are newer businesses and product-level risk-adjusted metrics are not yet meaningful. 540692|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 14% to INR931 crore and EBITDA margin expanded 405 bps to 7.7%, while Q4 volume fell to 1,912 MT from 2,349 MT.

540701|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell 4% to INR 6,776 mn and EBITDA to INR 600 mn, mainly from an INR 10 mn order deferred to H2.
540701|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 6,776 mn versus INR 7,080 mn a year earlier, a 4% decline, which management attributed mainly to an order pushed from Q1 into the latter half of FY27. EBITDA fell to INR 600 mn from INR 1,406 mn, and the company posted a loss before tax of about INR 512 mn after finance costs of about INR 370 mn and an FX loss of about INR 117.3 mn. The CDMO segment revenue fell to INR 5,343 mn while Marketable Molecules rose to INR 1,432 mn. Management guided to single-digit group revenue growth for FY27 with EBITDA margin similar to or slightly above FY26, and said a promoter-level ECB of up to CHF 200 mn is expected to close in 60-90 days.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,432 mn, up from INR 968 mn; margin normalised as cholesterol sales outweighed analogues versus a high analogue quarter last year. Vitamin D and analogues sales and margin reportedly rose.

Naroda and Bavla hold certifications from all major international health authorities; Naroda passed a Korea MFDS inspection and is under US FDA observation; two CEPs granted by EDQM.

qa_highlights.question: Why does cash stay overseas rather than repay India debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiary-to-parent loans are not permitted, and repatriation via dividends triggers tax leakage, so Swiss cash is kept as deposits to fund overseas needs.

540704|2026-03.headline: Matrimony.com Q4 FY26 consolidated billing rose 9.9% YoY to INR 126.1 crore; management guides Q1 FY27 PAT to more than double.
540704|2026-03.overview: Matchmaking billing grew 10.5% YoY to INR 125.4 crore in Q4 FY26, ahead of revenue growth of 8.4%, and Matchmaking EBITDA margin improved to 22% from 17.7% a year ago. Consolidated PAT rose 18.9% YoY to INR 9.7 crore, but full-year PAT fell to INR 34.2 crore from INR 45.3 crore as FY26 revenue grew only 0.9% and the Marriage Service and other segment loss persisted. Management said the one-year "Till You Marry" package is now flowing into revenue, narrowing the gap between billing and revenue. Management expects Q1 FY27 PAT to more than double year on year and billing growth in double digits or high single digits.

540716|2026-03.headline: ICICI Lombard FY26 PBT rose 10.2% to ₹36.59bn and 1/n PAT 10.5% to ₹27.72bn; Q4 GDPI grew 18.2% but FY26 GDPI grew only 7.0%.
540716|2026-03.overview: FY26 profit grew double digits despite a ₹0.55bn wage code charge, with Q4 1/n PAT up 7.3% to ₹5.47bn. Top-line growth was 7.0% for FY26 versus the industry's 9.2%, with commercial lines lagging (5.4%) and retail health (51.1%) and Q4 motor (15.0%) accelerating. Management flagged intensifying commercial and fire competition, a Motor TP loss ratio it says is overdue for repricing, and a transition to Ind AS starting FY27 with a plan to seek forbearance. Solvency stayed high at 2.67x and the final dividend was ₹7.00 per share (₹13.50 total).

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 Motor TP loss ratio much lower, and why is the crop loss ratio negative? Has IFRS PAT been quantified?

qa_highlights.question: Solvency is high at 2.7x; can excess capital be deployed via dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Solvency 1 (exposure-based capital) and a pending risk-based capital transition. It will use some solvency for growth as growth returns, and continues a dividend policy of about 25% of PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Health loss ratio split between retail and group, and Motor TP price hike outlook?

540716|2026-06.headline: ICICI Lombard Q1 FY27 PAT fell 46.0% to ₹4.03 bn, driven by a ₹1.65 bn Motor TP judgement provision and two large Fire losses.
540716|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 GDPI grew 7.5% to ₹83.18 bn, below industry growth of 10.9%, with retail lines driving growth while commercial lines de-grew 13.8%. Combined ratio rose to 107.2% from 102.9%, including a 2.8 pp hit from the Supreme Court Motor TP judgement provision and a 1.0 pp hit from two Fire large losses. Excluding these items, the combined ratio was 102.3% versus 102.2% a year ago, and PAT would have been ₹5.75 bn (down 23.0%). Investment income fell to ₹11.74 bn from ₹12.88 bn as capital gains halved, partly offset by higher portfolio yield and duration.

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: De-grew 13.8% in Q1 FY27 amid pricing pressure; SME share rose to 33.6% from 28.4%. Fire line declined 27.8% for the industry and the company de-grew about 32%; June Fire de-growth improved to about 18% for the company.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Grew 14.0% in line with industry (13.9%), market share 10.5%; new vehicle sales up 33.6% vs industry 14.9%. Mix: private car 49.8%, two-wheeler 28.7%, commercial vehicle 21.5%. Motor combined ratio 106.6% in FY26 vs industry 128.0%.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: Grew 24.9% vs industry 20.1%. Retail Health grew 69.5% with share up to 4.5% from 3.5%; Group Health grew 16.3% with 10.3% share. Management attributed the higher health loss ratio to industry-wide claim incidence, not company-specific.

guidance_outlook: Management did not give a quantified forward impact of the Motor TP judgement; said it is too early and will update each quarter.
Expects an upward Motor TP premium rate revision; judgement-driven industry loss ratio impact estimated at 12-15%, which it sees as the minimum price change needed.
Expects Fire price aggression to moderate after Q1, though full recovery of de-growth in the rest of the year is uncertain.
Health claim incidence watch-point for Q2 (monsoon-linked); next detailed update to come with October results.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or commissioning plans were discussed on the call; the call covered underwriting, pricing, reserving and claims only.

Capacity was referenced only qualitatively: management said reinsurance renewals were relatively soft and capacity had been made available across the industry, which drove Fire price competition. No company-specific capacity figures were given.

Motor claims and servicing scale were cited as operating metrics, not capacity: Preferred Partner Network served 75.6% of non-OEM motor claims in Q1 FY27 vs 74.6% in Q1 FY26; 168,521 health and travel claims were serviced through the IL TakeCare app vs 141,116 a year earlier.
Digital servicing capacity: digital interactions rose to 624K in Q1 FY27 from 214K in Q1 FY26; digital share of servicing was 69.0% in Q1 FY27 and 71.0% in June 2026.
Management did not discuss any new product launches, branch or distribution expansion, or timelines for system or platform commissioning.
demand_pricing: Industry Fire rates were cut sharply in the April renewal cycle; the reinsurance renewal was relatively soft, enabling capacity and competition.
Motor TP has seen no third-party price change for several years; the judgement adds a Motor TP loss ratio impact of 12-15% for the industry.
Retail Health share gain: contribution from long-term book in new retail health business rose to 53.4% from 31.8%.
Digital interactions rose to 624K from 214K; digital share of servicing 69% in Q1 FY27 and 71% in June 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ₹165 crore (₹1.65 bn) Motor TP provision only for Q1 business, and will it recur each quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the provision is a holistic assessment of exposures as at June 30, covering past book as well as Q1 business; it declined to say whether it will recur, citing variability in future quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Does the judgement affect closed cases, and what is the Fire loss ratio excluding the two large losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Closed cases typically do not reopen after court finality, so impact is largely on open exposures. Excluding the two large losses, Fire loss ratios should be within the historical 65-70% average range; the company has never exceeded 100% in Fire.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Health loss ratio rise despite GST benefit, and will it rise further in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise reflects industry-wide higher claim incidence, similar to last year's Q1; it is watching monsoon-linked claims into Q2 and will update in October.

qa_highlights.question: Arbitration award of about ₹78 crore: provision and impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The award relates to a policy about seven to eight years old and is on a gross basis; the company will pursue legal remedies and believes the net P&L impact is not material given reinsurance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the reserve prudence buffer still generate releases given the ₹165 crore charge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its reserving philosophy is unchanged, prudence will continue, and reserving triangles should continue to show favourable development over cycles.

risks_watch: Motor TP judgement: outcome of the General Insurance Council review petition, the TP price revision, and whether provisions recur in Q2-Q4.
Fire pricing: competitive intensity and soft reinsurance renewals; watch whether industry de-growth narrows through the year.
Health loss ratio trend into Q2 with monsoon-linked claim incidence.
Possible regulatory change to Motor TP commission norms, not yet specified; management said it will wait for the regulator.
Arbitral award (about ₹78 crore plus interest) under legal challenge; contested by the company.

We are very confident in terms of saying that our reserving philosophy is holding us good, so there is no impact.

540716|2026-09.headline: ICICI Lombard Q2 FY27 PAT rose 27.5% YoY to ₹10.31 bn, while H1 PAT fell 5.8% to ₹14.54 bn on a weaker Q1 and Motor TP reserving.
540716|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 profitability improved sharply: PBT grew 27.8% to ₹13.59 bn and PAT 27.5% to ₹10.31 bn, with combined ratio at 104.5% (102.7% ex-CAT). H1 was weaker, with PAT down 5.8% to ₹14.54 bn and combined ratio at 105.2%, reflecting the Q1 Supreme Court (Shishupal) Motor TP reserving of ₹1.65 bn and Q1 commercial large losses. GDPI grew 5.4% in H1 versus industry 8.9%, though ex-Crop and Mass Health Q2 growth of 13.9% was ahead of industry 13.2%. Management said no further Motor TP reserve top-up is needed and that the judgment is now business as usual.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: H1 growth 13.0% vs industry 13.1%, market share 10.3%; mix PC 49.8%, 2W 28.1%, CV 22.1%. Motor combined ratio 108.3% in Q1 FY27 vs industry 131.4%; management cites ~23 pts gap. H1 Motor loss ratio ~65.4% vs 66.6% last year.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: H1 growth 26.8% vs industry 21.0%. Retail Health grew 66.4% (industry 32.0%), share 4.7% in H1 and 5.0% exiting September. Group Health grew 15.4%, share stable at 8.8%; Group Health loss ratio 97.9% in Q2 vs 93.7% a year ago.

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: Ex-Fire growth 20.0% in Q2 and 13.2% in H1. Fire de-growth moderated to 21.2% in Q2 from 32.1% in Q1, with September at -6.0%. Fire market share 11.9% in Q2 (11.4% prior year); Marine cargo 19.0%; Engineering 16.4%; Liability 16.6%.

segments.name: Crop
segments.commentary: Management said it was deliberately cautious in underwriting Crop this year, which muted headline top-line growth against NEP growth.

guidance_outlook: Management expects earned premium momentum to continue into Q3 and Q4, with gross premium growth ahead of industry.
No further Motor TP reserving requirement anticipated after the ₹1.65 bn Q1 provision; judgment treated as business as usual, with ongoing monitoring.
Motor loss ratio range kept at 65% to 67% (aggregate Motor), with Group Health underwritten around mid-90s and Retail Health at 65% to 70%.
Digital sourcing to be scaled from 6.0% to 15% of business under a defined roadmap.
Expense of management kept within the 30% limit on an annual basis; the draft 25% limit is seen as a positive for the company.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed on the call.
Digital journeys handled 73% of customer interactions vs 39% a year ago; IL TakeCare app has 23.3 mn downloads.
Health underwriting WhatsApp GenAI bot used in over 40% of agency new business daily.
demand_pricing: Industry vehicle sales grew 21.1% in H1 FY27 and 26.9% in Q2, with September up 32.0%; management expects Motor growth to moderate on a higher base from Q3 after GST reform effects.
Retention improved 3% to 5% across retail lines (Motor and Health) in H1 vs last year.
Banca and corporate tie-ups contribute 12.5% to 15% of full-year premium, with single-digit exposure outside ICICI.
Reinsurance accepted is kept at a single-digit share of the overall book; management says no change in book quality in Q2.
Q2 Motor OD loss ratio was hit by Q2 flood events: ~₹118 mn of flood losses vs ~₹74-75 mn last year.

qa_highlights.question: Did Q1 Motor TP loss ratio jump reflect the Supreme Court judgment, and is more provisioning needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ₹1.65 bn was reserved in Q1 and no further reserving is needed; the judgment is now business as usual and development will be monitored over long cycles.

qa_highlights.question: Will IRDAI distribution reforms and commission cuts pressure third-party tariffs and renewals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reform is a recalibration that may lower costs and aid penetration, and tariff impact is uncertain. Retention rose 3% to 5%, and the company is increasing its renewal focus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Group Health and Retail Health loss ratio trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Group Health loss ratio was 97.9% in Q2 vs 93.7% a year ago, but down from ~99.9% in Q1. Retail indemnity was 64.6% vs 65.4% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Motor OD loss ratio deteriorate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to Q2 flood events (~₹118 mn vs ~₹74-75 mn last year). Ex-CAT, OD loss ratio was sequentially better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did commission and other opex ratios rise in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a higher retail mix, which carries higher acquisition cost but better loss outcomes, and said opex changes are business as usual.

qa_highlights.question: How would the 25% expense-of-management limit affect the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is well within the 30% EOM limit on an annual basis and sees the draft 25% limit as a positive for market share.

risks_watch: Motor TP tail development after the Shishupal judgment; any reserve release or strengthening in later quarters.
Distribution reform outcome: commission cuts, possible TP tariff changes, and POSP disruption in CV TP.
Commercial lines loss experience: Q1 large losses and Fire de-growth continuing; September Fire at -6.0%.
Base effect from GST reforms in Q3 and Q4 may moderate Motor growth.
IFRS transition impact not yet quantified; management said a separate briefing will follow.
Crop underwriting caution and Q2 flood/CAT events may weigh on loss ratios.

540719|2026-03.headline: SBI Life FY26 VoNB rose 12% to INR66.7bn at a 27.5% margin, but PAT grew only 2% to INR24.7bn due to GST and Labour Code one-offs.
540719|2026-03.overview: FY26 new business premium grew 20% to INR425.5bn with a 21.4% private market share, and individual APE grew 13% to INR221.1bn. Reported PAT rose only 2% to INR24.7bn; excluding GST and Labour Code impacts it would have been INR31.2bn (up 29%). VoNB was INR66.7bn (27.5% margin), and excluding GST it would have been INR70.3bn at a 29% margin. Management guided to around 14% growth and a 26-28% VoNB margin range, with the GST impact on commissions and expenses now reflected for the second half of FY26.

financial_highlights.change: +2% YoY; ex-GST and Labour Code INR31.2bn, +29%

segments.name: Individual protection
segments.commentary: Individual protection APE INR10.3bn (+24%); pure protection APE grew 122%; protection overall 9% of APE at INR22.4bn (+10%).

segments.commentary: Individual par APE INR17.3bn, up 133% on a low base after new par launches; par sum assured up 166%.

segments.commentary: Individual APE INR68.6bn (+15%); agent productivity INR2.6 lakh; non-ULIP share rose from 34% to 39%; over 1.2 lakh agents added gross and 120 branches opened.

segments.commentary: Grew 22% and contributed 11% of total APE; online channel grew 47% on APE (own website 48-50%).

guidance_outlook: Medium-term APE growth target of around 14%, in line with the 3-5 year CAGR; FY26 individual APE growth was 13% versus 13% guidance.
VoNB margin guided to 26-28% range for FY27-28, with the company aiming to report above 27%; management declined to extend the range to FY27-29.
GST impact on first-year commission for business written before 22 September 2025 is about 1.8-1.9% of margin on an annual basis; management says it is largely absorbed in the 27.5% margin.
Opex ratio expected to carry a full year of GST in FY27, but management expects it not to rise materially; IT and branch spend to continue.
Deferred annuity (regular-pay) product targeted for launch by June 2026, otherwise the next quarter.
Ind AS transition: forbearance sought, with adoption from 1 April 2027.
capex_capacity: Opened 120 new branches in FY26 and added over 1.2 lakh agents on a gross basis; management says newer branches are on track but not yet at breakeven.
Continued investment planned in branches, IT infrastructure and agency training; management says no other major expense is planned beyond IT strengthening.
Solvency of 1.90 funded by internal accruals with no fresh capital raised; the company is assessing Ind AS and RBC impacts.
demand_pricing: Customers are investing where they see value despite geopolitical volatility; February and March growth was described as decent, and management expects continued sales growth.
Q4 bancassurance sales declined year on year; management said the whole insurance sector was sluggish in Q4 and that banca met its internal budget for the year.
Non-par pricing is being adjusted with interest rates; a new non-par product replaced the existing one to reflect current yields, passing some benefit to customers.
Management is not planning higher sum assured ULIPs for now, but will decide on launching them in due course.
Online business grew 47% on APE; 99.7% of individual proposals were submitted digitally and 57% of individual policies went through automated underwriting.

qa_highlights.question: Is the persistency assumption change a negative in the VNB walk, and is there a reset in persistency assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is about 50 bps and not significant; changes were minor refinements across mortality, persistency and expenses, with a persistency improvement from long-term protection.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 14% growth at risk given banca grew only 9-11% for three years, and is banca realistically 10-11%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not guide channel-level growth; growth would come from agency and other channels, with 14% as an optimal mix. Protection growth is ticket-size-light and supports policy count.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 27-28% margin guidance conservative given FY26 ex-GST margin of 29%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a matter of perception; the range gives flexibility to balance 14% growth with margin, and the product mix is being improved.

qa_highlights.question: What is the GST impact on margins going forward and the opex ratio trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: GST for the second half is already in the 27.5% margin, and the full-year effect is about 1.8-1.9%. Opex ratio would be about 5.5% without GST and the Labour Code versus 5.3% in FY25; the 6.1% reflects GST and Labour Code costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EV operating variance strongly positive while VNB assumptions were strengthened?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said positive variance comes mainly from mortality and persistency, with lower expenses contributing. Assumption changes are minor refinements, and new and in-force business differ in product mix. Economic variance of 3.66% is split as 2.15% from equity, with the balance from bonds.

qa_highlights.question: Does open architecture in banca pose a risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is unaware of any such decision, that RBI guidelines are draft and due from 1 July and do not mention open architecture, and that the company will respond to regulatory changes if they arise.

540719|2026-06.headline: SBI Life Q1 FY27 VNB rose 29% to INR14.1bn, but VNB margin fell to 26.2% as GST and a one-off GTI group deal diluted mix.

Profit after tax rose 22% to INR7.2bn, helped by supportive market conditions, while the GST impact was INR2.3bn for the quarter. VNB margin of 26.2% was down year on year, which management attributed mainly to a higher share of lumpy group business (GTI) in APE. Management said the margin was within its 26–28% guidance, at the lower end, and expects it to move to the upper end as individual mix normalises.

segments.commentary: Group NBP INR32.9bn (37% of NBP), +41% YoY; group APE INR53.8bn, +36%; group protection APE INR12.3bn, +313%, driven by a large one-off GTI contract.

segments.commentary: Individual protection APE INR1.9bn, +18%; pure protection +41% on individual APE; ROP share of individual protection 68% vs 73% a year ago.

segments.name: Bancassurance (SBI and RRBs)
segments.commentary: 47% of total APE; individual APE INR24.5bn, +10%; SBI branch productivity INR4.1mn, +7%. Other banks grew 19% on individual NBP and 31% on APE; their mix is about 80% non-ULIP.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: Individual APE INR13.1bn, +20%; agent productivity INR2 lakh; non-ULIP share rose from 43% to 46%; 34,000+ agents added gross and 11 new branches opened.

guidance_outlook: IRP growth guidance of 14–15% for FY27 reaffirmed.

GST drag expected for one more quarter (Q2 FY27), with the impact ending thereafter; GST was waived from 22 September, so about 2.5 months of impact remain in Q1.
Pure protection growth expected to keep outpacing ROP; the company is shifting focus from ROP to non-ROP and pure protection.
Regular-pay deferred annuity plan expected to launch within the next quarter.
Non-ULIP share of IRP targeted to be sustained at around this level for the year.
Other-expense ratio expected to normalise over the next three quarters, but higher stamp duty tied to sum assured growth will persist.

Misselling ratio 0.02%; death claim settlement ratio 98.8%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 60 bps product-mix drag on VNB margin is due to the GTI group deal, and what is the normalised margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 60 bps mix drag relates only to GTI and that the company does not disclose product-wise margins. It said margin should return to normal as IRP share normalises. The 40 bps assumption-related item reflects the March 2026 annual review, and there was no assumption change in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GST drag going to persist, and how do expenses look?
qa_highlights.answer: GST drag of about 1.1 percentage points in Q1 is expected to continue into Q2 and then fade. Management said the rise in other expenses reflects one-off stamp duty tied to higher sum assured and labour code impacts, and it expects these to normalise over the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will agency growth be sustainable and will the channel mix shift affect costs or margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Agency APE grew 20% in Q1, with the current quarter at 19%-plus. Management expects a stronger contribution from agency in the remaining three quarters and a balanced mix of banca and agency going forward. It did not discuss cost impact in detail.

qa_highlights.question: What proportion of ULIPs carry rider attachment, and how is protection classified?
qa_highlights.answer: Rider attachment on ULIPs is about 45–50%, up from roughly 35% when riders were introduced 1–1.5 years earlier. Riders are counted within individual protection, and rider APE was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is individual protection growth lower than peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift from ROP to pure protection lowers ticket size, which makes headline growth look subdued. Individual protection grew 22% by its own measure against pure protection growth of 41%, with ROP share at 68%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the regular-pay deferred annuity plan launch slip, and what are the non-par and regulatory views?
qa_highlights.answer: The deferred annuity plan is expected in the next quarter and is being developed for an opportune time. On non-par, management said pricing is reviewed against yield movements. On regulation, management said it sees the company as well placed and expects future rules to be positive for the industry.

risks_watch: Group/GTI lumpiness: a large one-off group contract diluted Q1 VNB margin; sustainability of group APE mix and margin recovery to 26–28% range is the key test.
GST drag of about 110 bps on margin in Q1 FY27 with another quarter expected; watch whether Q2 drag falls as indicated.
Other-expense ratio rising (opex ratio 7.7% vs 6.3%) due to stamp duty and labour codes; watch cost discipline.

Credit protect flat YoY; watch for the promised uptick.
Rider APE not disclosed; pure protection ticket size is smaller, so protection growth optics may stay weaker than peers.
Regulatory changes flagged as an open question by management; details not yet clear.

540725|2026-03.headline: Share India standalone Q4 FY26 PAT rose 368% YoY to INR 75 crore on revenue of INR 383 crore (+103%).
540725|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue nearly doubled to INR 383 crore and PAT rose to INR 75 crore from INR 16 crore, with EPS of INR 17.6 versus INR 11.7. For FY26, standalone PAT rose 20% to INR 298 crore on revenue of INR 395 crore. Consolidated FY26 PAT was flat-to-down at INR 324 crore versus INR 328 crore, held back by fair value adjustments on investments held by group companies. Management pushed diversification into MTF, PMS, wealth distribution, debt (Share India Cred), AIF and commodities, while flagging RBI curbs on intraday bank limits for prop trading.

segments.name: Broking and trading (prop vs client)
segments.commentary: Prop contributed ~70% of revenue but ~49% of consolidated FY26 profit (~52% standalone). Client turnover reportedly exceeded prop turnover (53% vs 47%) for the first time; target 60% client share of turnover by year-end.

segments.name: MTF (margin trading finance)
segments.commentary: MTF book grew from INR 239 crore (FY25) to INR 424 crore (FY26); Dec-25 level was INR 457 crore. FY27 target INR 650 crore; FY28 vision also cited as INR 650 crore.

segments.name: NBFC
segments.commentary: Reported NIM of 17.64% for FY26, roughly flat with FY25; management said NIM will decline as the book shifts to secured lending.

segments.name: uTrade (algo platform)
segments.commentary: Active clients crossed 5,000 in FY26 (5,231 currently); still small in revenue, with focus on adoption. Multi-broker plan slowed by a SEBI circular requiring vendors to set up separately for each broker.

segments.name: Wealth management and PMS
segments.commentary: PMS launched in Q4 FY26 with AUM above INR 100 crore; FY27 target INR 200 crore. Third-party distribution team under Charu Sehgal to start operations in Q3. AIF CAT-3 application filed with SEBI, approval expected by end-Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Share India Cred (debt)
segments.commentary: Started operations in Q1 FY27 with six issues closed; FY27 target at least INR 500 crore of issues.

segments.name: Institutional business
segments.commentary: Institutional empanelments rose 35% from 137 to 186.

segments.name: Other subsidiaries
segments.commentary: NBFC, merchant banking, insurance and technology together contributed about 7% of FY26 bottom line. MSCI (Metropolitan Stock Exchange) cash segment doing INR 300-400 crore daily volume; Sizable stake held.

guidance_outlook: Annual EBITDA ~38% (+/-2%) and PAT margin ~22% (+/-2%) reaffirmed; management says no structural Q4 pressure.
MTF book target INR 650 crore by FY27, with mgmt saying INR 200 crore incremental is achievable if markets stay normal; deviation possible in low single digits on sentiment.
Target 30 new Tier-3 company-owned branches in next 2-3 years; 6 more targeted by FY27 year-end on top of 7 existing.
Prop share of profit targeted to fall to ~30% in three years; client share of turnover to reach 60% by FY27 year-end.
Share India Cred target INR 500 crore of issues in FY27; PMS AUM target INR 200 crore by FY27-end.
Silverleaf merger pending at NCLT; expected to conclude within about a quarter.
capex_capacity: Seven company-owned Tier-3 branches operating (Hyderabad, Indore, Bhopal, Varanasi, Agra, Raipur, Nagpur), with six more targeted by end FY27.
Target of at least INR 10-15 crore MTF per Tier-3 branch per year; 30 branches implied INR 300-500 crore.
AIF CAT-3 approval awaited from SEBI; wealth-management operations to start Q3 FY27.
Silverleaf merger pending at NCLT; post-merger plans include HFT trading.
MSCI exchange planning IPO segment, SME segment, and derivatives launch in FY27 (subject to approvals).
demand_pricing: Management said Q4 was volatile, with commodities (gold, silver, crude, natgas) driving turnover; cash ADTO rose to ~INR 2,000 crore in Q4 FY26 from ~INR 1,500 crore, and total ADTO rose to ~INR 4,500-5,000 crore from ~INR 1,400 crore in Q4 FY25 (figures as stated in call). Options were ~18% of Q4 ADTO.
MTF demand said to have risen in the last 1.5 months; Tier-3 pricing reportedly better because of less competition from sub-brokers.

RBI curbs: intraday bank limits for prop trading withdrawn; bank guarantees allowed for client business. Management estimates ~20% impact on overall deposits/limits used but minimal bottom-line effect; bank guarantees valid to 30 June can continue to expiry (up to March 2027).
SEBI market-making framework expected in 3-4 months; company is lobbying RBI for liquidity-provider relief.
Mgmt estimates INR 40,000-50,000 crore of capital to exit the market due to RBI curbs, which it expects to widen per-trade margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why do margins dip every March quarter and is that sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said Q4 was weak in FY25 and FY26 due to volatile markets; management prefers annual view with EBITDA ~38% and PAT ~22% (+/-2%). Sachin Gupta said Q4 pressure is not structural.

qa_highlights.question: Status of uTrade multi-broker plans and monetisation model?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Gupta said talks with Motilal Oswal and Dhan stalled after a SEBI circular requiring third-party vendors to set up infrastructure separately per broker, which is costly. No monetisation details were given.

qa_highlights.question: At what MTF AUM does the interest spread become meaningful, given borrowing costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said full-year borrowing costs will flow into FY27 and new NCD and third-party borrowing lines could cut costs by a few hundred basis points. Tier-3 direct branches are meant to remove mediators and lift NIM.

qa_highlights.question: Break up of brokerage vs prop income?
qa_highlights.answer: Prop contributes ~70% of revenue but ~49% of FY26 consolidated profit (52% standalone). Client turnover exceeded prop turnover for the first time (53% vs 47%).

qa_highlights.question: Impact of RBI regulation on prop business and Market Maker regime?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated ~20% impact on limits used and minimal impact on bottom line. Company sought liquidity-provider status; the company is hybrid-classified and can continue bank guarantees until expiry (up to March 2027).

qa_highlights.question: Ballpark revenue diversification in the next three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for 70% client and 30% prop share of profit over three years. Non-broking segments were ~7% of FY26 bottom line; detailed split not disclosed.

risks_watch: RBI curbs on prop intraday limits effective around 1 July 2026; watch for actual impact on prop turnover and margins versus the ~20% management estimate.
Consolidated PAT flat YoY due to fair value losses on group investments; recurrence risk.
NIM compression expected in NBFC as lending shifts to secured products; MTF book is cyclical with market sentiment.
Regulatory changes: SEBI vendor-per-broker circular hurts uTrade multi-broker plans; market-making framework still pending.
Silverleaf NCLT approval and AIF CAT-3 approval timing are uncertain.
540725|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and diversification, but defensive and hedged on the RBI prop curbs and market-dependent targets. Management repeatedly stressed that targets depend on normal markets and geopolitical stability.
key_quotes: So, the Company should be able to continue with the current margins. There is nothing like Q4 type of pressure on us.

So, hardly 20% impact in the overall limits will be there from the prop side, but on the bottom-line side, I don't think there will be much impact or there will be any impact, because per trade margin will improve.
So, MTF definitely depends on the market performance, and whatever the external reasons are, if market is performing good, demand for MTF goes up.

540725|2026-06.headline: Share India Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 48% YoY to Rs 124.41 crore on revenue of Rs 448 crore; management targets ~20% growth this year.
540725|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the company's strongest quarterly performance to date despite SEBI derivatives curbs and RBI funding restrictions on prop desks. Standalone revenue rose 28% YoY to Rs 349 crore and PAT rose 32% to Rs 90.85 crore; consolidated revenue rose 31% to Rs 448 crore and PAT rose 48% to Rs 124.41 crore, with consolidated PAT up 114% QoQ. Growth was attributed to MTF lending income, new subsidiaries (Share India Cred, GIFT City), PMS launch and merchant banking. Management plans CP and NCD issuance to offset funding constraints.

financial_highlights.value: Rs ~74 crore across six issues; EBITDA Rs 1.08 crore; PAT Rs 40 lakh

segments.name: Broking and trading (prop vs client)
segments.commentary: Management said prop contributes ~52% of profitability and ~48% from broking; on revenue, prop is ~58-60%. Client volume is ~60% versus prop ~40%.

segments.name: MTF lending
segments.commentary: MTF book ~Rs 470 crore at end Q1, targeted at Rs 1,000 crore in two years; management called MTF the main source of sustainable interest income.

segments.name: PMS / wealth
segments.commentary: PMS AUM Rs 150 crore at end Q1 (launched in Q1); target ~Rs 250 crore by year-end. Wealth distribution team hiring, operations targeted from Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Share India Cred (debt trading)
segments.commentary: Started operations in Q1 FY27 under Keshav Goyal; ~Rs 74 crore underwritten/sold across six issues, PAT Rs 40 lakh.

segments.name: GIFT City / IFSC
segments.commentary: Turned positive in Q1 with ~Rs 2 crore of income per management, after prior losses.

segments.commentary: Active institutional clients 212 versus 186 at Q4 (+15%). Merchant banking completed a main-board IPO raising Rs 167 crore (subscription above 12x) and one SME IPO of ~Rs 200 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management expects ~20% growth in the current financial year, subject to market conditions.

Branch economics: each branch targets Rs 15 crore MTF book within ~8 months to break even; branches not profitable after 12 months to be shut.
AIF launch expected in Q3 FY27 pending regulatory approval; wealth distribution operations also targeted from Q3 FY27.
PMS AUM target ~Rs 250 crore by financial year end.
Plans to issue commercial paper (rated Crisil A1+) and NCDs to diversify funding; CP programme initiated.
capex_capacity: Seven new branches opened recently against a 30-branch target over two years; branches rolled out in tranches of about eight.

Acquisition of Enshrine (property-holding company, up to Rs 45 crore consideration) to secure ~18,000 sq ft carpet-area office in Mumbai (Interface 11 area); management cited property value above Rs 42 crore.
Silverleaf (HFT technology firm) acquisition previously announced; expected to add technology stack and HFT protocols and support geographic expansion.
AI, automation and in-house platform Techyon cited as technology investments.
demand_pricing: Management said realisations improved during the quarter and commodity business showed improvement.
Industry headwinds cited: SEBI F&O regulatory tightening and RBI curbs on prop-desk top-desk funding; management said smaller brokers face difficulty meeting higher capital requirements.
Retail MTF demand in Tier-3 cities described as underserved, with limited broker options for MTF.
Mid and small-cap volatility affected MTF book; management said it held its numbers with mild growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the payback period for Tier-3 branches given lower ticket sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Gupta said each branch should reach break-even in ~8 months by building a Rs 15 crore MTF book; branches not profitable after 12 months will be closed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the stock underperforming despite low PE and high growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on share price, attributing it to industry regulatory consolidation and cited diversification, institutional clients and subsidiaries as positives.

qa_highlights.question: What is the purpose of acquiring Silverleaf, the tech company?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said Silverleaf (founded by IIT Bombay graduates, 12+ years in business) brings a technology stack and HFT protocols, supporting third-country expansion and back-end technology.

qa_highlights.question: What drove broking and trading performance and what is the prop vs broking split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business has shifted toward lending via MTF (~Rs 465-470 crore) and fee streams from PMS, MF distribution and third-party products; prop contributes ~52% of profit and broking ~48%.

qa_highlights.question: Why pay up to Rs 45 crore for Enshrine, a company with Rs 2-3 crore turnover?
qa_highlights.answer: Kamlesh Shah said the acquisition is mainly to obtain a Mumbai property (~18,000 sq ft carpet area, valued above Rs 42 crore) to consolidate Mumbai offices.

qa_highlights.question: Is prop still a very high share of total revenue and PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said prop was ~58-60% of revenue and ~52% of profit now, versus ~85-90% of revenue and ~70-75% of profit 8-9 years ago.

Funding transition: CP and NCD programmes not yet issued; funding costs and timing are open.
Regulatory approval pending for AIF launch (targeted Q3 FY27).
Stock underperformance despite strong earnings; management attributed this to sector consolidation and external factors.
Q1 benefited from merchant-banking IPOs and valuation gains; sustainability of these flows is not assured.
Branch expansion carries execution risk; management set a hard stop at 12 months for loss-making branches.
Enshrine acquisition value (up to Rs 45 crore) and Silverleaf integration: limited disclosure on rationale and financials.

Management reiterated the INR500 crore revenue aspiration and said the Middle East crisis is a watch item rather than a current drag.

540743|2026-03.headline: Godrej Agrovet Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR2,333 crore; FY27 guidance is early double-digit revenue and mid-teens PBT growth.
540743|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 9% YoY to INR2,333 crore and PBT before exceptional items rose 16.8% to INR87 crore, driven by volume growth and better mix. For FY26, revenue crossed INR10,000 crore at INR10,233 crore (+9%) and PBT before exceptionals rose 17.2% to INR569 crore. Animal Nutrition volumes grew 15% in Q4, Astec reached EBITDA break-even for the year, and Crop Care was hit by co-marketing channel inventory carry-forward. Management guided to early double-digit consolidated revenue growth and mid-teens PBT growth for FY27, with the Iran war and a weak monsoon forecast flagged as variables.

segments.name: Animal Nutrition
segments.commentary: Q4 volumes +15% YoY, well ahead of industry; cattle feed +24%. Margins expanded, helped by new Type 1 products, East and Central share gains, raw material cost reconfiguration, and a ~INR9.5 crore pet food manufacturing income booked in other income.

segments.name: Oil palm
segments.commentary: FY26 marked by record area expansion, strong volume growth and an all-time high oil extraction ratio. Q4 is seasonally weak (~60,000 t of FFB out of 6.37 lakh t annually) but margins held. Specialty fat refinery to start rolling out in May 2026.

segments.name: Crop Care
segments.commentary: Q4 hit by carry-forward of co-marketing channel inventory, lowering in-house volumes; partly offset by specialty products. FY27 is guided as a recovery year, with recovery from Q2 and very high double-digit growth in top and bottom line.

segments.name: Astec LifeSciences
segments.commentary: Achieved EBITDA break-even in FY26; Q4 revenue and EBITDA grew strongly on CDMO volumes, realisations and utilisation. FY26 mix was ~48% enterprise and ~52% CDMO; exports ~53% of revenue. Board reconstituted with Arijit Mukherjee as Executive Director.

segments.name: Creamline Dairy (CDPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~5% YoY ex bulk sales in Q4; profitability pressured by elevated milk procurement costs. Management expects milk prices to ease gradually from Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Godrej Foods
segments.commentary: EBITDA margins improved significantly in Q4 on Live Bird and Yummiez; branded revenue salience above 80% in FY26. Live Bird trading is being phased out; momos and frozen chicken entries planned.

540743|2026-06.headline: Godrej Agrovet Q1 FY27 consolidated sales rose 10% to INR2,852 crore; Crop Care fell 16.2% on delayed monsoon, while management still targets double-digit FY27 PBT growth.
540743|2026-06.overview: Consolidated sales grew 10% YoY to INR2,852 crore despite a delayed monsoon and geopolitical-driven inflation. Animal Nutrition (revenue +12.6%, reported segment result +29%) and Oil Palm (revenue +28.9%, segment result +14.4%) carried the quarter. Crop Care revenue fell 16.2% on a dry June and slower kharif sowing, and Dairy margins were squeezed by milk procurement costs and packaging inflation. Astec reached EBITDA breakeven versus an INR11 crore loss a year ago. Management reiterated FY27 double-digit consolidated PBT growth (versus earlier mid-teens guidance) but deferred a firmer view on Crop Care until end-September.

segments.commentary: Revenue +11.4% and volume +8%, but profitability hit by elevated milk procurement prices and packaging inflation. Route-to-market reconstitution (about 18-20 months) under new CEO Gaurav is starting.

qa_highlights.question: Can Crop Care recover in H2, and is the consolidated mid-teens PBT growth still achievable?

qa_highlights.question: Astec: revenue outlook and margin?

qa_highlights.question: Will the palm oil shift need extra capex, and what is the Foods/Dairy pricing picture?

540749|2026-03.headline: MAS Financial Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 25% YoY to INR104 crore, with AUM at INR15,304 crore, up 19%.
540749|2026-03.overview: Consolidated PAT for Q4 FY26 was INR104 crore versus INR83 crore a year earlier, and full-year PAT was INR379 crore, up 21%. Standalone AUM grew 18.71% and standalone PAT grew 23.39% YoY in the quarter to around INR100 crore. Standalone net Stage 3 was 1.70%, slightly better than 1.72% in December 2025, while gross Stage 3 edged up to 2.57% from 2.56%. Cost of borrowing fell 42 bps YoY to 9.39%, and management guided to 9.20-9.25% over the next two to three quarters. Credit cost was elevated because of deliberate aggressive write-offs of 90+ DPD assets, which management said were funded from profit.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Micro-enterprise loans (MEL)
segments.commentary: AUM rose about 20% to INR5,737 crore from INR4,793 crore.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - SME loans

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Two-wheeler
segments.commentary: AUM grew 35.43% to INR1,063 crore from INR785 crore; yields cited at 19-23%.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Salaried personal loan
segments.commentary: AUM grew around 22% to INR1,264 crore from INR1,040 crore.

segments.name: Housing finance subsidiary
segments.commentary: AUM rose 22.41% to INR940 crore from INR768 crore; Q4 PAT INR3.70 crore vs INR2.64 crore, net Stage 3 0.68%. Management aims for INR1,000 crore, now about a quarter later than planned.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 20-25% on a sustained basis; long-term target of INR1 lakh crore AUM by 2036.

Branch additions of 30-35 planned in FY27 after a year of consolidating existing branches.
Dividend: final dividend INR0.75 per share, total INR2 per share for FY26, about 10% payout.
Capital adequacy to be maintained at around 20%; debt tie-up for about half of FY27 done, full-year tie-up expected soon.
capex_capacity: More than 200 branches and about 16,500 centres; branch network to grow by 30-35 in FY27.
Average cash and cash equivalent balance of about INR1,000 crore plus unutilised cash credit of over INR200 crore.
Cash credit facility of about INR1,500 crore across 14 banks, utilised at 70-75%.
Sanctioned facilities over INR2,000 crore as of 31 March (term loans, NCDs, direct assignment, co-lending).
Term loan sanctioned pipeline of about INR1,300 crore; INR750 crore term loan raised in Q4 at 3-5 year tenor; INR100 crore NCDs raised in Q4.
Direct assignment of INR940 crore executed in Q4; a further INR500 crore+ of direct assignment and co-lending sanctions to be used in the current quarter.
demand_pricing: Direct sourcing is about 64% of the book; fintech partnerships are about 10% of business.
Yield rose about 40 bps sequentially, attributed to fintech mix and 2-wheeler growth; SME yields were also higher.
Management said assignment income is amortised, not upfront, and the NII rise was mainly from lower borrowing cost and the MCLR reset.
Standalone 90+ write-offs were aggressive in FY26 (more than 0.10% of assets), mostly unsecured per management.
Caution list added petrol pumps, gas agencies, transporters and some chemical industries in Feb-March 2026, alongside textile and agro, due to West Asia supply concerns.
Management reported no slowdown in disbursement growth as of the call.

qa_highlights.question: How is MAS using data and AI for risk-adjusted growth, and what early warning systems exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it back-tests risk models on its own repayment experience, not generic bureau scores; it moved from LOS to business rule engines and plans AI-based risk management after 6-9 months. Field checks included more than 2,000-3,000 commercial vehicle borrowers after the Middle East crisis, plus bounce data from 100% bank or e-NACH collections.

qa_highlights.question: Will the West Asia crisis and inflation affect lending and asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said asset quality should hold but is being watched closely; it is growing CV more slowly as an energy- and logistics-linked precaution. Disbursement growth has not slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for cost of borrowing and the Q4 cost of borrowing trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of borrowing is 9.39% and is expected to fall to 9.20-9.25% over 2-3 quarters. Q4 interest expense was about INR222 crore vs INR219 crore in Q3, with the MCLR reset adding to NII.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the origination and fee cost high, and what is driving opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the fees and commission depend on product structure. Fintech partners get the spread as commission, and yields rose about 0.5%. Opex is judged against ROA, not in isolation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise and what is the normalised level?
qa_highlights.answer: The rise was from deliberate write-offs of 90+ DPD assets, not stress. Normal credit cost is 1-1.25% of closing AUM; 1.5% is possible in quarters with aggressive write-offs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is CV growth slow, and what is the write-off and recovery policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is slowing CV growth for 1-2 quarters due to logistics and transport risk. Write-offs occur after 360 days across all products; recoveries are credited to P&L net.

risks_watch: Rising inflation and energy costs from the West Asia crisis could hit logistics, transport and fuel-linked MSMEs.
Credit cost is a function of aggressive write-off policy; quarterly credit costs could run towards 1.5%.

540749|2026-06.headline: MAS Financial Q1 FY27: consolidated AUM up 21% to INR16,100 crores and PAT up 27% to INR110 crores; credit cost guided 1.25%-1.75%.
540749|2026-06.overview: Consolidated AUM grew about 21% YoY to INR16,100 crores and PAT rose about 27% to INR110 crores, with standalone PAT up 25% to INR105 crores. Asset quality was stable, with standalone GNPA at 2.58% and NNPA at 1.70%, flat QoQ, and a management overlay of INR17.60 crores held. Borrowing cost fell 55 bps YoY to 9.25%, while credit cost rose to about 1.6% of AUM, which management attributed to higher on-book mix, a 5 bps rise in Stage 1/2 provisioning and prudent write-offs. Management reiterated 20-25% AUM growth guidance, with the call leaning toward the upper end for FY27.

segments.commentary: AUM INR976 crores, GS3 0.98% and NS3 0.68%; PBT up 62% to INR5.70 crores; average yield about 14%, credit cost about 0.5%. Expansion into Tamil Nadu and Karnataka starts this quarter.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance maintained at 20-25%, with management saying the full year is very likely to be at the higher end of the range.
Credit cost to stay in a 1.25%-1.75% range, depending on product mix; management pointed to commercial vehicles as high-yield, high-loss.
ROA target of 2.75%-3.25%, with an aspiration of 3%+.
Net interest margin target of 8%-8.5% on a 7%-7.5% spread; incremental borrowing cost 9.2%-9.25%, expected to stay stable (9.2%-9.3% per Q&A).
Direct distribution share (currently 66%-67%) expected to reach 70%-72% in 1-1.5 years; off-book target kept at 20-25% of AUM.
Used CV growth expected to pick up only after 1-2 quarters; housing finance AUM expected to inch up in the next few quarters.
Credit rating upgrade being pursued, timing not given; sub-9% borrowing cost called far-fetched in the next 1-2 quarters.
capex_capacity: Distribution of 16,500 centres through 209 branches, with more than 200 NBFC partners providing about 33% of originations; direct share 67%.
Employee count reduced by 380 in Q1 due to technology adoption; no quantified headcount target given.
In-house tech team of close to 100 people; LOS live for all products, with BRE added and straight-through processing improving.
Branches opened after March 2024 expected to mature (sweat) by 2027-28 or earlier.
demand_pricing: Standalone MSME/SME demand stable across manufacturing and trading; eligible demand fell in Q1 due to tighter credit screens on energy-dependent sectors (restaurants, gas-dependent manufacturing, export businesses).
Used CV demand robust, but eligible demand lower because of fuel-cost tightening.
Two-wheeler Q1 degrowth QoQ attributed to seasonality; monsoon and Gujarat floods flagged as temporary and not expected to cause major stress.
Working capital demand rising for some businesses on higher input costs; underwriting parameters also tightened.
Write-offs were INR29 crores in March and INR19 crores in June, offset by higher ECL provisioning, keeping impairment cost flat QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise from about 1.2-1.3% to about 1.6% of AUM despite the microfinance impact and Q4 write-offs last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher on-book assets (on-book up 8.25% QoQ vs AUM up 5.5%), which added INR6-7 crores of Stage 1/2 provisioning from a 5 bps rise to 0.7%. Prudent write-offs and mix shift toward higher-yield commercial vehicles also contributed; ROA not affected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20-25% growth guidance at risk given the West Asia conflict and energy-linked stress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said energy-dependent segments were tightened early and stress was limited; eligible demand fell in Q1 and Q2 but normalised, and guidance is expected to hold with the upper end targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Will borrowing cost fall further from 9.25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to predict and depends on RBI and liquidity; the target is to stabilise at 9.2%-9.3%, with a credit rating upgrade being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the Stage 1/2 provisioning increase and whether there are macro-related buffers?
qa_highlights.answer: Stage 1/2 provisioning rose to 0.7% from 0.65%, adding INR6-7 crores; management described it as a buffer.

qa_highlights.question: What was the nature of the INR10 crore OCPS redemption in the subsidiary MRHMFL?
qa_highlights.answer: The OCPS was refunded to the parent because the housing subsidiary's CRAR exceeded 37% and it did not need the capital.

qa_highlights.question: Why did off-book share fall and what is the housing finance growth plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Off-book is dynamic and chosen by price; target stays at 20-25%. Housing finance plans to expand into Tamil Nadu and Karnataka from Q1, with results expected in Q3-Q4.

risks_watch: Used CV: eligible demand softer on fuel-cost-driven credit tightening; management says growth push is 1-2 quarters away, and CV is high-yield, high-loss, so credit cost direction depends on mix.

Credit cost: rose to about 1.6% of AUM from about 1.2-1.3% a year earlier; management guides a 1.25%-1.75% range and Stage 1/2 provisioning went to 0.7% from 0.65% (INR6-7 crores), which management calls a buffer.
Energy-linked and West Asia stress: eligible demand fell in Q1 and Q2 and management says it has normalised; the next quarter will show whether this holds.

key_quotes: So, very high possibility, yes. We are working on that quite optimistic. Can't predict, but you are thinking on the right lines.

So, currently, sub-9 immediately within next 1 or 2 quarters looks like a far -fetched assumption.

rows.why: Direct share is 66%-67% now and management has guided to 70%-72% in 1-1.5 years, which supports spread and yield.

540750|2026-03.headline: IEX Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 10.8% YoY to INR 129.8 crore on record 39.4 billion units traded volume.
540750|2026-03.overview: IEX delivered record quarterly electricity volume of 39.4 billion units (up 24.3% YoY) and consolidated revenue of INR 196.4 crore (up 12.5%), with PAT up 10.8% to INR 129.8 crore. Full-year PAT rose 14.9% to INR 492.9 crore and a final dividend of INR 2 per share was declared. Exchange prices fell sharply on higher sell-side liquidity (DAM down 12.2% YoY in Q4), and other income dropped about 29% sequentially-adjusted per analyst, attributed to treasury mark-to-market losses in March. Market coupling (CERC draft of April 17, 2026 naming Grid India as MCO, comments till May 16) is the dominant overhang, with management disputing its benefit. Gas exchange (IGX) volumes fell 8% in Q4 on Middle East supply disruption and management expects no growth in Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: INR 2 per share (200% of face value)

segments.name: Electricity - DAM/RTM
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 DAM price averaged INR 3.89/unit (down 12.2% YoY) and RTM INR 3.68/unit (down 15%) as DAM sell-bids rose about 49%. RTM was 39% of electricity volumes in FY26 (55 billion units, up about 41%).

segments.name: Green market (G-DAM)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 green volume rose 26.5% to 2.4 billion units; FY26 volume 10.8 billion units (+23%).

segments.name: Renewable energy certificates (REC)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 RECs traded 71.7 lakh (+6% YoY); FY26 187 lakh (+5%).

segments.name: IGX (gas exchange)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume down 8% on Middle East supply disruption; FY26 volume 76.8 million MMBtu (+28%); Q4 PAT INR 9.4 crore (+5.4%). Exchange holds about 3% of India's gas consumption and 20% of spot market.

segments.name: ICX (I-REC)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 issued 46 lakh I-RECs (+29% YoY); FY26 179 lakh (over +200%). Q4 revenue INR 2.2 crore; FY26 INR 7.7 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management expects electricity volume growth of 15-20% annually to continue in FY27, dependent on demand-supply conditions.
IGX gas volumes expected flat YoY in Q1 FY27 and to grow from Q2 FY27 if Middle East supply normalises.
Coal exchange: draft Coal Regulations 2025 out; final regulations expected later in calendar 2026; board gave in-principle approval to explore setting up a coal exchange.
Management says market coupling would add no value and cost Grid India extra; IEX says it would absorb software changes at no extra cost.
Buyback under consideration; SEBI has not finalised the mechanism, and the company is awaiting SEBI's open-market route draft.
capex_capacity: IGX IPO process has been initiated; management says it is progressing well but did not give status detail.
PNGRB has given IGX until December 31, 2026 to complete the stake reduction.
Pending CERC approvals: TAM extension to 11 months, green RTM petition (reserved), and peak DAM/peak RTM segments for merchant storage (reserved).
BESS: 13 GW under first VGF tranche underway; about three-quarters of the 30 GW second tranche awarded.
SECI 500 MW / 3-hour RE CfD pilot (1,500 MWh/day), backed by a INR 76 crore stabilisation fund; applies to battery capacity per management.
demand_pricing: DAM sell liquidity rose about 44% for FY26; FY26 DAM average INR 3.86/unit (down about 14%) and RTM INR 3.59/unit (down 16%).
More than 70% of cleared volume is now through the API system; management says over 5,000 industrial consumers use the platform.
Management says exchange customer count is rising and no customers have been lost to rival exchanges since the July 2025 coupling order.
Management sees the TAM segment (uniform liquidity across three exchanges) as evidence that transaction fees (about INR 0.036-0.037/unit) would hold up under coupling.
VPPA interest is currently limited, per management; data centres and multinationals could add demand later.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall about 29% versus the recent quarterly run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vineet Harlalka said the December quarter included a one-time treasury gain, and March saw mark-to-market losses from the Iran conflict and rupee weakness. He expects the numbers to recover as markets recover.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the final PMR and market coupling procedure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot estimate; PMR 2021 was notified in February 2021 after a 2019 draft, and the regulator will consider comments and market redesign.

qa_highlights.question: Would IEX lose volumes and margins if market coupling goes through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customer loyalty and value-added services would retain share; cited TAM margins holding at about INR 0.036-0.037/unit despite shared liquidity. No additional software cost is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is RTM coupling feasible, given 48 auctions a day?
qa_highlights.answer: Management doubts RTM coupling is feasible: it would move from 48 to 288 five-minute blocks with no slack time, and an aggregation failure at one exchange could cause price jerks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the buyback stance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said a buyback is a good option after the revised tax structure; the company is considering it and awaiting SEBI's open-market route decision.

qa_highlights.question: Will electricity volume growth continue in FY27 and why did REC volumes fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 15-20% volume growth. On RECs, management said there was no fall: REC volume rose 5% in FY26.

risks_watch: Market coupling: CERC draft (April 17, 2026) names Grid India as MCO; comments close May 16, 2026, and the timeline for final rules is unknown.
Gas exchange volumes weak in Q1 FY27 on Middle East supply disruption and high gas prices.
Treasury and other income volatility from mark-to-market swings (other income fell in Q4).
Continued DAM/RTM price decline (down 12-15% YoY in Q4) could pressure fee income if volumes do not offset.

segments.commentary: Sole I-REC issuer in India; management cited about 200% growth in I-REC volumes last year. Q1 REC volumes were down sharply YoY, which management attributed to the first quarter and possible RPO buy-out confusion.

segments.commentary: Incorporated as a separate company in June 2026; coal rules notified 4 June 2026 require e-auction and marketplace trades to move to exchanges within six months of launch. 540762|2026-03.headline: TII standalone Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16% YoY to Rs 2,279 Cr and PBT (pre-exceptional) rose 10% to Rs 361 Cr.
540762|2026-03.overview: Standalone revenue for Q4 FY26 was Rs 2,279 Cr versus Rs 1,957 Cr a year earlier, with full-year revenue of Rs 8,556 Cr against Rs 7,893 Cr. Pre-exceptional PBT for the quarter was Rs 361 Cr versus Rs 327 Cr, and full-year ROIC held at 44%. Consolidated revenue rose to Rs 6,215 Cr from Rs 5,150 Cr, helped by CG Power (56% stake) revenue of Rs 3,442 Cr. Management described volumes as still strong, while flagging commodity and fuel cost inflation, partly recoverable from customers with a one-to-two-quarter lag. Growth in EV three-wheelers was held back in Q4 by a body-in-white supplier problem, now being resolved in-house.

Engineering revenue rose 21% to Rs 1,566 Cr with flat PBIT at Rs 153 Cr, and Metal Formed Products PBIT fell to Rs 28 Cr from Rs 37 Cr despite 11.5% revenue growth. The e-mobility (Clean Mobility) business posted its highest-ever quarterly turnover of close to Rs 240 Cr and management said losses likely peaked, with volumes up about 64% QoQ. Management said steel price recovery, including Q1 under-recovery, will be fully recovered, while non-steel inflation (fuel, freight) recovery talks with OEMs are ongoing.

Mutual fund market share was 9.02%, flat QoQ, and equity yield compressed to 52 bps (ex-arbitrage) from about 54 bps in Q1, which management attributed to telescopic pricing and equity inflows. 540768|2026-03.headline: Mahindra Logistics returned to profit in Q4 FY26, with reported PAT of INR20.2 crores versus a INR6.7 crores loss a year earlier.

rows.label: Freight forwarding build phase
rows.why: Freight forwarding revenue fell 44% YoY to INR50.6 crore and the business is in a build phase in H2 FY27, with real delivery expected only in FY28; geopolitical disruption is delaying new contracts.

rows.label: Manpower cost pass-through
rows.why: The PF wage-ceiling change (INR15,000 to INR25,000) adds cost and many contracts lack pass-through clauses, so pass-through is only partial, while fuel (INR8.10 per litre-equivalent) was fully passed through.

tone.note: Management was confident on the MESPL EBITDA turnaround, new business wins and balance sheet, but cautious on margin timelines (100 bps target now medium-term) and declined to quantify MESPL margins or the tech spend, which analysts pushed on.

540769|2026-03.headline: New India Assurance FY26 profit after tax rose 40% to INR 1,384 crore, but combined ratio worsened to 122.57% on wage-revision charges.
540769|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 GWP grew only 1.63% to INR 11,619 crore, reflecting competitive property pricing, while Indian domestic GDP grew 10.9% versus the industry's 9.3%. The full-year combined ratio rose to 122.57% (116.67% excluding the wage revision impact) as the company absorbed INR 3,525 crore of wage and family pension revision costs. Incurred claim ratio rose to 98.65% on Motor TP court awards, the Air India aviation loss, marine claims and NATCAT flood claims not fully recovered under reinsurance. Management guided to a Motor single-digit growth and double-digit overall growth in FY27, led by Health Retail.

financial_highlights.change: +1.63% vs INR 11,433 crore in Q4 FY25
+61% vs INR 347 crore in Q4 FY25
vs 116.78% in FY25; 116.67% excluding wage revision (vs 115.34%)
vs INR 6,124 crore loss in FY25
vs 1.91 times in FY25; regulatory minimum 1.5 times

segments.name: Health and PA
segments.commentary: 47.57% of book; premium up 12.62% in FY26 but only 2.58% in Q4. ICR improved to 99.05% from 100.98%, helped by TPA audits raised from 30% to 50%.

segments.name: Fire
segments.commentary: Premium up 10.76% in FY26 but down 4.33% in Q4 on property rate cuts. ICR rose to 76.54% from 71.20% on small NATCAT claims not fully reinsured.

segments.name: Motor OD
segments.commentary: Premium up only 2% in FY26 and 11.48% in Q4 after deliberate portfolio pruning. ICR worsened to 108.85% from 104.22%; management expects about a year to see impact.

segments.name: Motor TP
segments.commentary: Premium up 0.13% in FY26 with no tariff revision yet; ICR rose to 113.86% from 108.17% as court awards increased.

segments.name: Marine
segments.commentary: Premium up 11.43% in FY26 and 20.26% in Q4; ICR jumped to 86.74% from 53.74% on cargo claims and a general average claim.

segments.name: Crop
segments.commentary: Premium declined as inward crop reinsurance was not accepted; ICR rose to 96.15% from 81.02% on legacy claims.

segments.name: Other lines
segments.commentary: Premium up 12.48% in FY26 and 2.03% in Q4; ICR rose to 63.40% from 58.77%. Miscellaneous ex-crop grew about 26% per analyst question, driven by engineering, liability and surety bonds.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 industry growth in double digits; New India to grow double digits overall.
Motor growth to be single digit in FY27, with focus on profitability over volume.
Overall ratios expected to show a reducing trend in FY27 as Motor portfolio recalibration takes hold.
Motor mix target: private cars and two-wheelers to dominate; CVs above 7,500 cc to be reduced; two-wheelers to move toward double-digit share selectively.
Motor OD premium increases planned on selected segments; commissions and payouts to be adjusted dynamically in commercial lines.
Health Retail to be the primary growth driver under the 'GO RETAIL' mandate.
capex_capacity: Motor portfolio churn started from Q2 FY26; management says about another year is needed to reach the target mix.
IT infrastructure revamp nearing completion; all retail products online; mobile super apps for customers, intermediaries and surveyors launched.
Automated survey appointment and digital survey reports implemented.
Digital marketing and sales piloted for a few Health products, to be extended to other lines.
Bharat Maritime Pool operationalised with sovereign guarantee; company acting as lead insurer for P&I and hull risk.
demand_pricing: Industry GDP reached about INR 3.36 lakh crore in FY26, up 9.3%; New India's domestic share rose from 12.56% to 12.74%.
Segment market shares: Fire 17.56%, Marine 17.77%, Motor 9.91%, Health and PA 14.93%, other lines 15.13%.
Property rates fell sharply in H2 FY26 on competition, driving Fire Q4 degrowth.
Motor competition described as extremely competitive; discounts rising every quarter over the past year.
Motor sales recovered after GST rationalisation: private cars grew 17.8% and two-wheelers 21.5% in H2 FY26; Q4 growth was 16.3% and 24.7%.
Distribution mix (domestic): broker 35.79%, direct 30.13%, agency 25.91%, dealer 7.56%, bancassurance 0.61%.
Commissions cut across many lines including Health; reinsurance commissions increased. Q4 commission ratio fell to 9.53% from 11.17%.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the Motor portfolio course correction take, when will loss ratios fall, and will OD premiums be repriced?
qa_highlights.answer: Correction began in Q2 FY26 and needs about another year; overall ratios expected to fall in FY27. OD premium increases planned on selected segments. Competition remains extremely competitive with discounts rising each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the target Motor mix?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 mix: private cars 47.56%, commercial vehicles 45.60%, two-wheelers 6.79%. Plan to exit CVs above 7,500 cc and grow private cars and two-wheelers, with two-wheelers toward double digits selectively.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the commission ratio decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissions reduced across many lines including Health, and reinsurance commissions increased, so net commission moved in the company's favour.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 growth outlook and capital gains for FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Double-digit growth expected for the company, with Motor at single digit. FY26 capital gains were about INR 5,477 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Where will Health and PA profitability go?
qa_highlights.answer: Health ICR reduced by about 2% and commission ratio cut, which management says significantly raised segment profitability; individual Health demand supported by 18% GST waiver.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is market share gain and how will underwriting discipline hold with faster growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth described as strategic, mainly retail; underwriting guidelines set by head office with strict periodic monitoring.

risks_watch: Combined ratio of 122.57% and ICR of 98.65%; watch whether ratios fall in FY27 as management guided.
Motor TP premium revision still pending while court awards rise; Motor OD ICR at 108.85%.
Wage revision and family pension costs (INR 3,525 crore in FY26; INR 597 crore absorbed in Q4) may weigh on future results.
Q4 GWP growth of 1.63% and Fire degrowth of 4.33% amid property rate cuts.
Long-run market share decline from about 19% (FY09) to 12.74% amid rising competition from new private insurers.
Solvency ratio fell to 1.84x from 1.91x; fair value of investments fell to INR 13,878 crore from INR 21,406 crore.

Answers on pricing, commissions and competition were brief and lacked specific targets.
key_quotes: We have just started this course correction in Motor from the second quarter of this year.
It would be a single digit for Motor, double digit for the entire book.
We have reduced the ICR this year by 2% and also brought down the commission ratio.

rows.why: Q4 GWP grew only 1.63% to INR 11,619 crore, Fire premium fell 4.33% in Q4 and Motor is guided to single-digit growth, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.why: Management plans OD premium increases on selected segments, with Motor OD ICR at 108.85% versus 104.22% a year earlier, though competition is extremely intense and discounts are rising each quarter.
