rows.why: No tariff revision yet, while Motor TP premium grew only 0.13% in FY26 and TP ICR rose to 113.86% from 108.17% on court awards.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, market leadership and Health profitability but defensive on the 122.57% combined ratio and Motor losses, relying on a one-year timeline; analysts pushed on Motor loss ratios, OD repricing, commissions and sustainability of share gains.

540774|2026-03.headline: IFGL Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 2% YoY to INR 276 crore and FY26 consolidated income grew 14% to INR 1,904 crore; consolidated Q4 EBITDA margin 8.6%.
540774|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 total income was INR 278 crore (+2% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 11.8%, while FY26 standalone EBITDA margin was 11.3%. Domestic revenue grew 7% YoY in Q4 and 20% for FY26 to INR 864 crore, but exports fell 11% in FY26 on geopolitical and market headwinds. Margins were hit by product mix shifts, lower exports and higher raw material and freight costs. Management also announced a senior leadership reshuffle, with Mukesh Rawal moving to India operations and Manoj Rakhecha to international operations.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 2.15 per share (21.5% of face value)

segments.name: Domestic (India)
segments.commentary: Domestic revenue reached INR 864 crore, up 7% YoY in Q4 and 20% for FY26. Management says growth comes from share gains in large integrated steel plants and new small foundry accounts; it does not split the growth by source.

segments.name: Exports (India-made)
segments.commentary: Export revenue fell 11% in FY26 on geopolitical and external market headwinds. Management says volumes have started to improve, and it has added manpower to rebuild export accounts.

segments.name: USA (Americas)
segments.commentary: US revenue grew 26% YoY in Q4 and 25% in FY26, with subsidiary EBITDA margins back in the high-teens (described later as double-digit). Management calls the margins sustainable.

segments.name: Sheffield Refractories (UK)
segments.commentary: Management reports strong performance with healthy growth, operating leverage and sustained customer demand. Phase 1 of the India technology transfer is complete.

segments.name: Hofmann Ceramics (Germany)
segments.commentary: Losses fell significantly in FY26 after turnaround steps and cost cuts. Management expects the business to move close to breakeven during FY27.

segments.name: Monocon (UK)
segments.commentary: Revenue recovered despite losing a key high-margin UK customer after a plant closure. Management targets breakeven by Q4 FY27 and is entering foundry and new geographies.

guidance_outlook: Management is targeting double-digit domestic volume growth in FY27, and says it expects to grow well above underlying market growth over the medium term.
Management expects US results to show major growth in FY27 and expects the Americas to remain an important contributor.
Hofmann is expected to move close to breakeven during FY27; Monocon is targeted to reach breakeven by Q4 FY27.
Management is in talks with customers on price revisions and expects a reasonable pass-through of cost increases.
The Sheffield plastic ramming technology is expected to be ready for full-fledged market entry by end of CY2026, after trials.
Consolidated amortisation of about INR 26.7 crore a year ends from FY27 because the legacy goodwill from the 2017 amalgamation is fully amortised.
capex_capacity: Greenfield project in Khurda, Odisha: work has picked up, but the Board is still evaluating pace and structure, with no timeline given.
Gujarat (Bhachau) greenfield plant: awaiting statutory approvals from the Government of India under Press Note 3; no timeline given.
Vizag plant: first energy optimizing furnace (EOF) campaign completed with a lining and tuyere blocks made in-house, exceeding 1,000 heats.
Management says recent capex in Vizag, Rourkela and R&D will mature and generate returns; capex is described as under control.
Alumina and basic brick capacity for cement is planned at Bhachau and a joint venture basic brick line is coming up.
demand_pricing: Indian steel capacity expansion announcements are expected to drive refractory demand; management says customers increasingly prefer full-range refractory solution providers.
Raw material costs remain elevated due to energy, freight and currency; imported minerals and shipping rates are the key cost swing factors.
Competitive pricing has been accepted in bricks and casting flux to win new accounts, with margins initially lean.
Early FY27 saw LPG availability issues linked to West Asia developments.
Europe: order books are improving, with policy support for domestic manufacturing, defence and infrastructure. German foundries serving specialised alloys are on an uptrend.
Monocon has raised prices where input and logistics costs require, and says customers are accepting this.

qa_highlights.question: What operational triggers will reverse the five-year decline in return metrics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said market conditions have changed and pointed to the US turnaround and Hofmann/Monocon fixes, with results expected within a year. It also said recent capex will mature and generate returns.

qa_highlights.question: Why has working capital expanded, and what is the plan for inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said working capital cycle has reduced versus last year and cash was generated from it, and that inventory is on a declining trend. No quantified inventory days were given.

qa_highlights.question: How will capital deployment be balanced against rising net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said debt is negligible, that investment in Vizag, Rourkela and R&D is for future returns, and that capex is under control. Consolidated debt is INR 195.6 crore against cash of INR 122 crore.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Sheffield technology transfer add to top line, and what is the delta?
qa_highlights.answer: Mukesh Rawal said the customer base is identified, equipment is online and trial orders are in hand, with full market entry expected by end of CY2026. He said the revenue delta would be provided later by the CFO. No figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US demand outlook for Q1 FY27 and for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects major US growth in FY27, with new customer trials succeeding. Mexico is growing and foundry business is being added in the US and Mexico.

qa_highlights.question: Is the domestic volume growth target 15-20% for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company is at least targeting double-digit domestic growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Monocon's turnaround and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Monocon is entering new geographies and products, including foundries, with trials underway. Management aims to restore profitability by Q4 FY27 and is seeking price hikes where needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why are exports underwhelming, and is it a deliberate pullback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift to India was a deliberate decision because global steel is shrinking, and it will retarget exports as opportunities arise. Geopolitical factors and European plant closures were cited.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving senior management exits?
qa_highlights.answer: Mihir Bajoria said the exits are normal churn after the former CEO, Mr. Arasu, left with his team. Mukesh Rawal said the top team is restructured and in place, and he returns full-time from August.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from product mix, lower exports, and raw material and shipping cost swings; price pass-through is still under negotiation.
Leadership transition: former CEO and senior team exits, with Mukesh Rawal full-time from August and Manoj Rakhecha moving to international operations.
Export volumes fell 11% in FY26 and export accounts may need rebuilding.
Hofmann and Monocon are still loss-making, with breakeven targets for FY27 and Q4 FY27.
Working capital and inventory levels are high, and consolidated net debt has emerged versus earlier cash-rich position.
Ongoing ambiguity over Khurda and Gujarat greenfield timing, pending government approvals.
540774|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on domestic share gains and the US business, but cautious on exports, Europe and Monocon. Evasive on capex timing (Khurda and Gujarat greenfield) and on exact revenue deltas, and defensive on leadership churn.
key_quotes: Importantly, these appointments represent continuity rather than change.
I'm pleased to share that Phase 1 has been successfully completed, including product recipe transfer, knowledge sharing and joint product development activities.
So, I am a very firm believer that the numbers what we have presented for US are not one -off, but those would be sustainable quarter-on-quarter, you know.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management is targeting at least double-digit domestic volume growth in FY27 after domestic revenue grew 20% in FY26 to INR 864 crore, and US revenue grew 25% in FY26 with major growth guided for FY27; however exports fell 11% in FY26.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not disclosed, and the Board is still evaluating pace and structure of the Khurda greenfield, so a formal capex decision is conditional on market conditions and government approvals for Gujarat.

rows.why: No revenue or margin guidance raise was given; management guided only at least double-digit domestic volume growth and breakeven targets for Hofmann (FY27) and Monocon (Q4 FY27), with exports still weak.

rows.why: Raw material, freight and LPG availability issues linked to West Asia, plus lean margins from competitive pricing in bricks and casting flux, and Monocon's loss of a key high-margin UK customer, create risk to the Monocon Q4 FY27 breakeven target and margins.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The Sheffield plastic ramming technology is expected to be ready for full-fledged market entry by end of CY2026 after trials, with customer base identified and trial orders in hand, though no revenue delta was quantified.

rows.label: Hofmann and Monocon losses narrowing to breakeven
rows.when: Hofmann near breakeven during FY27; Monocon breakeven by Q4
rows.why: Hofmann losses fell significantly in FY26 after cost cuts and Monocon revenue recovered despite losing a key high-margin UK customer, with explicit breakeven targets set by management.

rows.label: Consolidated amortisation of INR 26.7 crore ends from FY27
rows.why: Legacy goodwill from the 2017 amalgamation is fully amortised, removing about INR 26.7 crore a year of consolidated amortisation against FY26 consolidated EBITDA of INR 146 crore.

rows.label: Price revisions with customers
rows.why: Management is in talks on price revisions and expects reasonable pass-through of cost increases, but Monocon's price hikes are accepted only where needed and bricks and casting flux were priced competitively to win accounts.

tone.note: Management was confident on domestic share gains, the US business and the Sheffield technology, but cautious on exports, Europe and Monocon and evasive on Khurda and Gujarat greenfield timing and on the Sheffield revenue delta; analysts pushed on returns, net debt, working capital and leadership chu

540774|2026-06.headline: IFGL Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA fell 17% YoY to INR31 crore on raw material and LPG cost spikes, while consolidated PAT rose 58% to INR17 crore.
540774|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue rose 8% YoY to INR297 crore, with domestic up 7% and exports up 9%, but gross margin fell to 43% from 47% on higher raw material prices. Standalone EBITDA dropped 17% YoY to INR31 crore as input costs and LPG availability constraints outpaced price increases, which management says will pass through with a lag. Consolidated total income rose 13% YoY to INR515 crore and consolidated EBITDA rose 2% to INR40 crore, with PAT up 58% to INR17 crore. The Europe segment was weak because British Steel's low output cut offtake at Sheffield Refractories, while US operations grew double digits with improving margins.

financial_highlights.change: Management says base has grown; target double-digit for year-end

segments.name: Standalone India
segments.commentary: Revenue INR297 crore (+8% YoY); EBITDA INR31 crore (-17% YoY) hit by raw material costs and LPG/fuel price surge. Price increases were implemented but are only partly offsetting costs.

segments.name: Europe (Monocon UK + Sheffield Refractories)
segments.commentary: Management attributed the weak quarter mainly to Sheffield Refractories' low sales due to British Steel's blast furnace problems, with losses rising to about INR7 crore from INR3 crore QoQ (per analyst). Monocon UK losses reportedly fell QoQ and it is approaching breakeven.

segments.name: US subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Revenue grew double digits YoY with improved margins from cost optimization; management described margins as more than double-digit and robust.

segments.name: Monocon and Sheffield Refractories (overall)
segments.commentary: Combined revenue grew double digits YoY despite headwinds; Monocon has opened offices in Australia and Saudi Arabia and is entering iron and steel and foundry refractories.

segments.name: Hofmann Ceramic
segments.commentary: Order book held at similar levels YoY; management targets reducing losses and breakeven by end FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects price increases to flow through progressively over coming quarters, but says they are temporary and offset only input cost rises, with no additional margin expected from them.
Consolidated EBITDA margin target is double digit, dependent on geopolitics and overseas demand; earlier 12% margin reference was not reaffirmed explicitly.
British Steel expected to restart blast furnace and normalize offtake in Q2 FY27; Sheffield Refractories expected back to normal.
Speciality Steel (ex-Liberty Rotherham) melt shops are expected to restart around November-December 2026 per market sources.
Management says staff cost is at about 10% of revenue and is not expected to go beyond this level.
Management believes the worst is behind on profitability, but cautioned that conditions can change quickly.
capex_capacity: Sheffield Refractories Phase 1 plastic ramming mass production has started at IFGL Vizag facility; marketing trials underway, with full customer trials and accreditation still needed.
Adding mag carbon brick and casting flux new lines could add INR150-200 crore of revenue at peak capacity for these two products.

Chinese JV: government appropriate authority approval sought; authorities advised changing location and reapplying, so the project is on hold. Investment so far is only in land (Gujarat), with some spend.

R&D facility in Odisha: management said spend is around INR20 crore, disputing an analyst's INR100-150 crore figure. R&D is developing foundry materials, thin slab caster tundish SEN for the US, and recycled material use.
demand_pricing: India steel demand forecast to grow 7.4% in 2026 and 9.2% in 2027 (management citation).
US steel production up 6% YoY; US business revenue up double digits, with new product introductions (thin slab caster tundish SEN) made in the US.
UK: British Steel now in public ownership; British Steel produced at very low levels in Q1 due to blast furnace problems.
Ocean freight spikes due to geopolitical situation hit UK and China operations.
Price increases were negotiated per contract and are temporary, tied to input costs from geopolitical tension.
Management said there was no market share loss in domestic business; the base has grown, which lowered the percentage growth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove overseas subsidiary growth and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Manoj Rakhecha said the Americas drove top-line growth with robust margins. Management expects momentum to continue across subsidiaries and aims to turn loss-making units (UK, Europe, America, Germany) back to profit. Company-wise margins were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall 17% if there was no competitive pricing pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said raw material and LPG/fuel costs rose sharply due to geopolitics, and price increases from customers were not enough to offset them.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Europe EBITDA turn negative (-8%) after nearing breakeven in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe comprises Monocon UK and Sheffield Refractories. Sheffield's sales were low because British Steel's output was minimal; Monocon UK is near breakeven. Q2 expected to normalize; no orders lost, just timing.

qa_highlights.question: Will staff costs stay near 10% of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Agarwal said standalone staff cost of INR28.7 crore is up from INR24 crore in Q4 but level with Q1 FY26; management aims to contain it. Consolidated employee cost rose partly due to a provision reversal last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is 12% consolidated EBITDA margin still the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is aiming for double-digit consolidated EBITDA margin, dependent on geopolitics and overseas demand, and expects to return to that level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Chinese JV and R&D investment?
qa_highlights.answer: The Chinese JV is on hold pending government approval; the company must change location and reapply. Only land in Gujarat has been bought so far. R&D spend is about INR20 crore per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is the worst behind for profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Manoj Rakhecha agreed with that view for today but cautioned that conditions can change quickly; he cited early green shoots in European steel.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak revenue capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: No overall peak revenue figure given; the two new lines (mag carbon brick and casting flux) could add INR150-200 crore at peak.

risks_watch: Raw material and LPG/fuel costs: management says price increases are temporary, only offset input costs, and lag cost increases; watch whether standalone EBITDA margin recovers as price increases flow through in coming quarters.
British Steel blast furnace restart and Sheffield Refractories offtake: management expects normalisation in Q2 FY27; a delay would keep Europe segment loss-making.
Monocon UK and Europe losses: Europe EBITDA went to -8% with Sheffield losses rising to about INR7 crore from about INR3 crore QoQ (per analyst); track whether Monocon UK reaches breakeven.
Speciality Steel (ex-Liberty Rotherham) melt shop restart, reported by market sources for November-December 2026; no firm confirmation given.
Chinese JV on hold pending government approval, with a location change and reapplication required; only land in Gujarat acquired so far.

Consolidated employee cost: management says standalone staff cost is around 10% of revenue and will not go beyond this; consolidated employee cost rose partly due to a prior-quarter provision reversal. Watch for containment.
key_quotes: The contraction was primarily driven by higher raw material costs arising from geopolitical unc ertainties and supply chain disruptions, along with elevated LPG costs due to availability constraints during the quarter.
And these are all temporary price increase based on the input cost, which has increased on this geopolitical front.
So far it's only been done in land and some money has been spent because we've been marketing other products
So definitely, the worst is behind us.

540777|2026-03.headline: HDFC Life FY26 VNB rose only 2% to INR 4,034 crores; NBM fell to 24.2% after GST and surrender-value impacts, with Q4 growth slowing at HDFC Bank.
540777|2026-03.overview: FY26 individual APE grew 7% YoY, but top-line growth fell below the company's original expectation, with the slowdown concentrated in Q4 from unabsorbed GST, softer bancassurance and deferred demand in March. Proprietary channels grew 15-16% in Q4 and FY26, and protection grew 43% for the year. VNB rose 2% to INR 4,034 crores and NBM fell 140 bps to 24.2%, with 130 bps from GST/SSV, 90 bps from fixed-cost absorption, and 40 bps from persistency assumption strengthening, partly offset by 120 bps of product mix. Management said the GST drag is tapering (about 110 bps in Q4) and should be neutralised by H1 FY27.

segments.commentary: Mix rose about 300 bps YoY to around 8% of individual APE in Q4; AGNI, a variable annuity linked to Nifty 50, launched in Q4 at a ticket size of INR 25 lakh and above.

qa_highlights.question: How has counter share in HDFC Bank changed in Q4 vs the nine months, and what gives confidence it will normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 counter share was lower than the 9-month level; FY26 closed in the early 60s% vs mid-60s% prior year. Management says it knows which cohorts it let go and what it takes to compete back, and expects to regain share as GST costs are absorbed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the participating fund in deficit and why is new business strain rising faster?
qa_highlights.answer: Deficit reflects GST ITC loss on renewal commission and maintenance expenses, plus higher surrender-value reserves from October 2024 regulation changes. Strain rose because of protection and credit protect growth, higher ULIP multiples and rider attachment, and GST impact.

qa_highlights.question: Can VNB grow in line with the 2023 plan, and what is the normalised three-year VNB CAGR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says FY23-FY26 CAGR was about 3%; adjusting for roughly INR 1,000 crore of GST and SSV effects, the normalised three-year VNB CAGR would be about 9-10%. Management expects a 1.8x-2x growth over four years to remain the aim.

qa_highlights.question: Why did persistency assumption changes and the yield-curve movement not show up separately in the VNB walk?
qa_highlights.answer: Economic assumption changes are captured within product profile rather than shown separately, since repricing is dynamic. Persistency sensitivity rose because ULIP mix increased and surrender-value rules now affect non-linked margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand to deeper markets, and what are the returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says Tier 2 and 3 is a priority, with customers acquired in FY26 over 72% new to HDFC Life and Tier 2/3 growing faster than Tier 1. Payback is about 1.5x longer than metro branches.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the dividend maintained when a INR 1,000 crore preferential issue is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the capital is growth capital for protection, the dividend is business as usual for retail and pension shareholders, and the company balanced both objectives by keeping the payout flat.

540777|2026-06.headline: HDFC Life Q1 FY27 VNB rose 9% to INR 879 crores at a 25% margin, with individual APE up 7% and HDFC Bank channel subdued.
540777|2026-06.overview: Individual APE grew 7% YoY and overall APE 9%, led by credit life and group, while channels excluding HDFC Bank grew about 17% with agency up 21%. VNB rose 9% to INR 879 crores and new business margin was 25%, up 100 bps QoQ, after absorbing about 60 bps residual GST impact. Profit after tax was INR 611 crores (up 12%, or 17% excluding GST), embedded value INR 65,860 crores and solvency 185%. 13-month persistency moderated about 200 bps to 84%, and HDFC Bank channel business stayed soft as the company ceded share during competitive pricing in FY26 and says it has now recovered.

segments.commentary: Retail protection grew 60% YoY, driven mainly by aggregators; market share across partners broadly stable.

qa_highlights.question: Why has margin improved only modestly over the last 7-8 years versus peers, and what is the basis for confidence in FY27 growth and VNB?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins expanded 100-150 bps per two-year period to FY22, then fell about 90 bps (FY22-24) on regulatory changes, with 26.3% in FY24 and a 100 bps surrender-charge impact in FY25; the GST impact was 300 bps, of which about 110 bps remained at FY26 end, 50 bps was absorbed in Q1 and about 60 bps is still to go. Growth confidence rests on agency (up 21%) and proprietary channels (up over 20%).

qa_highlights.question: Will non-par and product mix sustain, and what happens to margins if ULIP picks up?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said ULIP mix will not rise meaningfully, non-par expected to hold mid-20s share, annuities to stay well above last year, and NBM to stay around 25%-odd. Protection's share may stay roughly where it is, and growth may be higher in the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Has the HDFC Bank counter share recovered, and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bank share has returned to roughly the level of a year ago on a run-rate basis, with pricing more benign; the company declined to give channel-wise growth guidance and said it is tracking selectively by segment (non-par, protection, par over unit-linked).

qa_highlights.question: Is the non-par recovery demand-led or a result of company pricing and yield-curve effects?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it is a combination: competitor intensity has eased, the company can compete on sensible terms, headline rates are higher than a year ago, and customer asset allocation toward guaranteed products is also a driver. He said the company will not compete on price alone.

qa_highlights.question: What is the banca growth outlook, and how does HDFC Bank compare on a 2-year CAGR basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Banca beyond HDFC Bank grew about 15% in Q1. HDFC Bank was described as marginally lower or flattish YoY; on a 2-year CAGR basis it is similar to other banks at about 10%, and management guided 10-12% growth for HDFC Bank.

qa_highlights.question: How much runway does capital have before a fundraise, and what is the variable annuity opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Solvency is 185% with INR 500 crore sub-debt capacity (about 4% upside); management is comfortable with 15-18 months runway at the current run rate. Variable annuity: two product structures launched, aimed at customers willing to commit for a longer period, slightly younger and with lower ticket sizes; margins said to be above company average.

qa_highlights.question: What is the persistency outlook, given traditional persistency fell from 88-89% to about 83%?
qa_highlights.answer: Appointed Actuary cited a shift to lower ticket sizes after the tax change, a product feature that drove lapses (now moderated, about 40-50 bps effect), and the Q1 March-pace effect. Expected traditional persistency range is 84-85%; 87-88% was not expected in the near term.

540777|2026-09.headline: HDFC Life H1 FY27 VNB rose 12% to ₹2,037 crore at a 24.7% margin, while solvency fell to 180% on capital consumption.
540777|2026-09.overview: Q2 individual APE growth of 13% (overall) and 11% in H1 kept HDFC Life ahead of the private industry, with individual weighted received premium up 11% in Q2 and market share up 10bps to 16.2%. VNB reached ₹2,037 crore (up 12%, Q2 up 15%) and margin expanded to 24.7% from 24.5%. Persistency softened on unit-linked renewals and a non-par cohort, and the EV walk showed negative operating and investment variances from equity underperformance, yield rises and wider credit spreads. Solvency fell to 180%, prompting a ₹500 crore subordinated debt raise. Management spent much of the call on the IRDAI distribution-economics consultation paper, where it was non-committal on specifics.

financial_highlights.change: Regulatory requirement 150%; ₹500 crore sub-debt expected to add about 4 percentage points
Q2 individual weighted received premium +11% vs private industry +10%

segments.name: Bancassurance (HDFC Bank)
segments.commentary: HDFC Bank-sourced individual APE grew 12% in Q2, slightly ahead of company growth; the bank accounts for about 48% of APE in Q2 but less than 40% of NBP. Other bancassurance partners grew 13% in Q2, and a new J&K Bank partnership was announced.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: Agency grew 13% in H1, faster than the company and the agency market. Branches opened in the last ~30 months contribute about 17% of agency business versus 12% a year ago; protection and annuity together are about 30% of channel mix versus 15% previously.

segments.commentary: Unit-linked 45%, non-par savings 22% (from about 18%), participating 13%, annuity 12% (versus 4-5% previously), retail protection 8% (from about 7%). Retail protection grew 33% in H1; protection plus riders is 11% of APE; credit protect grew 19%.

segments.commentary: Pension business AUM reached ₹1.8 lakh crore, up 28% YoY. MSCI ESG rating upgraded to AAA from AA.

VNB growth to be in line with APE or slightly ahead; management will prioritise VNB growth over margin, with margin an outcome of mix and competition.
GST cost benefit (about 15% cost reduction) gets fully baked into the business model from H2 FY27; scale recovery is expected to lift margins, but most will be reinvested.
Expects persistency to recover by year-end, particularly unit-linked renewals, with the non-par cohort run-off progressing.
Expects to remain comfortably above the 150% regulatory minimum through FY27 after the ₹500 crore sub-debt, which is expected to close in the current quarter.
Protection growth expected to normalise in H2 against a 57% base (H2 FY26 post-GST), while remaining strong on a two-year CAGR basis.

qa_highlights.question: What changed at HDFC Bank that drove growth recovery, and did IRRs or commissions change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited granular branch-level engagement, a withdrawal of extra contests about a year ago, and fixing credit and people issues over the last 3-4 months. Rates were kept competitive with higher yields; no change in commercial payouts.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EV walk operating variance is persistency, and what drove the investment variance?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating variance was primarily unit-linked persistency plus residual non-par run-off. Investment variance came from equity returns of about 3-3.5% versus 5% expected, a 25-30bps short-end yield rise, and wider credit spreads.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the capital consumption and how will solvency evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term profitable products lock capital under the current regime; the sub-debt adds about 4 percentage points, and management expects to remain comfortably above 150% through FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How do the proposed commission limits affect VNB margin and EoM?
qa_highlights.answer: Expense ratio about 21%, with commissions more than half; under the proposed levels, commissions fall to half or less, so a 15% EoM is mathematically achievable, subject to scale and glide-path considerations.

qa_highlights.question: Is persistency pressure concentrated in TULIPs or the wider unit-linked book?
qa_highlights.answer: Not limited to any product: pressure is uniform across unit-linked. Recent unit-linked persistency variance is captured in the EV; management expects most to be recovered by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit life share, and what is the HDFC Bank share of it?
qa_highlights.answer: HDFC Bank contributes less than one-third of credit life business, which is diversified across MFIs, NBFCs, banks and the HDFC Group. Management would not disclose the bundled-versus-separate premium collection mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Palghar GST demand, and does the appeal change the provisioning stance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the balance-sheet figure is correct and it is treated as a contingent liability (₹942 crore base, with the accrued total in the books). Interest is excluded and management is confident on the merits, so no provision was taken; contingent liabilities rose to ₹2,207 crore from ₹1,870 crore.

risks_watch: Distribution-reform consultation: commission caps, closed-architecture tilt and possible credit-life restrictions could affect bancassurance and group business; draft regulation timing is uncertain.
Unit-linked renewal persistency and the non-par cohort run-off: recovery is expected by year-end and needs monitoring.
Solvency at 180% with capital consumption ongoing; RBC transition timing (possibly next year) is open.
Palghar GST demand (₹942 crore base, contingent liability) and the reported ₹2,423 crore figure in the appeal: the exact amount and solvency impact remained unclear.
Protection growth normalisation in H2 as the GST-exemption base effect kicks in (base growth of 57% in H2 FY26).
Equity and yield volatility driving investment variance and the EV walk.

540795|2026-03.headline: Dynamic Cables Q4 FY26 revenue growth slowed to 7% YoY (core products ~20%), with a greenfield plant delayed to September 2026 and order book at INR808 crores.
540795|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue (up 17% YoY), operating profit up 23% to INR130 crores at a 10.8% margin, and PAT up 30% to INR84 crores. Q4 overall growth was only 7% because low-value LV conductors and railway signalling cables were discontinued, while core products grew about 20%. The greenfield capacity has slipped roughly 15 months versus earlier guidance and is now targeted to start production around September 2026. Order book stood at INR808 crores at 31 March 2026, with management attributing softer March order booking to aluminium and PVC price spikes.

Management cited ~11% YoY growth (analyst figure; ~18% also cited)
Lower YoY per analyst; management steered to operating margin

segments.commentary: Private 80%, Government 13%, Export 7% of FY26 sales. Export declined slightly in FY26 and March 2026 exports were nil.

guidance_outlook: No short-term or yearly guidance given; long-term growth guidance of 18-20% (value terms, multi-year) reiterated, with ~1.5x industry growth expected in FY27 ('should be able to do it').
New greenfield plant targeted to go live around September 2026, with trial production in next 3-4 months; no firm date given. Capacity to be available ahead of the seasonally stronger H2 FY27.
H1 FY27 growth to be managed from existing facilities; management said current capacity is sufficient for H1 order book.

Further capex expected each year to sustain growth, but not as intense as FY26; next capex set not yet crystallised. FY26 capex was high due to the greenfield plant.

TS Conductor tie-up (carbon core HTLS conductors) needs little incremental capex as existing facilities can be used; no hard revenue timeline, with type testing and approvals expected to take about a year.

demand_pricing: Aluminium and PVC prices spiked in March 2026; management says customers deferred orders, but acceptance is gradually building and grid-driven demand cannot be deferred for long.

Railway signalling cables discontinued due to high competitive intensity and low margins; capacity redirected to power cables.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 growth came from volume versus realisation, and why is growth soft?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall Q4 growth was 7%, but core products grew about 20%; the gap reflects discontinued LV conductors and railway cables. Realisation grew 12% and volume 8% for core products. The high Q4 FY25 base (38-39% growth) and March order deferrals also weighed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 growth outlook given the capex delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated that it does not give yearly guidance and that long-term growth is 18-20%. H1 FY27 is to be served from existing capacity, with the new plant targeted for September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the greenfield plant slip?
qa_highlights.answer: Three causes: delayed regulatory approvals, imported machinery shipments delayed by freight issues after the Iran war, and AERB compliance requirements. Management now says most machinery and civil work is done.

qa_highlights.question: What happened to gross margin and other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin varies with product, customer and freight mix and steered analysts to operating margin, which was steady at the 10.5-11% guided range. Employee cost decline was attributed to a one-time Q4 FY25 bonus accrual.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TS Conductor tie-up and what does it mean for revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an entry step into the high-voltage conductor market using carbon core HTLS technology, mainly for the domestic market. Product approvals and type testing take about a year, and there is no hard revenue timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 capacity be enough, and what is the next capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is fungible across products. Next capex is not yet decided, but incremental capex is directionally expected to sustain growth.

540795|2026-06.headline: Dynamic Cables Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to a record Q1 level, with EBITDA up 41% to INR38 crore and order book at INR811 crore.
540795|2026-06.overview: Management reported record first-quarter revenue, up 33% YoY, with EBITDA up 41% to INR38 crore (margin 10.9%) and PAT up 37% to INR25 crore. Growth was largely price-driven: volume grew only 5-6% against a high base of roughly 25-26% last year, as aluminium price spikes led to order postponements in April-May. The company entered the US market in the quarter with first supplies, and the new capacity expansion is on track for commissioning from September 2026, with meaningful revenue expected from Q4. Order book stood at INR811 crore as of 30 June 2026, with customers booking shorter cycles at elevated prices.

segments.name: HV cables
segments.commentary: 68% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Core growth driver alongside T&D demand.

segments.name: LV cables
segments.commentary: 30% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Company has been moving mix away from LV toward HV and MV.

segments.name: Conductor
segments.commentary: 2% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Conductor volume growth was lower than cable volume growth in the quarter.

segments.name: Solar / renewable cables
segments.commentary: About 20% of revenue in Q1; expected to remain in a similar range for FY27 H1, rising in H2 as new plant comes on. Management sees 25-30% growth for the next 3-4 years.

segments.name: Railway signalling
segments.commentary: Temporarily held back due to weak margins and competition; not a shutdown. Zero contribution in last Q1, so no base effect this quarter.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: 13% of revenue. US contributed about 15% of exports in its first quarter; Asia, Southeast Asia and Africa remain the core; Middle East negligible.

guidance_outlook: No formal annual guidance; management reiterated 18-20% growth record over the last 10-15 years and aims to sustain a similar long-term rate, with some quarters of higher, others of moderate growth.
New plant (about INR45 crore capex) to commission from September 2026; meaningful revenue expected only from Q4 FY27.
Target optimum utilisation of 80-85% of the new plant by end FY28, roughly 18 months from commencement.
Asset turnover of 6-7x on the new plant implies revenue addition; brownfield expansion possible later.
Solar cable revenue share to stay around 20% for FY27; more notable increase next year.
US market: margins initially similar to domestic, with possible incremental margins later; no one-year target given.
capex_capacity: New plant: capex about INR45 crore, commissioning from September 2026 (delay behind, on track per management).
Existing capacity utilisation about 85%.
E-beam technology is new; will be launched first at the new facility.

HTLS conductor and data centre cable products: management says most capex is fungible with existing machinery, with limited add-on capex needed; focus is on product development and customer approvals.
Licensed for HV/LV and MV cables for the US market.
demand_pricing: Price variation clause in variable-price contracts passes input cost changes to customers; fixed-price contracts are hedged by booking raw material at order time (about 20% of order book is fixed-price).
Order book of INR811 crore; April-May order inflow was weak as customers resisted booking at elevated aluminium prices; orders now limited to near-term (2-4 month) execution.
Order cycles and order sizes have shortened due to global volatility and tariffs; management says dispatches not impacted.
Competition described as healthy for now despite capacity expansion across the industry; demand picking up with expansion.
US market is distribution-led; competition is global (US local makers, Mexico, Turkey, India, China). Management cites large replacement demand over 10-20 years.
Management says some Adani/Birla cable business is for captive use; Birla focused on house wires; sees low risk to orders from these groups.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company protecting margins if copper and aluminium costs stay high?
qa_highlights.answer: Variable-price contracts carry a clause passing input cost changes to customers; for fixed-price orders, raw material is booked at order time to protect margins.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of Q1 volume and realisation growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume grew 5-6% YoY; most of the balance of revenue growth came from aluminium-driven price increases. Base effect was high at about 25-26% volume growth last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why was growth weaker in Q1 and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Base effect, plus customer order postponements after a sharp input price rise in March-May. Management expects improvement as prices settle but calls the environment very uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new plant on schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, regulatory delays are behind; commissioning planned for September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why is order book only about 10% up YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers were reluctant to book at elevated prices in April-May; weak order booking was industry-wide and should pick up as prices stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US export opportunity and business model?
qa_highlights.answer: First US supplies started this quarter after 15-18 months of work on licences and tariffs; US contributed about 15% of exports. Model is distributor-led, with HV/LV and MV cables licensed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off and full-year guidance position?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-offs; the high growth came from price increases. No annual guidance, but long-term growth of 18-20% is maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue will the new capex add and how fast will it ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Meaningful revenue from Q4 FY27; target 80-85% utilisation by end FY28; asset turnover 6-7x on INR45 crore capex.

qa_highlights.question: Is pricing competition intensifying from capacity expansions?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition is currently healthy; demand is rising in step with industry expansion, and the T&D story is seen as secular.

qa_highlights.question: Why was debt higher versus March 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory value rose 20-25% due to higher raw material prices (quantity unchanged); receivables comparison on last-six-month sales is unchanged in debtor days.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company diversifying into house wires?
qa_highlights.answer: Only the B2B building wire segment, not B2C distribution or branding; positioned as an additional product in similar segments.

Volume growth of 5-6% against a high base; watch whether volume recovers as management expects.
Commodity price volatility: inventory values rose, raising debt; watch working capital and borrowing costs.

US export ramp is at an early stage; reorders and cross-referencing not yet proven.
Railway signalling business held back; re-entry timing unclear.
Industry-wide capacity additions in HV/EHV could pressure pricing later.

540795|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 31% YoY to INR712 crore and operating margin held at 10.44%, though Q2 gross margin fell to 16-17%.
540795|2026-09.overview: Dynamic Cables reported H1 FY27 revenue of INR712 crore (up 31% YoY), operating profit of INR74.3 crore (up 29%) at a 10.44% margin, and PAT of INR47.1 crore (up 24%). Management attributed the Q2 gross margin decline to product and order mix plus some commodity volatility, and said volume growth was about 6% in the quarter, with the rest of growth from price. The new manufacturing plant's machinery is installed and is expected to contribute from H2 FY27, with a ramp-up over 3-4 quarters. Management reiterated 10-11% EBITDA margin and sub-15%-of-EBITDA finance cost guidance and a long-term ~20% value growth CAGR.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin decline to 16-17%?

540879|2026-06.headline: Apollo Micro Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 17% YoY to INR156 crores, while consolidated revenue jumped 88% to INR251 crores; standalone PAT up 43% to INR28 crores.
540879|2026-06.overview: Management reported its best June quarter, with standalone revenue of INR156 crores (+17% YoY), EBITDA incl. other income of about INR48 crores, and PAT of INR28 crores, giving record EBITDA and PAT margins of 31% and 18%. Consolidated revenue was INR251 crores (+88% YoY) and consolidated EBITDA excluding other income was INR54 crores (+31%). 540900|2026-03.headline: Newgen FY26 revenue rose 6% to INR1,574 crore and Q4 rose 5.3% to INR457 crore, while management declined to guide FY27 growth.
540900|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 6% Y-o-Y to INR1,574 crore, with subscription revenue up 24% to INR525 crore and SaaS up 36%. Q4 revenue was INR457 crore against INR430 crore in Q4 FY25, with Q4 SaaS up 44%. Profit after tax was INR301 crore reported, or INR334 crore excluding a one-time Labour Code impact and a INR42 crore legal provision; management described the adjusted PAT as up 6% and the adjusted net margin as 21.3%. Large-deal closures slowed in India, Middle East and EMEA on geopolitical uncertainty and decision delays, and management withheld a FY27 growth number, asking for one more quarter of visibility.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 17% Y-o-Y; Q4 U.S. revenue was INR106 crore, up 20% Y-o-Y, driven by insurance journey-led deals and ECM-led banking wins.

segments.name: APAC
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 14% Y-o-Y; management cited strong momentum and newly opened markets in Australia and the U.K., where most deals are subscription.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue growth muted; license revenue fell more than 20-30% Y-o-Y on lower large-deal wins, while other revenue streams grew. Management said the worst is over.

segments.name: EMEA
segments.commentary: Large-deal closures slowed on West Asia geopolitical uncertainty, especially late in FY26; collections slowed, pushing up trade receivables and DSO.

segments.name: Annuity mix (FY26)

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 growth band and should double-digit growth be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not give a number and asked for one more quarter; the company expects growth to compound from a smaller license base and from subscription revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did deferred revenue rise from about INR220 crore to about INR300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to subscription and ATS renewals, plus growth in Australia, the U.K. and U.S., not to a spike in license sales.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue is at risk from client AI-driven budget pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the two most exposed streams, about 40% of revenue, could see a 2-3% impact this year.

EBITDA adjusted for other income was INR56 crore (15.7% margin) and PAT was INR63 crore (17.6% net margin), with management reiterating expected full-year margin expansion. Leadership changed: Tarun Nandwani becomes CEO from 1 August 2026, and a Chief Growth Officer role was created.

540900|2026-09.headline: Newgen Q2 FY27 revenue rose 5.4% to INR422 crore, with H1 up 8.8% to INR779 crore; license revenue fell 19.2% YoY against a high base.
540900|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 5.4% YoY to INR422 crore and H1 grew 8.8% to INR779 crore, led by EMEA (+19.4%) and US (+17.1%), while India (-12.6%) and APAC (-6.4%) declined. EBITDA rose 6.5% to INR109 crore with a 25.8% margin, and PAT rose 6.3% to INR87 crore (20.6% margin). Subscription revenue overtook license revenue during the quarter, and management attributed the license decline to deal closure timing rather than weaker demand. Management reiterated double-digit FY27 growth, which implies a stronger H2 than H1's roughly 8%.

540902|2026-03.headline: Amber FY26 consolidated revenue rose 22% to INR12,186 crore, but management flags 50-100 bps consolidated margin pressure in FY27 from commodity and wage costs.
540902|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue grew 22% to INR12,186 crore and operating EBITDA grew 22% to INR970 crore, with adjusted PAT of INR338 crore (up 22%). Q4 revenue rose 10% to INR4,148 crore, operating EBITDA rose 15% to INR362 crore, and adjusted PAT rose 27% to INR162 crore. Management guided to a temporary 50-100 bps consolidated margin squeeze in FY27 from copper clad laminate and gold costs, currency depreciation and minimum wage hikes. Electronics is guided to about 40% growth in FY27 at 9.5-10% margin after a job-work conversion, and Railways to 30-35% growth at 16-17% margin.

Management guides FY27 growth in line with the industry at about 12-13%, with percentage margin diluted by price hikes but per-unit margin intact. Non-RAC is about 32% of consolidated revenue.

segments.name: Electronics
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR3,268 crore (+49%) and EBITDA INR287 crore (+89%), about 8.8% margin. PCBA is about INR2,281 crore at roughly 5% margin; PCB is about INR600 crore at 12-13% margin. FY27 guided to about 40% growth at 9.5-10% margin after two customers moved from purchase to job-work agreements.

segments.name: Railway Systems and Defense
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR535 crore (+19%) and EBITDA INR90 crore (+8%). Order book above INR2,600 crore. Sidwal's Faridabad greenfield plant is in trial production with commercial production expected this quarter; FY27 and FY28 growth guided at 30-35% with 16-17% margin.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated margin pressure of 50-100 bps in FY27, described as temporary and expected to normalise as the macro environment improves.
Consumer Durables FY27 growth to track the RAC industry at about 12-13%, after industry growth of about 20% in Q1 FY27.
Electronics FY27 revenue growth of about 40% with 9.5-10% EBITDA margin.
Railways FY27 and FY28 growth of 30-35%, margin 16-17%, subject to no disruption in Indian Railways or Metro offtake.
FY27 gross capex of INR1,800-2,000 crore, of which cash outflow is about INR1,100-1,200 crore after supplier credit terms; FY28 cash outflow about INR1,400-1,500 crore.

capex_capacity: Ascent-K Circuit HDI PCB plant in Noida: construction to start around June 2026, 15-16 months to build, then 3-4 months of trial production; mass production from Q3-Q4 FY28. Backed by over INR4,500 crore of ECMS investment approvals across Ascent-K, Ascent and Shogini.
Ascent Circuits Hosur: construction delayed about one quarter by a pollution consent issue; trial production by Q3 FY27 and commercial production by mid-February 2027.

Subsidies: about 48% of plant and machinery via ECMS and 42% from the UP government on building and plant and machinery, received with a 5-6 year lag. Land received at about a 25% discount; the subsidy flow is expected from FY28.

Sri City RAC capacity augmented. Railway Faridabad greenfield plant in trial production. Yujin factory in Korea completed, awaiting RDSO approval (12-15 months), with INR178 crore couplers order book.
demand_pricing: Industry view: RAC volumes were down about 30% in Q1 and Q2 FY26 and recovered in Q3-Q4, leaving FY26 roughly flat. Industry expected to grow about 20% in Q1 FY27 and 12-13% for FY27.

Price increases of about 14% YoY on finished goods: one in January 2026 from the star-rating change and one in April 2026 for commodity costs. Copper clad laminate prices are up more than 60% in one year and still rising; gold is up about 60%.
PCB pricing: Tier 1 EMS pass-through works on a quarterly lag, but PCB (Tier 2) has about a two-quarter lag. Two price increases of about 15% and 18% have been received, with more under negotiation.
Compressor import relief: government allowed imports of about 30% of last year's volumes for compressors below 2 tonne, extended for a year. Management says there is no compressor shortage.
Electronics margin pressure: PCBA about 5% and PCB about 12-13% versus a normal 16-17%. Management expects the price increases to flow through over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What are the RAC industry growth expectations for Q1 and FY27, and which segments face margin pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry expected to grow about 20% in Q1 FY27 and 12-13% for the full year. Margin pressure comes from minimum wage hikes (35% in Haryana, about 22% in UP), CCL and gold costs, and currency depreciation. Indian Railway fixed-price contracts cannot pass costs through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10-12% price increase reasonable?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases are about 14% YoY, from a January star-rating change and an April commodity-driven hike.

qa_highlights.question: Will compressor shortages hurt FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says there is no shortage. Five new domestic manufacturers have come up, and imports of 30% of last year's volumes are allowed. Commercial AC compressors are still largely imported.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Consumer Durables finished-goods share rise, and is it realisation-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Finished goods rose because gas-charging customers moved to ODM solutions, not because of realisation. Finished goods fell from about 80% at listing in FY18 to about 40% now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PCB versus PCBA mix and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 Electronics: PCBA about INR2,281 crore at about 5% margin; PCB about INR600 crore at 12-13%; Power-One about 15% margin; Unitronics not disclosed as it is listed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and net cash outflow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 gross capex INR1,800-2,000 crore with cash outflow of about INR1,100-1,200 crore. FY28 cash outflow of about INR1,400-1,500 crore.

540902|2026-06.headline: Amber Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to INR3,888 crore and operating EBITDA 28% to INR337 crore, with Electronics EBITDA more than doubling.
540902|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to INR3,888 crore and operating EBITDA grew 28% to INR337 crore, with adjusted PAT of INR126 crore (up 19%) before a INR123 crore exceptional loss. Electronics was the standout, with revenue up 29% and EBITDA more than doubling to a 10.8% margin. Railway & Defense EBITDA fell 26% on mix, copper, currency and Haryana minimum wage hikes. Management flagged that PCB margins were compressed by a roughly two-quarter pass-through lag and that cost pressure persists through H1, while Q1 benefited from pre-stocking of compressors and copper. The IL JIN facility incident was a new overhang, with insurance cover and the impact still being assessed.

segments.name: Consumer Durable
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,758 crore (+8%) and EBITDA INR214 crore (+12%) despite commodity and minimum wage headwinds; management attributed the modest growth to a high base. RAC is roughly 55-60% of the division, with the remainder non-RAC.

segments.name: Electronics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR985 crore (+29%) and EBITDA INR107 crore (10.8% margin, up from about 6.4%). Bare PCB margin compressed on copper clad laminate (CCL) costs, and the EMS segment grew more slowly as customers destocked and shifted to job work. Management reiterated FY27 growth of about 40%.

segments.name: Railway Sub-systems & Defense
segments.commentary: Revenue INR144 crore (+18%) but EBITDA fell 26% to INR16 crore on product mix, including first trains supplied through a principal, plus copper, currency and a 35% Haryana minimum wage hike. FY27 revenue growth guided at 30-35% and EBITDA margin at 15-16%.

guidance_outlook: Electronics: FY27 growth of about 40% reiterated; EMS full-year guidance intact per Sanjay Arora.
Railway Sub-systems & Defense: FY27 revenue growth 30-35% and EBITDA margin 15-16%.
Consumer Durable: growth in line with RAC industry, cited as 13-15%; no percentage margin guidance given.
Group margin: earlier 50-100 bps decline guidance for FY27 now moderated, with margins seen normalising if no further currency or commodity disruption.
PCB margin: currently about 12% versus about 16% normal; expected to recover from Q3 FY27 to a 15-16% normalised range, subject to no further CCL price rises.

Oppo mobile: trial production in Q4 FY27, commercial production from Q1 FY28, about 8 million units in year one, rising to 15-16 million in year two; revenue-recognition model to be clarified in 15-20 days.
IL JIN: fundraise enabling resolution up to INR5,000 crore; quantum and form not yet decided. IL JIN production impact being assessed, with guidance expected to be met.
capex_capacity: PCB capex: about INR3,200 crore at Jewar (UP), where construction has started and trial production is about 18 months away; Hosur (Tamil Nadu) about INR1,000 crore, with the plant to be running this financial year; Shogini (Pune) INR500 crore. All three were approved under the ECMS scheme.
Jewar HDI PCB groundbreaking held with Ascent-K / Korea Circuit; air conditioner plant construction planned to start in 2028, with trial production in 2029.
Sidwal greenfield facility in Faridabad (HVAC, pantry, doors, gangways) is now operational.
Asset turn in PCB business about 0.8:1 depending on complexity.
CCL backward integration: Amber in discussion with JV partners; target own CCL plants by 2029-30.
demand_pricing: Consumer Durable: BEE tonnage labelling mandatory from 1 July 2026 has created mixed inventory in the trade; management expects inventory to clear by Diwali, a strong summer from November, and not very high festive demand.
Q1 Consumer Durable margins were helped by pre-buying of compressors and copper ahead of QCO enforcement, and by a premium mix (5-star and 2-tonne). Management said this would not be annualised.
PCB: pass-through to customers is progressing, with some customers raising prices in July. Copper clad laminate prices keep rising, driven by AI and data-centre demand and a shortage.
Electronics TAM: management cited $185 billion of electronics consumption, a $16-17 billion addressable market for PCB, PCBA and power electronics today, and an estimated $35-40 billion by FY30.
Power electronics (PLC, HMI, solar inverters, UPS, BESS) expected to grow 35-40%.

540935|2026-06.headline: Galaxy Surfactants Q1 FY27 EBITDA hit a record INR 252.5 crore (INR 35,458/MT), nearly double YoY; FY27 EBITDA/MT guidance raised to INR 24,000–25,000.
540935|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose to INR 252.5 crore from INR 135.1 crore in Q1 FY26, with EBITDA per metric ton at INR 35,458 versus about INR 20,009 a year earlier. Consolidated volumes grew 5% YoY, with India up 11% and Rest of World up 6%, while AMET volumes fell 4% YoY but rose 19% QoQ after West Asia logistics disruptions cut April–May supply. Management attributed the margin jump to reformulation-led volume recovery, a richer specialty mix, commercial execution and feedstock volatility, and said some of these gains may not persist. FY27 volume guidance of 6–8% was maintained, while EBITDA/MT guidance was raised to INR 24,000–25,000 from INR 19,000–21,000; management implied roughly INR 21,000–22,000 per MT for the remaining three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is standalone peak revenue INR 400-500 crores?

qa_highlights.question: What drives Innoxel's FY27 margin expansion, and how much is CDMO?

541153|2026-03.headline: Bandhan Bank Q4FY26 PAT rose 68% YoY to INR 534 crore, with NIM up to 6.2% and credit cost easing to 2%.
541153|2026-03.overview: Bandhan Bank reported Q4FY26 PAT of INR 534 crore, up 68% YoY and 159% QoQ, with ROA of 1.1% and ROE of 9% for the quarter. NIM rose to 6.2% from 5.9% in Q3 on a 23 bps QoQ fall in deposit costs, while credit cost fell to 2% from 3.3%. Slippages declined to INR 1,028 crore from INR 1,314 crore, led by EEB, and collection efficiency improved. Full-year FY26 PAT was INR 1,224 crore, with NII down 5.8% YoY, and opex was elevated in Q4 by PSLC and IT items.

financial_highlights.change: from 31% last year; bulk deposits -7% YoY

segments.name: EEB (microfinance and related)
segments.commentary: EEB book INR 53,906 crore, down YoY (about -5%) but up 8% QoQ; 23% of advances. EEB slippages fell to INR 690 crore from INR 942 crore; 0-90 DPD pool fell to about 3.1% from 4.6%.

segments.name: Non-EEB book
segments.commentary: Non-EEB advances grew 25% YoY and form about two-thirds of total advances. Retail grew 46% YoY (CV, CE, auto, gold loans); wholesale grew 33% YoY.

segments.name: Secured book
segments.commentary: Secured book grew 25% YoY and forms about 56% of advances, against a target of 58% by March 2027.

segments.name: Fee income
segments.commentary: Other income grew 10% YoY and 12% QoQ; third-party distribution income rose 34% YoY and processing fees rebounded.

guidance_outlook: ROA guided at 1.6%-1.7% (management also cited 1.6%-1.8%, give or take 10 bps) by exit FY27 (Q4FY27); management says it will work towards this, calling it a challenge.
NIM guided at around 6% on total assets (about 6.5% on earning assets) by exit FY27; a further 10-20 bps improvement expected over the next 2-3 quarters from term deposit repricing.
Credit cost guided at 1.6%-1.7% by Q4FY27 from 2% in Q4FY26; FY26 credit cost was 3%.
Advances growth targeted at around 14%-15%; deposit growth to be better than advances, but industry credit growth now exceeds deposit growth.
PSL certificate cost expected to fall about 50% in FY27 versus FY26 and to be nearly neutralised in FY28.
Opex-to-average-assets remains a focus; FY26 was about 4% against guidance. Other income to add about 10 bps to ROA.

Expected ECL transition impact about INR 1,250 crore (based on December 2025 portfolio), spread over 5 years at about INR 250 crore a year, or roughly 16-17 bps CRAR impact each year; flow impact still being computed under the latest circular.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 1,955 branches; housing finance centres largely upgraded to full banking branches, some merged with existing branches.
4,400 EEB banking units across the country.
Average LCR in Q4 ranged 130%-140%; period-end LCR about 131%, down from about 200% a year earlier as bulk deposits fell.
Capital adequacy 18.0% CRAR and 17.3% Tier 1; management says ample headroom for growth.

Collection efficiency ex-bucket 99.6% for Q4 (99.3% in Q3) and 99.7% for March; management says no adverse effect on collections from elections or the Middle East war so far in April, though a few basis points dipped.
Deposit competition is intense; competitor deposit rates rose sharply in March 2026, and bank chose not to grow bulk deposits in Q4.
Yield on advances rose 14 bps QoQ, helped by the Q3 ARC sale removing NPAs from the base and the EEB mix shift.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NII grow only 4% QoQ despite strong advance growth and margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the back-ended loan growth (about 50% of incremental FY growth came in Q4, with late-March disbursals not yet earning), two fewer days in the quarter, and the 25 bps December repo cut impacting about 46% of the book (11 bps effect).

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state credit cost after the RBI ECL norms, and what are the standard asset provisions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management holds about INR 1,072 crore of standard asset provisions, including an extra 75 bps on standard assets: EEB at 1% vs 0.25% required, and personal loans/ABG at about 0.4%. Flow impact is still being computed; the INR 1,250 crore transition estimate is based on the December 2025 book.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins keep improving, and what is the NIM trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects another 10-20 bps of NIM improvement over the next 2-3 quarters as term deposits reprice, with a best-effort aim of about 6% NIM on total assets by exit FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the PSL shortfall and how will it be fixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 PSLC cost was about INR 150 crore (INR 60 crore higher QoQ). The aim is a roughly 50% cut in FY27 and near zero in FY28, with EEB loans qualifying for PSL rising from about 10-15% to about 40%, targeting 60-65%.

qa_highlights.question: What were the one-off items in opex?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 120 crore in recurring-type items: PSLC cost up around INR 60 crore QoQ and IT expenses up around INR 50 crore, with timing-related elements expected not to repeat immediately. Separately, INR 73 crore extra employee cost came from keeping branches open on holidays.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a government deposit share and how much is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Government deposits are about INR 6,000 crore; about 12% of CASA is from government deposits. Retail composition, including CASA and retail term deposits, rose to 74% from 69% a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROA path and what would drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA rose from 0.2% in September to 0.4% in December and 1.1% in Q4. Drivers cited are lower credit cost, higher NIM, higher other income (about 10 bps expected), and lower PSLC costs; management acknowledged a 50-60 bps journey to the target.

Management stated no NPA sale is currently planned, but an ARC-sale option remains open.
Media reports of promoter-level activity; management called them rumours and said there is no impact on the Bank's shareholding.

541153|2026-06.headline: Bandhan Bank cut its FY27 exit ROA aspiration to 1.2%-1.4% from 1.6%-1.8%, citing funding costs and tech costs; Q1 PAT rose 35% YoY to INR 502 crores.
541153|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 showed better seasonal resilience than prior first quarters: gross advances grew 16% YoY to INR 1.56 lakh crores, with non-EEB up 27% and secured book at 57% of advances. Margin held at 6.2%, PAT was INR 502 crores (+35% YoY), and gross NPA eased to 3.1%. Management lowered its Q4 FY27 exit ROA guidance to 1.2%-1.4% from 1.6%-1.8%, attributing the cut to external factors (funding costs, technology costs, Middle East energy crisis, monsoon), and said the medium-term aspiration could slip beyond its original timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the ROA aspiration cut, and is it due to asset quality or funding costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cut is due to external factors: NIM stretch of about 30 bps (funding costs, no further margin uplift to 6.5%) and about 10 bps opex (tech costs ~4.3% of assets vs 4.2% guided). Credit cost is improving (2.0% to 1.8%).

qa_highlights.question: Why hasn't FCNR and easing liquidity relieved funding costs?

qa_highlights.question: Why is the bank growing low-margin wholesale banking?

rows.why: Management declined to commit to sustaining Q1's 40% growth through the year and guided Q2 margins lower, so an upgrade is not signalled; FY27 growth is only guided as higher than FY26 with no numeric target.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management explicitly said Q2 FY27 margins will be hit somewhat, with LPG furnaces affected in Q1 and possibly Q2 and raw-material prices (nickel, molybdenum, tungsten, cobalt) rising sharply, and fixed-price defence contracts leave the company exposed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Bulletproof jacket (ABHED) testing expected to complete this quarter with certificates next quarter, isothermal forging for super alloys and four super alloy plus three titanium grade orders to execute this year, and S400 testing revenue is conservatively about 10% of export base with clarity in a couple of quarters.

rows.label: Export base expansion to ~10% of turnover
rows.why: Current-year export sales are Rs 33 crore with open export order book of about Rs 25 crore against a target of about 10% of turnover (Rs 100-120 crore), and management expects at least 15-20% increase on that base over 3-4 years.

rows.label: Titanium and super alloy orders
rows.why: Titanium orders worth about Rs 600 crore are cited after the new melting facility melted about 750 tonnes last year, with orders for four super alloy grades and three titanium grades to be executed this year, and management says these carry higher margins than special steel.

rows.label: Metal bank for one customer
rows.when: Q2 FY27 clarity, implementation next quarter
rows.why: Procurement is under way for one customer with further clarity expected by end of Q2 FY27, but the benefits are customer-owned and off balance sheet, so implementation and utilisation are still unconfirmed.

tone.note: Management was confident on the medium-term margin recovery, titanium/super alloy orders and certifications, but cautious and evasive on Q2 margins, the Rs 1,000 crore capex timeline and S400 revenue; analysts pushed on margins and capex returns.

541233|2026-03.headline: FY26 was Lemon Tree's best year: revenue Rs 1,452.7 crore (+13%), PAT Rs 288.3 crore (+19%), with margin down 126 bps to 48.1%.
541233|2026-03.overview: Lemon Tree reported record FY26 and Q4 FY26 on occupancy, ARR, revenue, EBITDA, PBT, PAT and cash profit, with Q4 revenue of Rs 419.5 crore (+11%) and PAT of Rs 116.5 crore (+8%). Net EBITDA margin fell to 48.1% for FY26 and 52% for Q4, which management attributes to renovation spend, technology investment and the GST change. Management guided that these three cost heads fall to about 3.7% of revenue by FY28, and set out a proposed demerger that would leave Lemon Tree as an asset-light entity and Fleur Hotels as an owner/lessor platform. Q4 demand softened in March and April from the Middle East conflict and airline disruption, with corporate travel weaker and occupancy hitting what management called a ceiling.

financial_highlights.change: Highest ever for a full financial year
from Rs 1,699 crore a year ago

segments.name: Lemon Tree (asset-light, managed and franchised)
segments.commentary: Opened 20 managed/franchised hotels (1,523 rooms) and signed 55 (4,912 rooms) in FY26; total pipeline 22,581 rooms across 268 hotels, of which 131 hotels and 11,811 rooms are operational. Keys RevPAR grew 20% and Aurika 19% for FY25 to FY26 on management's figures.

segments.name: Fleur Hotels (owned/leased)
segments.commentary: Post-scheme, Fleur to have 5,600 rooms across 39 operational hotels; 4 hotels with 875 rooms in confirmed pipeline, including 572 rooms at Nehru Place (estimated capex Rs 700 crore). Fees Rs 95.8 crore, +8% on a same-store basis.

segments.name: Aurika brand
segments.commentary: Highest ARR and margin product; Aurika occupancy rose from 62% to 74% for FY26 with RevPAR +19%, though Q4 occupancy fell 2% as a large Mumbai wet-lease ended. Aurika has only two hotels (Mumbai and Udaipur).

guidance_outlook: Cost heads (GST impact, technology, renovation) expected to fall from 5.8% of revenue in FY26 to about 4.8% in FY27 and 3.7% in FY28 onward, adding roughly 1% of revenue a year, plus Rs 25-30 crore of one-off costs (Delhi property tax ex gratia, labour code) that drop out from FY27.
FY27 renovation spend about 1.9% of revenue, normal renovation thereafter at about 1.3% (possibly 1.0-1.2%); GST impact rising from 1% to 2% of revenue in FY27 as it becomes a full year.
Expected openings of about 2,000 rooms in FY27, rising to about 3,000 in FY28 and 4,000 in FY29; management says openings lag signings by about three years, with signings of about 5,000 rooms a year.

Lemon Tree standalone post-demerger: steady-state flow-through on management fees of 75-80%, currently about 60% pro forma; steady-state PAT about 60% of revenue (per management, after tax and no interest or depreciation).

Fleur targets up to Rs 3,000 crore of deployable capital over 12-18 months (including Warburg primary investment), and plans to add about 2,500 rooms; management does not give fee guidance for FY27-28.
Demerger: CCI approval received in April; SEBI and shareholder/creditor approvals underway; NCLT timing 6-18 months, with management giving 12-18 months as the outer limit.
Debt-to-EBITDA about 2.25x now; consolidated debt may rise to Rs 2,500-3,000 crore if Rs 1,500 crore is deployed, temporarily.
capex_capacity: Renovation: about 5,000 rooms to be renovated, of which 4,000 heavy renovation with about 85% complete; about 400-500 rooms under renovation in Q4 and similar in Q1.
Keys Whitefield renovation expected to complete in about 4 months; Keys Hosur Road under renovation; Keys Pimpri, Pune completed.
Aurika Naldehra, Shimla: 2 of 3 blocks to open by Q2 FY27 for the summer season.
Aurika Varanasi: 47-room heritage licence signed January 2026 on the ghat by the Ganges.

Nehru Place (572 rooms, North India's largest hotel) awaiting final approval before construction; estimated Rs 700 crore; Andaz (525 rooms) nearby, with cash flow over 3.5 years, 60% in the last 18 months.
Acquisition valuations cited at 8x-16x EBITDA; greenfield build 3-4 years, renovation-led acquisitions 1-2 years, operating assets immediate.
demand_pricing: Mid-March decision to prioritise occupancy over rate; April-May tactical pricing to keep an occupancy premium, with ARR roughly flat YoY; Q4 occupancy reached what management called a ceiling.

Corporate travel slowed in March as companies cut travel due to fares and the war; corporate share of occupancy fell to 55% from 59% in Q4 (negotiated room nights 55.4% for the full year vs 56.1%). Retail filled the gap at lower rates.
Indigo shutdown in December and the Middle East war (from early March, continuing into April) cited as headwinds; May described as surprisingly good.
Mumbai micro-market saw about 2,000 keys added in the last year (from Accor Fairmont to Ginger), creating a temporary supply glut for Aurika Mumbai.
Target: 65% of business from retail (direct, B2C, loyalty) once the portfolio reaches 20,000-25,000 operating rooms.
Loyalty programme has about 24 lakh members, driving about 25% of room nights per management.
Indian mid-market: management says demand outpaces supply; cites 2.5 million unbranded rooms in India as a conversion opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Would Fleur's inventory be managed by a non-Lemon Tree operator post-demerger, and how would that work?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Fleur is brand-agnostic and would choose whichever brand makes economic sense, while Lemon Tree should not be discriminated against; it cited a lost 5-star NCLT bid as an example.

qa_highlights.question: Why Aurika RevPAR growth (3%) lags Keys (16%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to micro-market differences and timing; full-year FY26 RevPAR growth was 19% for Aurika and 20% for Keys, with Keys set to keep growing as renovations finish.

qa_highlights.question: How confident are you on conversion of signings into openings, and what fee numbers for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Openings lag signings by about three years; management declined to give fee guidance but expects about 2,000 rooms opened in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-saving path and steady-state margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Renovation, GST and technology costs to fall to about 3.7% of revenue by FY28; pro forma Lemon Tree flow-through is about 60% now, targeted at 70%+ and then 75-80%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised demerger timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: CCI approval came in April; SEBI/shareholder/creditor steps underway; NCLT is the main variable, with 12-18 months the outer limit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did incentive-linked management fees lag for third-party hotels versus Fleur?
qa_highlights.answer: Incentive fees (1-5% of revenue depending on GOP slab) fell as renovation and GST cut owned-hotel EBITDA margins; third-party fees rose 23% from net additions, Fleur fees rose 8% on a same-store basis.

qa_highlights.question: What peak debt level is comfortable after Fleur's deployment?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-to-EBITDA about 2.25x now; consolidated debt could rise to Rs 2,500-3,000 crore temporarily if Rs 1,500 crore is deployed.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation for standalone Lemon Tree post-demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Lemon Tree to be debt-free and cash-generative; Board to decide a dividend or buyback policy; no F&B expansion planned, with a high hurdle for acquisitions.

risks_watch: NCLT timing for the Fleur demerger: management guides 6-18 months, with 12-18 months as the outer limit; CCI approval received in April, SEBI, shareholder and creditor steps still pending.

Demand softness: corporate share of occupancy fell to 55% in Q4 from 59%; March and April were weak on the Middle East conflict and airline disruption, though management said May was surprisingly good.

Margin recovery depends on renovation spend falling to about 1.9% of revenue in FY27 and GST impact and technology costs easing; standalone flow-through is about 60% pro forma versus a 70%+ steady-state target.
Openings execution: about 2,000 rooms targeted in FY27 versus 1,523 rooms opened in FY26; openings lag signings by about three years and owner-finance delays could cause slippage.

Leverage post-deployment: consolidated debt could rise to Rs 2,500-3,000 crore from about Rs 1,500 crore if Rs 1,500 crore is deployed, versus debt-to-EBITDA of about 2.25x now; Fleur's 2,500-room pipeline is not yet firm.
Aurika weakness: Q4 occupancy fell 2% after a large Mumbai wet-lease ended and Mumbai micro-market supply rose by about 2,000 keys; Keys RevPAR growth depends on completing renovations.
key_quotes: FY26 was the best year in Lemon Tree's history across Occupancy, ARR, Revenue, EBITDA, PBT, PAT, Cash Profit and Q4 FY26 was the best ever fourth quarter on the same parameters.
I want to take this opportunity to continue the conversation on the demerger scheme.
I do not want to give guidance, but I can give you a direction.
Corporate travel is the first that kind of dries up when war happens because it is under the control normally of the CEO or an equivalent CXO and it is a one -person decision.
Lemon Tree will not need any significant capital other than potentially investments in technology or in marketing and so on.

Tone on the Q4 softness was defensive, attributing weakness to Indigo, the war and Mumbai supply.
